instruction:
The Vellmar Delta Geodetic Office published adjusted benchmark heights and subsidence rates for the VDL-26 double-run levelling campaign from a saved adjustment run pack. The published figures in `/app/data/adjusted_heights_published.csv` and `/app/data/subsidence_published.json` are wrong in ways that reach the setup reductions, the section values, the network adjustment, the control, the loop closures and the rate classes. Everything needed to redo the campaign from the field book shards is under `/app/data`: the handbook `/app/data/levelling_handbook.md` holds the rules and the order of authority, `/app/data/feed_layouts.md` describes the shard layouts, and `/app/data/output_contract.md` fixes the columns, keys, vocabularies, decimals and order of every report. Working out which of the other files can be trusted, and for what, is part of the job.

The finished work is one program, `/app/out/run_levelnet.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/run_levelnet.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`. It reads a campaign laid out like `/app/data` from whatever directory it is given, leaves that directory untouched, and writes into OUT_DIR the twenty-one reports named below plus `/app/out/manifest.json` and nothing else. If OUT_DIR does not exist yet, the program creates it. After your last edit you run it once with `/app/data` as input and `/app/out` as output, so the files left in `/app/out` are its own output. It is run again later on fresh campaigns placed elsewhere, with other seeds, networks, site clocks, memo tables, profile settings, workbook date systems, rod pairs, journals, rulings and file names, and with memo, workbook and YAML files written by other tools, so every figure has to come out of the input at run time and nothing may be carried over from the shipped files. Each run has to finish within two minutes. Arithmetic, comparisons and rounding follow the handbook exactly. A report is accepted only when it matches the contract exactly, and every other report rests on the eight core reports (setup ledger, run summaries, section pairs, adjustment iterations, adjusted heights, residuals, network summary and subsidence rates), which have to be exact on the shipped campaign and on every fresh campaign.

The reports are every reduced setup in `/app/out/setup_ledger.csv`; every run with its status in `/app/out/run_summaries.tsv`; every section with its selected run pair in `/app/out/section_pairs.psv`; every resolved benchmark token in `/app/out/benchmark_resolution.csv`; the control points in `/app/out/control_points.json`; every adjustment round of every network component in `/app/out/adjustment_iterations.jsonl`; the adjusted heights in `/app/out/adjusted_heights.csv`, with the residuals in `/app/out/residuals.tsv` and the component statistics in `/app/out/network_summary.json`; the loop misclosures in `/app/out/loop_closures.xml`; the rates in `/app/out/subsidence_rates.csv`; every excluded setup, run and section in `/app/out/excluded_records.jsonl`; the settlement counters in `/app/out/dedup_report.json` and the per-shard counts in `/app/out/source_lineage.json`; the rod certificates used in `/app/out/rod_certificates_used.tsv`; the governing settings applied in `/app/out/parameters_used.yaml`; the comparisons with the published heights in `/app/out/variance_vs_published.csv`, with the published rates in `/app/out/rate_vs_published.psv`, with the network dashboard in `/app/out/dashboard_disagreements.csv` and with the control height cache in `/app/out/cache_divergence.jsonl`; and the summary in `/app/out/reconciliation.md`. The manifest lists the other reports in contract order with their sizes and SHA-256 digests.

Use only the Python standard library and install nothing. Do not modify, add or delete anything under `/app/data`. When you finish, `/app/out` holds only the program and the twenty-two files named above; keep scratch work elsewhere.

Your final message lists the defects of the published run, each with the handbook rule or memo table that overrides it, and names the memo tables, workbook sheets and shard files you set aside.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

instruction:
# Campaign dose ration settlement

The animal health service has handed you the export folder `/app/data` for a fortnightly dose
campaign across four veterinary regions and two holder segments. Doses are scarce, so every
round rations what the depots hold. The folder carries the campaign contract, the rule
documents it names, configuration registers, the primary export streams, reference tables, a
correction stream, two settlement observation logs and one retired runbook. The contract tier
is the single source of truth for every quantity, and `corpus_index.md` names the tier of each
file. Read `source_manifest.md` and `corpus_index.md` before anything else. The retired runbook
governs nothing. Nothing in the folder tells you which records disagree with each other;
finding that out is the work.

Build a settlement program at `/app/out/derive_report.py`. It accepts `--data` with a corpus
folder and `--out` with an output folder, and it writes nine documents:
`/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json`,
`/app/out/region_East.json`, `/app/out/segment_commercial.json`,
`/app/out/segment_public.json`, `/app/out/summary.json`, `/app/out/policy_audit.json` and
`/app/out/data_quality.json`. Run it over `/app/data` into `/app/out` so those nine documents
sit beside it when you finish. The same program will be run over campaign extracts nobody has
seen, with other round counts, other block counts, other clock offsets and other settlement
evidence, so every rule it applies has to come from the corpus it is given. Use only the Python
standard library, run no external commands from the program, and keep the program offline.

`output_contract.md` fixes every document name, every key, every enumerated value and every
ordering, and it binds to the letter. Every quantity is an exact whole number of doses. A
document counts only when every quantity in it is exact; a close total earns nothing. Block
identities carry their restock epoch in the form `BLK-0042#2` and lot identities carry their
production year in the form `LOT-1182@2033`. Each settled claim carries exactly one outcome and
one reason from the registers in `reason_codes.json`, chosen by the precedence those registers
declare. Rejected requisitions carry exactly one reject code. Nobody recorded how many records
disagree with each other, so there is no count to check yourself against.

Work the campaign in one pass over the rounds in calendar order. Admission precedes identity,
identity precedes the governing head count, the governing head count precedes the entitlement,
the entitlement precedes the claimable quantity, the claimable quantity precedes the award, and
the award precedes the carried claim of the next round. Two rules the registers leave unstated
are settled by the observation logs, and `policy_audit.json` reports each settled reading in the
key the output contract names for it. Where two rules could both apply to one record, the
precedence stated in `campaign_contract.md` decides which one does, and applying a rule to
records it does not reach costs exactly as much as failing to apply it where it does. Leave
`/app/data` untouched, write nothing else into `/app/out`, and make a second run over the same
corpus produce the same nine documents. The program reads only the folder passed to `--data`,
and it works whatever that folder is called.

Finish with a message that states these quantities. How many settled claims took their
governing head count from the field intake and how many from the dispatch stream. How many
settled claims took it from the registry, and how many distinct blocks took it from the registry
at least once. How many of the governing tokens in the governance observation log name each
of the three sources. How many entries of the clearance observation log record a carried claim
that was cleared and how many record one left standing. How many lots entered a
regional pool and how many stayed outside every pool. How many pooled lots took their dose
content from a laboratory assay and how many took it from the reference table. The pooled dose
content before the substitution derate, the content after it and the doses the derate costs.
Which round the claims of the round the calendar removed settled in, and how many claims arrived
that way. How many requisitions were refused because the effective reading fell at the closing
instant of a claim window, and how many because it fell before the opening instant. How many
claims took exactly one dose from the remainder step of the ladder, and in how many cells that
step ran. State every figure as an exact whole number, and say plainly which observation
evidence settled each of the two unstated rules and what in that evidence settled it.

You have 10800 seconds to complete this task. Solve it from the corpus in front of you without
searching online for solutions or task specific hints.

instruction:
Our sign-in gateway lost the tool that replays its attempt journal into a lockout table, and the source went with it. Until it is back, nobody can tell which accounts are locked or for how long. Everything left of it is in `/app/data`. `conventions.md` holds the rules the team wrote down, `reports.md` gives the exact shape of the three output files, and `handover.md` holds notes the last operator wrote from memory. The team does not trust `handover.md`; where it disagrees with `conventions.md` or the worked examples, it is wrong. Read all three notes before you start writing code.

Two worked examples ship with their answers. Their input files carry the prefix `example_a_` or `example_b_`, and the files they should produce carry `example_a_out_` or `example_b_out_`. The five input files with no prefix (`attempts.jsonl`, `policy.json`, `overrides.csv`, `locks.prev.json`, `manifest.json`) are the live intake, and nobody has its answers.

`conventions.md` says that six rules of the old tool were never written down. Working out those six rules from the worked examples is part of the task. They cover whether a user is still locked at the second its lock ends, whether a failure exactly one window old still counts, which of several `overrides.csv` rows for one user stands, what a correct password from a locked user gets, how long a repeat lock lasts, and the order of records that share one second.

Both worked examples use mode word zero. The live intake's `manifest.json` carries mode word 254, and every other intake the program will later meet carries either mode word zero or mode word 254. `conventions.md` says which seven bit values are in use and that what each bit does was never written down; working out what the program must do when mode word 254 is set is part of the task as well. The live intake has no answers, but its manifest carries a SHA-256 for each report and for each of the two tables in `locks.json`, and those digests are the evidence for the bits.

Write the replay tool as one Python program at `/app/out/lockout.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/lockout.py IN_DIR OUT_DIR`. It reads the five input files with no prefix from `IN_DIR`, takes the mode word from that folder's `manifest.json`, and writes `locks.json`, `decisions.jsonl` and `summary.json` into `OUT_DIR`, byte for byte in the form `reports.md` gives and replacing any copies already there. It exits with status 0 when it has written them. `decisions.jsonl` must exist even when it is empty, and the `table_digest` in `summary.json` must agree with the `locks.json` written in the same run. A run over a journal of a thousand lines should finish in well under a minute. Write it as named functions, and leave no bare `except` and no debug print in the file.

The same program will later be run on other folders with this layout, with different policies, users, sources, overrides, previous tables and damaged lines, so nothing about the shipped folder may be written into the program, including user names, source addresses or the table digest in code or comments. The program must use only the Python 3.12 standard library, must work with no network access, must leave `IN_DIR` unchanged, and must produce identical output when run twice on the same input. Leave everything under `/app/data` as it is.

Run your finished program over `/app/data` into an output directory of your own outside `/app/data`, and then end with a closing report that gives, for the live intake: `events`, `allows`, `fails`, `locks`, `denies`, `ignored`, `retransmitted`, `active`, `banned` and the full `table_digest`, each as your program wrote it, the user, `until` and `strikes` of every live lock left in `locks.json`, and every banned source with its `until`. For each of the six unwritten rules, state in words the reading your program follows and name the worked example file and journal `seq` that settled it, or say plainly that the examples did not settle it and you made a choice. For each of the seven mode bits, state what your program does when it is set and name the live manifest digests you compared to settle it, or say that the bit stays open. Also say whether your program reproduced both worked examples byte for byte, and whether its live reports and table digests agree with every digest in the live `manifest.json`.

A partial replay tool that is written down and reported on is worth more than a perfect one that never gets finished, so make sure the program is in place and the closing report is written before the time limit, even if some rules or bits are still open.

instruction:
A source archive at `/app/data/tool.zip` holds `sentinel-ctl`, a stdlib-plus-pyarrow policy compiler for a multi-tenant access-control bundle whose compiled security numbers have drifted from the authoritative policy. The binding policy is spread across the many reference files under `/app/data/`: the numeric base tables, the effective-time windows, the tenant multipliers, the version map, the reconstruction, rounding, and unit rules, and a request corpus. Study the tool and the reference material together and work out what is wrong.

Extract the tool to `/app/tool` and repair its `/app/tool/cli.py` so the tool runs on Python 3.12, then use the repaired tool itself to produce the main configuration `/app/out/config.json` rather than hand-writing it or bypassing the tool. Every configuration value must equal the authoritative policy resolved from the reference material, and the tenant and role parameters must be resolved by traversing the dependency chain in the order each file points to the next rather than by reading a value from a file reached out of order.

Each rule that binds a value is stated in the reference file that holds the data it governs, and `output_field_spec.txt` and `report_field_spec.txt` fix the shape of every artifact. The repaired `resolve` subcommand must work, with the options in the tool's README, on any reference corpus with the same file layout and stated value ranges as `/app/data`, and every document it writes must match that corpus's authoritative policy in full. Each `resolve` run must finish within 60 seconds.

Record the resolved authoritative policy in `/app/out/validation_report.json`, including the resolved param key, tenant, effective version, and risk threshold. The report also records the threshold reconciliation iteration sequence and its converged value, and the resolution order of every file consumed and every superseded or legacy branch rejected. It must also record whether every delivered artifact is present and whether the configuration matches the resolved policy. The exact field names for `validation_report.json`, `summary.json`, `profile_dev.json` and `profile_prod.json` are documented in `output_field_spec.txt` under the data directory, so match that field spec exactly. Record the real CLI command transcript, the delivered configuration digest, and the canonical trailer in `/app/out/report.json`. Deliver the repaired tool as a byte-deterministic archive at `/app/out/tool.zip` with the same member layout as `/app/data/tool.zip`. Produce the two environment profiles at `/app/out/profile_dev.json` and `/app/out/profile_prod.json`. Write `/app/out/summary.json` listing every input file present in the reference data, the profiles produced, and the artifacts written. Keep `config.json` and both profiles flat and scalar, keep every artifact deterministic across runs and free of timestamps, uuids, or seeds, and keep every JSON artifact free of network hosts and secrets. In your final response, summarize the completed work and state where each delivered artifact was written.

The clinical pharmacology unit published the VRX-BE-2614 bioequivalence report `/app/data/be_report_published.csv` with its statistics `/app/data/be_statistics_published.json`, both produced by the saved rerun pack `/app/data/nca_rerun_pack.md`, and the report is wrong in ways that reach the concentrations, the sampling times, the populations and the intervals. Everything needed to redo it from the LC-MS/MS injection exports is in `/app/data`. The governance memo, the bioanalytical workbook, the analysis profile and the handbook `/app/data/be_analysis_handbook.md` (revision 5) are the authority over the rerun pack, the published files, caches, dashboards, bulletins, drafts, quick references and legacy sheets; `/app/data/feed_layouts.md` describes the record shapes and `/app/data/output_contract.md` fixes the columns, keys, order and vocabularies of every report. Working out which rules the published run broke and which shipped files can be trusted is part of the job.

The finished work is one program, `/app/out/run_be.py`, which runs as `python3 /app/out/run_be.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, reads a corpus laid out like `/app/data` from whatever directory it is given and writes into `OUT_DIR` the reports named below and nothing else; after its last edit you run it once on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as the output directory, so the files left in `/app/out` are its own output. It is run again later on fresh copies of the corpus placed elsewhere, with other studies, subjects, runs, memo tables, profile settings, site calendars, workbook date systems, alias chains, correction journals and adverse events, so every figure has to come out of the input at run time and nothing may be carried over from the shipped files. Numbers are written and compared under the rounding rules of handbook H21 and H22, which also say when a value sitting on a rounding midpoint may round either way. A report counts only when it matches exactly, and the calibration, run acceptance, study-sample, reported concentration, sampling time, NCA, population and statistics reports count only when all of them are exact on the shipped corpus and on every changed copy at once, so a near miss anywhere earns nothing for the reports built on them.

The reports are the curve of every analysed run in `/app/out/calibration_fits.json`; the back-calculation of every calibration standard in `/app/out/standard_backcalc.tsv`; every QC and dilution QC result in `/app/out/qc_results.csv`; the acceptance decision of every analysed run beside the lab's own status in `/app/out/run_acceptance.csv`; every study-sample result in `/app/out/tube_results.psv`; the reported concentration of every scheduled tube and analyte in `/app/out/reported_concentrations.csv`; the dose instant, draw instant and elapsed time of every scheduled tube in `/app/out/sampling_times.xml`; the incurred sample reanalysis in `/app/out/isr_assessment.json`; the non-compartmental parameters of every profile in `/app/out/nca_parameters.csv` and every terminal-phase candidate fit with the chosen one in `/app/out/lambda_z_selection.jsonl`; the average bioequivalence statistics in `/app/out/be_statistics.json` with the summary table in `/app/out/be_summary.md`; the inclusion decision of every randomized subject, analyte and parameter in `/app/out/analysis_populations.csv`; every subject-level exclusion in `/app/out/excluded_subjects.jsonl`; the mean concentration profiles in `/app/out/mean_profiles.csv`; the revision and void counters in `/app/out/dedup_report.json` and the per-shard counts in `/app/out/source_lineage.json`; the resolution of every observed run, subject and relabelled tube token in `/app/out/alias_resolution.csv`; the governing settings applied, emesis passes included, in `/app/out/parameters_used.yaml`; the profile-by-profile comparison with the published report in `/app/out/variance_vs_published.csv` and the interval comparison in `/app/out/reconciliation.md`; and `/app/out/manifest.json`, listing the other reports in contract order with their sizes and SHA-256 digests.

Use only the Python standard library and install nothing. Do not modify, add or delete anything under `/app/data`, and when you finish `/app/out` should hold only the program and the twenty-two files named above, with scratch work kept elsewhere.

Your final message should list each defect you found in the published run with the rerun-pack step, file or handbook rule that shows it; name the withdrawn, draft and decoy tables, sheets and files you set aside; name the subject that only the first emesis window pass would have excluded; and name a tube whose draw time depends on a reversal entry that cancels another reversal, with the correction entry that stays in effect.

instruction:
The flat exports under `/app/data` are the working set for a network replan cycle. A previous planning run published a dispatch plan and a headline objective that the desks no longer trust. Rebuild the cost coefficients from the registers, re-solve the plan the operating contract defines, and publish the corrected plan with its audit artifacts. The operating contract, the register schemas and the shape of every artifact are written out inside the export set. File names there are operational codes rather than descriptions, so work out what each export governs from the export set itself.

Deliver a reusable optimizer at `/app/out/solver.py` that takes an input directory and an output directory and writes every artifact under the output directory. It will be run on other export sets laid out under the same contract, so its results must follow from the inputs it is given. Each run on one export set must finish within 400 seconds. Use only the Python standard library, no network, and do not start other programs from it. It runs as a single process: no subprocess, fork or multiprocessing pool. Do not import `random`, `uuid` or `secrets` in it, and do not read the clock (`time.time`, `datetime.now` and the like). The program must read only from the input directory and write only inside the output directory. Leave `/app/data` as you found it, and leave the artifacts for the shipped export set under `/app/out`.

```bash
python3 /app/out/solver.py <DATA_DIR> <OUT_DIR>
```

All money is integer United States cents. Each decision must be solved to exact optimality under the contract.

The artifacts are `/app/out/corrected_coefficients.jsonl`, `/app/out/objective.json`, `/app/out/optimal_plan.jsonl`, `/app/out/production_schedule.csv`, `/app/out/holding_profile.csv`, `/app/out/sourcing_allocation.csv`, `/app/out/plant_utilization.csv`, `/app/out/shortfall_ledger.csv`, `/app/out/retrofit_selection.json`, `/app/out/budget_utilization.json`, `/app/out/period_costs.json`, `/app/out/item_summary.json`, `/app/out/binding_constraints.json`, `/app/out/optimality_certificate.json`, `/app/out/sensitivity_report.json`, `/app/out/incumbent_delta.json`, `/app/out/coefficient_corrections.csv`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/rejected_records.csv`, `/app/out/reconciliation.txt` and `/app/out/audit_summary.md`, each written under the output directory with the same name when the optimizer runs elsewhere.

In your final reply, state for the shipped export set the corrected total objective, the total setup cost and the total holding cost of the corrected plan in cents, the number of production lots the plan opens, and the total demand units the plan leaves uncovered.

instruction:
The extract in `/app/data` comes from a household budgeting office for the month 2026-09. The office keeps five client households, one in each of its five districts, closes their envelope ledger at month end and then runs the envelope sweep that rebalances the envelopes of each household. The documents shipped with the data govern this work. Terms that the documents' glossary defines carry their defined meaning wherever they appear in the documents.

Write one program, `/app/out/transform.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/transform.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, that closes the ledger and sweeps the five households of an extract in this layout and writes every report the documents define into OUT_DIR. Run it on the shipped extract with OUT_DIR set to `/app/out`, so that the canonical ledger lands at `/app/out/normalized.jsonl`, the month summary at `/app/out/summary.json`, the input-quality counts at `/app/out/data_quality.json`, the category summary at `/app/out/product_summary.json`, the five household reports at `/app/out/region_central.json`, `/app/out/region_east.json`, `/app/out/region_north.json`, `/app/out/region_south.json` and `/app/out/region_west.json`, and the four segment reports at `/app/out/segment_consumer.json`, `/app/out/segment_corporate.json`, `/app/out/segment_enterprise.json` and `/app/out/segment_smb.json`, beside the other reports the documents define. It will also be run on other extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular month. The program creates OUT_DIR if it does not exist. The program is self-contained and imports nothing from its own folder; only the program and the thirteen reports named above are collected.

Every report follows the layout and form the documents give, exactly: text reports byte for byte, database and workbook reports value for value. The reports must be identical across repeated runs, working directories, extract locations and output directories. When an extract breaks one of the rules of the inputs that `std_ledger.md` lists, the program stops with an error and writes no report. Where `office.ini` and the governing parameter sheet give one household different values, `office.ini` governs the household's round budget and the sheet every other parameter. Each call of the program finishes within 60 seconds. The program runs as a single process and starts no subprocess, fork or process pool. It reads no clock and imports none of random, uuid or secrets. The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR and its own directory, and write nothing outside OUT_DIR. Use only the Python standard library, and open no network connection. No except clause in the program discards an error, and every except clause names the exception classes it catches. Every function in the program is at most 60 lines long. Leave the shipped extract unchanged.

Each what-if is worked out by rerunning the whole ledger close and sweep with exactly the change named, on a copy of the extract, with everything else as shipped. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its own right. Answer these nine:

1. The register gives envelope VB18 a need two dollars larger than shipped. What exit and rounds figure does the central household report, and what final balances for VB18 and VA98?
2. The register gives envelope VF80 a need 14 dollars smaller than shipped. What exit, rounds figure and damping figure does the east household report?
3. The central household's `damping_percent` in the governing parameter sheet takes each whole-number value from 20 to 60 in turn. At which of those values does the central household end with the exit `stalled`?
4. The register gives envelope VD27 a need 18 dollars smaller than shipped. What exit, rounds figure and damping figure does the east household report, and what final balances for VF45 and VD27?
5. In the `keep_plan` table, every envelope of the west household moves to the plan coded `KP-1` followed by its category code, and the row for category code C46 is removed from `stmt_fees.csv`. On that copy, `charge_cents` on the row for category code C33 takes each whole-number value from 135 to 175 in turn. For which of those values does the program write its reports?
6. `cutoff_seq` in `office.ini` takes each whole-number value from 1 to 80 in turn. At which of those values does the west household report its smallest moved dollars, and what is that figure?
7. The register gives envelope VF80 a need 14 dollars smaller than shipped. How many envelopes of the five households end with a final balance at or above their need?
8. The central household's `damping_percent` in the governing parameter sheet is 20. What moved dollars does the central household report?
9. The west household's `round_budget` in the governing parameter sheet is 3. What moved dollars does the west household report?

In your final message, give the nine what-if answers. instruction:
# Close the coexistence measurement year

The national band coexistence register must publish its occupancy measurement. Its corpus sits at `/app/data`: monthly register extracts, zone office logs, committee minute books, reference tables, observation records, configuration layers and policy notes. Everything that governs the measurement is written in that corpus and nowhere else.

Work offline. Online lookup of any kind is not allowed, and no outside source describes this register. You have 14400 seconds to complete this task.

## Deliverables

Write exactly these files into `/app/out`, and nothing else:

`/app/out/derive_report.py`, `/app/out/summary.json`, `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json`, `/app/out/region_East.json`, `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and `/app/out/segment_public.json`.

`output_contract.md` in the corpus fixes every key name, every value type, the ordering of every list and the exactness of every figure. Follow it to the letter. Every measure is an exact integer count of kilohertz seconds and no document may carry a floating point value. A document counts only when every figure in it is exact. A figure that is close is a figure that is wrong, and no rounded, scaled or abbreviated measure is accepted anywhere.

## What the measurement must satisfy

1. The measurable spectrum follows the band plan and the channel raster, including every channel the raster withdraws.
2. Every holder reference reaches its canonical form, and the redirections are closed to a fixpoint.
3. Each grant carries the licence segment and the filing zone that the registry and the status history give it.
4. The visibility cutoff of `measure_config.ini` governs every source record, every state event and every notice.
5. The governing record of each layer is chosen under the tiebreak this register uses, which you must settle from the corpus rather than assume.
6. Each field group of each grant is settled by precedence, including the documented exception, which you must also settle from the corpus rather than assume.
7. The clock keying of the zone summer windows is settled from the corpus evidence.
8. Every stamp reaches universal time under the unit and clock declarations of the corpus.
9. Every grant the register withdrew is withdrawn, and every remaining grant is tested against the reject codes in the published order, with one code recorded for each rejected grant.
10. The active intervals of every surviving grant follow its state events.
11. Every extent is trimmed to the usable channels and to the measurement horizon.
12. The reservation recurrences are expanded, the exceptions are applied, and the reserved spectrum is subtracted.
13. Every subordinate grant is clipped to the measurable extent of its parent, in dependency order.
14. The final extents of each grant are reduced as the contract describes before anything counts them.
15. The covered set, the part covered once and the part covered twice or more are measured per zone and in total.
16. The excess of every overlap cell is charged as the contract describes, and each zone names its highest charged grants.
17. Each zone union is broken down by local calendar month and by band.
18. Each segment is measured and names its largest holders.
19. The duty audit runs over the local months of every audited holder.
20. Every record file is recounted, compared against the manifest, and every reject code and note code of the vocabulary is tallied.
21. `/app/out/derive_report.py` is rerunnable. Invoked as `python3 derive_report.py <corpus_dir> <output_dir>` it reads a corpus laid out like this one, writes the same nine json documents into the output directory, uses only the python standard library, reads nothing outside the corpus directory it is given, writes nothing outside the output directory it is given, and leaves the corpus unchanged.

## Closing message

Finish with a message that states, as exact integers in plain prose:

1. the number of grant identifiers that carry a visible governing record in all three layers, counted over every grant identifier in the register including the withdrawn ones;
2. the union measure this register would publish if the visibility cutoff admitted every record;
3. the number of reservation occurrences across the four zones if the exceptions file were ignored;
4. the number of grants whose governing layer for the exception field group is moved by the exception, counted over the grants that survive withdrawal and pass every reject test;
5. the number of alias identifiers that need three or more redirections;
6. the number of distinct frequency bounds among the final extents of the East zone, counting a shared lower and upper bound once;
7. the number of grants that take their time group and their frequency group from different layers, counted over the grants that survive withdrawal;
8. the total of every declared row count in the manifest;
9. the number of grants that carry more than one final extent.

None of those nine figures belongs in any document. In the same message name, for each of the three rules you had to settle from evidence, the corpus file that settled it and what that file showed. State the residual of three identities: the four zone unions against the total union, the once covered part plus the twice or more covered part against the union, and the charged excess against the excess. Say plainly anything you could not finish.

instruction:
A model serving fleet ran a small program called the inference gate. Every shift it read the run of metered inference probes, scored each probe into a verdict, and rolled the shift up per endpoint, per precision class and for the fleet as a whole. When the serving controller was replaced the gate went with it and nobody kept a copy. What survives is in `/app/data`: one recorded shift, one older shift the team had already worked through and published the verdicts for, and a short file of digests over the four reports the gate wrote for the recorded shift.

The probes of each shift ship as a binary file, `probes.bin`, in the format `/app/data/wire-format.md` documents; decode it to recover the probe records before you do anything with them. The notes in `/app/data/gate.md` and `/app/data/reports.md` describe the gate and its four reports: the input columns, the way the meter column has to be read back, the carried endpoint state, the ordered stages, the verdict ladder, the key set of every report, the byte form each is written in, what the gate writes for a shift holding no probe at all, and how each digest is taken. What they do not give is any of the numbers, and they do not list them. Every figure the stages apply, every mode the carry update names and every threshold the ladder and the rollups consult was a controller constant nobody wrote down, and working out what that list even holds is part of the job. Read both notes end to end before you write anything: they are the only description of the contract you have to meet.

The evidence comes in two parts. First the worked example: `/app/data/example_probes.bin` with the four `example_` lookup tables beside it is an older shift, and `/app/data/example_verdicts.jsonl` holds the verdicts the gate wrote for it. Nothing else was published for that shift and nothing says which parts of the gate it exercises, so what it settles and what it leaves open is yours to work out.

The second part is thinner. `/app/data/probes.bin` and the four lookup tables beside it are the recorded shift, and no report for it survives. `/app/data/digest.json` carries one sha256 over each of the four reports, and a digest goes green only when every probe of the shift resolves correctly. There is no partial signal underneath it and no score is confirmed until the whole shift is. Everything the worked example leaves open has to be reasoned out of the stage order and the carried state, then confirmed in one go.

Rebuild the gate as a single reusable program at this path:

```text
/app/out/gate.py
```

The program takes two command line arguments, the input directory first and the output directory second, and writes `verdicts.jsonl`, `endpoints.json`, `precision.csv` and `shift.json` into the output directory in the exact form `/app/data/reports.md` describes, down to the key order, the separators, the integer formatting and the trailing newline of every file. It has to work on any shift in this schema rather than the recorded one alone: it will be driven over shifts you have never seen, holding endpoints, runtimes, variants and callers that are not in this directory, and over a shift holding no endpoint and no probe at all. Use only the Python standard library. Work every figure out from the input files at run time and keep precomputed answers out of the program. Two runs over one input directory must write byte identical files. Treat everything in `/app/data` as read only and leave it unchanged, and keep any scratch work elsewhere.

Check your fit rather than settling on the first reading that matches part of what you have. Set a block of the recorded shift aside while you work the constants out, then replay that held back block and check it too. Where two readings both fit what you have looked at, build a small input of your own on which they disagree and run both over it. Work one figure out a second time through a calculation separate from the program you deliver. Before you finish, take the digest of each of your own four output files and check all four against the published ones.

Run your finished program over `/app/data` and give a closing report in your final message. State each of these ten figures, using these names, as plain whole numbers measured over the recorded shift, and keep every one of them out of the report files themselves:

```text
total_score          the sum of score over every probe in the recorded shift
total_backlog        the sum of backlog_before over every probe in the recorded shift
top_score_total      the sum of top_score over every endpoint
flagged_score        the sum of score over every probe that resolved to flagged
saturate_band_score  the sum of score over every probe carrying the saturate band
high_band_score      the sum of score over every probe carrying the high band
base_band_score      the sum of score over every probe carrying the base band
clear_score          the sum of score_total over every endpoint that ended on clear
throttle_endpoints   how many endpoints ended on the throttle disposition
budget_end_total     the sum of budget_end over every endpoint
```

A partial gate that is written down and reported on is worth far more than a perfect one that never gets written. Put a first working version of the program at the deliverable path early, while you are still unsure of most of the constants, and print the ten figures from it. Everything after that is improvement on something that already exists.

Watch the clock and stop yourself. Work on the constants for at most 1500 seconds of elapsed time. The moment those 1500 seconds are gone, or the moment your last few attempts have taught you nothing new, stop the recovery work whatever state it is in, rewrite the program from the best reading you have, run it over `/app/data`, state the ten figures and end your turn. Do not carry on until the limit below is reached: that limit is where the work is cut off, not where it is meant to finish, and reaching it is a failure even if the code was close. Ending your turn early with partial work written down is what finishing this job looks like.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
The Kettleridge beamtime facility closed one custody epoch and withdrew the publication. The replay the desk ran finishes, writes a full and plausible set of documents, and still gets the credit state wrong: the ledger it publishes disagrees with the same ledger rebuilt from the first event, and at some steps it hands credit to a station that could not have held it. What survives is the working papers under `/app/data`: the epoch contract, one paper per stage, the policy notes, the closed vocabularies, the registers with their revision histories, and this epoch's journal, checkpoint, link and archive material. Every identifier, revision, control value and threshold was minted for this epoch alone, so no source outside `/app/data` settles any of it.

Start at `/app/data/00_open_this_first.txt`, then `/app/data/custody_program_contract.md`, which names the fourteen stages and the paper that specifies each one. `/app/data/data_lineage.md` maps each paper to its stage and names the papers that govern nothing. `/app/data/readings_not_in_force.md` lists readings of these papers this facility does not support, each beside the reading in force. The file names describe a role, not the contents, so open a paper before you decide what it holds.

Three papers are not plain text, and each governs the values listed for it below. `/app/data/custody_parameter_workbook.xlsx` holds the class conversion factors, the class reversal scales, the class carry quanta and the per revision allotment ceilings across two sheets, one in force and one superseded; pick the live sheet by matching its epoch key cell against the epoch header, not by name and not by position. `/app/data/custody_board_memo.pdf` holds the revalidation round ceiling, the implausible quantity ceiling and the settlement floor. `/app/data/precedence_directive.docx` holds the five level re offer ladder, the duplicate target rule and the dependency closure rule. Read all three.

`/app/data/project.zip` holds the `bcrep` package as the facility currently runs it. Extract it, work out where it departs from the papers, and repair it there. Its own suite passes as it shipped, which tells you where the faults are absent rather than where they are.

Deliver the repaired package as `/app/out/package.zip`, laid out with `pyproject.toml` at the archive root, a `src/bcrep` source tree, and the shipped `tests` directory carried through unchanged, module for module and byte for byte. Keep every module `/app/data/package_expectations.toml` names. Restrict it to the Python standard library on the 3.12 series. It has to run as `python3 -m bcrep --data <papers> --out <destination>` with the two options in either order, create the destination when it is absent, write the derived documents there and write nothing else there, and leave the paper directory byte for byte as it found it. Hold nothing about this epoch inside it: every identifier, count, control value, threshold and vocabulary member has to be read from the directory it is pointed at. Two runs over one directory have to produce identical bytes, and the same epoch under another directory name has to produce them again.

Publish every whole quantity as a whole number of the unit its stage names, and every ratio at exactly twelve decimal places, in exact rational arithmetic, rounding where the stage paper places it and nowhere else. Keep binary floating point out of the derivation and publish no negative zero. Carry the balances, the nested allotments, the derived counters, the pending queue and the applied and reversed ledgers from one event into the next rather than settling a step on its own. A replay that opens from a restored checkpoint has to reach the same state as a replay of the same end boundary from the first event.

Write the preparation record `/app/out/unit_normalisation.json`, `/app/out/alias_resolution.jsonl`, `/app/out/canonical_order.csv` and `/app/out/quarantine_ledger.csv`. Write the boundary record `/app/out/checkpoint_selection.json`, `/app/out/replay_window.json`, `/app/out/dependency_closure.json` and `/app/out/checkpoint_reconciliation.json`. Write the replay record `/app/out/transition_log.jsonl`, `/app/out/compensation_register.csv`, `/app/out/derived_counters.csv` and `/app/out/eligibility_passes.json`. Write the settlement record `/app/out/final_state.json`, `/app/out/derived_index.jsonl`, `/app/out/equivalence_report.json`, `/app/out/state_at_event.json` and `/app/out/bounded_replay.json`. Write the repair record `/app/out/repair_report.json`, `/app/out/selftest.json`, `/app/out/defect_register.md` and `/app/out/verification_notes.md`. Write `/app/out/run_manifest.txt` carrying the core digest and the publication digest, and `/app/out/summary.json` carrying the control totals.

Match every document to `/app/data/output_schema_reference.md` exactly, header line, column order, row order, key names and value types, and follow `/app/data/serialisation_and_digest_contract.md` for encoding, line endings, key ordering, indentation and the trailing newline. Take the two digests last, over the bytes already written.

Read `/app/data/00_open_this_first.txt` again before you decide a branch is absent. This epoch is one acquisition profile and does not reach every documented branch, so implement each quiet branch from its stage paper rather than from what this epoch happens to exercise.

Report, in your final message, the live workbook sheet with the epoch key cell you matched it on, the checkpoint you selected with its watermark position, the count of events set aside under each reason code, the class carry quantum that governs the station holding the largest settled balance, the number of re offer rounds you ran with whether the run settled, the compensating events you recorded as void beside the reason each one was void, and every defect you repaired beside the stage it sits in.

You have 3600 seconds to complete this task.

The array timing network has closed one publication interval, the publication was withdrawn and the engineer who ran it is gone. What survives are the working papers under `/app/data`, the network contract, one specification per stage, the policy papers, the closed vocabularies and the interval's acquisition, calibration, archive and register material. Every identifier, epoch, delay and control value was minted for this interval alone, so nothing online and no source outside `/app/data` settles it. Recompute the interval and hand back the published documents and the program that produces them.

Start at `/app/data/readme_first.txt`, then `/app/data/network_contract_overview.md`, which names the thirteen stages and their specifications. `/app/data/data_lineage.md` maps each paper to its stage and names the papers that govern nothing. `/app/data/known_traps_and_footguns.md` lists fifty readings of these papers this network does not support, each beside the reading in force. The file names describe a role, not the contents.

Two papers are not plain text and carry values found in no other file. `/app/data/timing_network_workbook.xlsx` holds the class ceiling weights, the node weight cap and the uncertainty component table across two sheets, one live and one a superseded draft. `/app/data/network_calibration_memo.pdf` holds the oscillator weight cap, the cap sweep budget and the minimum history length. Read both, and select the live sheet by matching its key cell against the interval header, not by name or position.

Work the thirteen stages in order. Attribute every acquisition row onto the grid, set aside the rows the ordered predicates catch and pick one canonical reading per cluster. Select the applicable delay report for each canonical reading and apply it in the unit the readings use. Bring every reading to one sense. Build the link graph from the register, split it into components, root each and grow its spanning tree on the uncertainty a node carries back to its root. Carry the tree paths into node offsets and record dead time rather than filling it. Turn the node offsets and the local monitor into a deviation series per oscillator. Predict every oscillator from the previous interval's archive, take the residual dispersion and form the raw weights. Run the caps in the order the capping policy states, without letting the grid cost the weight vector any mass. Form the free ensemble scale at every epoch and steer it onto the primary realisation. Publish the node offsets, the uncertainty budget and the dissemination ledger, and take the digests last.

Publish every whole quantity as a whole number in the unit its stage names, and every ratio at exactly twelve decimal places, in exact rational arithmetic, rounding where the stage specification places it and nowhere else. Keep binary floating point out of the derivation and publish no negative zero.

Deliver twenty seven derived documents. Write `/app/out/reading_ledger.csv`, `/app/out/link_differences.psv`, `/app/out/oscillator_series.csv`, `/app/out/weight_book.json`, `/app/out/ensemble_scale.csv` and `/app/out/steered_scale.csv` as the six core files, and `/app/out/publication_manifest.json` carrying the core digest over those six and the publication digest over the other twenty six. Write the acquisition record `/app/out/withdrawal_ledger.tsv`, `/app/out/calibration_selection.csv`, `/app/out/link_graph.json`, `/app/out/epoch_grid.csv` and `/app/out/deadtime_ledger.jsonl`. Write the ensemble record `/app/out/prediction_book.json`, `/app/out/dispersion_table.csv`, `/app/out/weight_sweep_trace.jsonl` and `/app/out/steering_plan.json`. Write the dissemination record `/app/out/node_offsets.csv`, `/app/out/uncertainty_budget.tsv` and `/app/out/dissemination_ledger.psv`. Write one report per named node, `/app/out/node_report_nd_arden.json`, `/app/out/node_report_nd_calder.json`, `/app/out/node_report_nd_jarrow.json` and `/app/out/node_report_nd_lyddon.json`. Write `/app/out/network_reconciliation.xml`, the summaries `/app/out/timescale_report.md` and `/app/out/ensemble_summary.md`, and the site index `/app/out/node_index.conf`.

Match every document to `/app/data/output_schema_reference.md` exactly, header line, column order, row order, key names and JSON value types, and follow `/app/data/serialisation_and_digest_contract.md` for encoding, line endings, key ordering, indentation, empty file shape and the trailing newline.

Write `/app/out/timescale.py` to the contract in `/app/data/timescale_program_contract.md`. It has to accept a data option and an out option in either order, create the output directory when absent, write the twenty seven documents there, exit zero, write nothing else there and leave its input directory byte for byte as it found it. Restrict it to the Python standard library; it has to read the workbook and the memo. Hold nothing about this interval inside it: every identifier, count, control value, threshold and vocabulary member has to be read from the directory it is pointed at. Two runs over one input directory have to produce identical bytes, and the same interval under another directory name has to produce them again.

Read `/app/data/corpus_sentinel_note.txt` before you decide a branch is absent. This interval is one acquisition profile and does not reach every documented branch, so implement the quiet branches from their specifications.

Report, in your final message, the canonical reading count and the rows set aside under each reason, every component with its role and root, the tree edges of the anchored component in admission order, the excluded oscillators with their reasons, the oscillator that took a class ceiling weight and the ceiling it took, the two cap values with the outcome of each capping pass, the steering step and its outcome, the withheld nodes with the status of each, and the live workbook sheet key with the sheet you took it from.

instruction:
You are the policy convergence engineer for the offline security policy compiler installed as sealb-ctl. The source archive `/app/data/tool.zip` ships a broken stdlib-only CLI. The written derivation contract lives in `/app/data/config_contract.md`, and `/app/data/config_schema.json`, `/app/data/defaults.json`, `/app/data/env_overrides.json`, `/app/data/validation_rules.json`, and `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` complete the spine. The fifty evidence corpora `/app/data/c01_cve_severity.csv` through `/app/data/c50_oauth_scopes.bang` carry the rows. Every bit of every delivered artifact must be derived from these files; nothing may be invented, networked, or hand-written. Use only the Python standard library.

Satisfy every one of these requirements:

1. Extract `/app/data/tool.zip` safely to `/app/tool` and repair the broken CLI so every subcommand runs offline.
2. Replay `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` strictly in ascending `seq` order; the file is intentionally out of order.
3. Classify each journal operation against `/app/data/validation_rules.json`; a `set` on an integer spine key must carry a JSON integer value inside its `bounds`, not a JSON string of digits.
4. Treat a valid `unset` as a restore to the `defaults.json` value for that key; last-set-wins while ignoring `unset` is wrong.
5. Generate the base spine as `/app/out/config.json` by driving the repaired CLI (init / set / validate), not by hand-writing JSON.
6. Produce the four zone profiles at `/app/out/profile_core.json`, `/app/out/profile_edge.json`, `/app/out/profile_dmz.json`, `/app/out/profile_mgmt.json` by starting from the finished spine, applying `/app/data/env_overrides.json` deltas, and replaying only that zone's valid journal operations.
7. Reduce the fifty corpora into `/app/out/aggregates.json`. The effective upper bound of every corpus is the composite shift described in requirement 24; a single misclassified journal op moves the effective upper bound of every one of the fifty corpora, which is why the three moduli are pairwise coprime.
8. Count a row only when its `zone` is byte-exactly one of `core`, `edge`, `dmz`, `mgmt`, its `flag` is byte-exactly `active`, and `str(int(value)) == value` on the raw field bytes. Reject `-0`, `-00`, `-000`, leading zeros, leading `+`, surrounding spaces, underscores, hex, floats, units, words, scientific notation, and every non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari U+0966..U+096F, Arabic-Indic U+0660..U+0669, Gujarati U+0AE6..U+0AEF, full-width U+FF10..U+FF19).
9. Mirror aggregates into `/app/out/aggregates.csv`, `/app/out/aggregates.tsv`, `/app/out/aggregates.xml`, `/app/out/aggregates.ini`, `/app/out/aggregates.env`, `/app/out/aggregates.md`, and `/app/out/aggregates.txt`, corpora in sorted name order; `.env` keys upper-cased.
10. Emit `/app/out/zone_totals.json` with the counted-row total per active zone across every corpus.
11. Emit `/app/out/corpus_index.json` with `count` and a `corpora` list carrying `name`, `format`, `op`, `lo`, `hi`, `eligible_rows`, and `value`.
12. Emit `/app/out/posture.json` with `aggregate_total`, `corpus_count`, `max_corpus`, `max_value` (ties broken by the earlier name), `nonzero_corpora`, `zip_sha256` (sha256 hex of `/app/out/tool.zip` bytes), `config_sha256` (sha256 hex of `/app/out/config.json` bytes), and `touch_rejected` (count of rejected `touch` journal operations).
13. Emit `/app/out/rejected_ops.json` with `rejected` (the ascending `seq` list of every invalid journal operation) and `count`.
14. Emit `/app/out/validation_report.json` with `ok` and `checks` covering `all_artifacts_present`, `config_matches_policy`, `config_scalar_flat`, `command_failures`, `rejected_ops` (the same ascending `seq` list as `rejected_ops.json`'s `rejected`), per-zone `profiles` (`scalar_flat`, `trailer`), `corpus_count`, `aggregate_total`, `commands_through_cli` (count of CLI invocations captured in `report.json`'s `commands` list; at least 53 covering `init`, every `set`, `validate`, `export-report`, and the fifty `aggregate` calls), and `zip_shift` (equal to `Z mod 53` from requirement 24).
15. Emit `/app/out/summary.json` with `tool`, `profile_tag`, `trailer`, `profiles`, `artifacts` (in the order the `summary.json` entry of `/app/data/config_contract.md` gives), `artifact_count`, `inputs` (sorted names of every file under `/app/data`), `input_count`, `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`.
16. Emit `/app/out/report.json` through the repaired tool's `export-report` subcommand with `ok`, `tool`, `config_path`, `config_sha256` (sha256 hex of `/app/out/config.json` bytes), `trailer`, and `commands` (one object per CLI call, each with `argv`, `returncode`, `stdout`). No timestamps or run-dependent fields.
17. Rebuild the repaired tool deterministically as `/app/out/tool.zip` (ZIP_STORED, fixed epoch, fixed external_attr, sorted member order) so its sha256 is reproducible across runs.
18. Emit `/app/out/manifest.sha256`: one `<sha256>  <name>` line per delivered artifact except `tool.zip`, `report.json` and `manifest.sha256` itself, names in sorted order, two spaces between.
19. Every JSON artifact is written with these exact parameters: UTF-8, `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, indent=2, separators=(",", ": "), ensure_ascii=False)`, plus a single trailing `\n`. Default `json.dumps(obj)` breaks the manifest.
20. The configuration must stay flat scalars only; no nested dicts or lists in `/app/out/config.json` or in any profile.
21. Keep the workflow deterministic and offline: no network, no wall-clock timestamps, no random seeds, no reliance on dict insertion order. Running the pipeline twice must produce byte-identical artifacts.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not consult online solutions or hints specific to this task.

22. The journal replay is stateful.
23. The journal carries a third op `touch` in addition to `set` and `unset`. A `touch` is valid only when its `value` is byte-equal to the key's current post-replay value at that moment; otherwise it is rejected and counts toward J. `touch` never changes the spine.
24. The effective upper bound of every corpus is `hi + (R mod 97) + (J mod 31) + (Z mod 53)`, where Z is the first 16 hex characters of `sha256(/app/out/tool.zip)` parsed as a hex integer. The three moduli (97, 31, 53) are pairwise coprime, so any error anywhere in the pipeline (misclassified op, non-reproducible ZIP, miscount of rejected ops) moves the effective upper bound of every corpus.

instruction:
Implement the codec for POLYP, a proprietary field element container the Quadrature evaluation grid writes. The container directory holds a written specification for the format together with supporting reference material; read the specification carefully and work out the grammar, the record modes, the state semantics, the rejection rules and the CRC trailer from what it documents. Everything a decoder and encoder need is written down somewhere under `/app/data`, and part of the task is deciding which of those files matters for a given question. Eight situations a container can present are settled by neither the specification nor its companion notes; deciding how the decoder treats them is part of the task.

Your job is to deliver a decoder and an encoder that agree with that specification on captures you will not see. Write the decoder to `/app/decode.py` and the encoder to `/app/encode.py`. `/app/decode.py`, invoked as `python3 /app/decode.py <input.vcm>`, should print one JSON object to stdout and exit 0, with nothing else on stdout, and it should still exit 0 when a file turns out to be damaged. `/app/encode.py`, invoked as `python3 /app/encode.py <document.json> <output.vcm>`, should read a document in that same JSON shape and write the container it came from, reproducing the original file byte for byte. A decoded capture looks like this:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "flags": {"reserved_bit_0": false},
  "record_count": 2,
  "base_value": 0,
  "records": [
    {"key": 1, "mode": "raw", "wide_value": true, "long_key": false, "raw_value": 42, "value": 42},
    {"key": 2, "mode": "raw", "wide_value": true, "long_key": false, "raw_value": -3, "value": -3}
  ]
}
```

The `records` array carries exactly `record_count` objects in file order. The `value` field is always the fully-resolved signed integer for that record, and the pre-resolution payload each mode records lets the encoder rebuild the file byte for byte. Keys are integers when short and UTF-8 strings when long. Every number must be an integer, and key order and whitespace inside the JSON are up to you. When a file has to be rejected, the decoder reports the failure as a single JSON error object carrying exactly the keys the specification defines for that error, following the precedence the specification sets out.

Alongside the two programs, leave a JSONL decoding of your own illustrative examples at `/app/out/decoded_examples.jsonl`, a deterministic summary of the grammar you recovered and the header layout and mode mapping at `/app/out/format_report.json`, a deterministic self-check that each illustrative example satisfies `encode(decode(bytes)) == bytes` at `/app/out/roundtrip_report.json`, and a deterministic summary of the documented error paths and their precedence at `/app/out/error_analysis.json`, each in the shape the decoder appendix lays out. Do not put hidden or reseeded corpus answers in any of these files; they cover only examples you construct yourself.

Both programs will be run against captures you have not seen, in a clean Python 3.12 that has only the standard library, so anything you pip install here will not be present at grading time. Only the six artifact paths named above are collected; `/app/decode.py` and `/app/encode.py` cannot import helper modules you write alongside them, and they cannot read `/app/data` while they run. POLYP is invented for this task, so there is nothing about it to find elsewhere. The program implementation must generalize: your decoder and encoder will be tested against captures in the same format on other domains, so your logic cannot memorize specifics of the shipped corpus, key on input filenames, reassign standard-library functions, or change its output between runs on the same input.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

instruction:
The extract in `/app/data` comes from a river basin authority's hydrometric office for the irrigation season 2026-S3. The authority keeps four closed storage basins and balances the storage of each of them at season end, then accounts a conveyance loss for every canal gauging of the season. The documents shipped with the data govern this work.

Write one program, `/app/out/derive_report.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/derive_report.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, that balances the four basins of an extract in this layout and writes every report the documents define into OUT_DIR. OUT_DIR may not exist yet; the program creates it. Run it on the shipped extract with OUT_DIR set to `/app/out`, so that the season summary lands at `/app/out/summary.json`, the parameter audit at `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, the input-quality counts at `/app/out/data_quality.json`, the four basin reports at `/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json` and `/app/out/region_East.json`, and the two segment loss reports at `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and `/app/out/segment_public.json`, beside the other reports the documents define. It will also be run on other extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular season. The program is self-contained and imports nothing from its own folder; only the program and the nine reports named above are collected.

Every report follows the layout and form the documents give, exactly: text reports byte for byte, database and workbook reports value for value. The reports must be identical across repeated runs, working directories, extract locations and output directories. When an input breaks a rule the documents state for it, the program stops with an error and writes no report. Each call of the program finishes within 60 seconds. The program runs as a single process and starts no subprocess, fork or process pool. It reads no clock and imports none of random, uuid or secrets. The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR and its own directory, and write nothing outside OUT_DIR. Use only the Python standard library, and open no network connection. No except clause in the program discards an error, and every except clause names the exception classes it catches. Every function in the program is at most 60 lines long. Leave the shipped extract unchanged.

Each what-if is worked out by rerunning the whole balancing with exactly the change named, on a copy of the extract, with everything else as shipped. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its own right. Answer these nine:

1. `gx_a.csv` records gauging GX51226 with `sense` set to `nil`. What exit and megalitres transferred does the East basin report?
2. `gx_a.csv` records gauging GX91323 with `sense` set to `rev`. What exit and megalitres transferred does the North basin report?
3. `gx_a.csv` records gauging GX32436 with `sense` set to `fwd`. What round count and megalitres transferred does the East basin report?
4. `gx_c.jsonl` records gauging GX97622 with `drawn_by` set to `to`. What round count and megalitres transferred does the East basin report?
5. `gx_b.tsv` records gauging GX32525 with `drawn_upper` set to `0`. What exit, round count and megalitres transferred does the West basin report?
6. The South basin's `damping_percent` is taken in steps of 5 from 5 to 100. At which of these values does the South basin end balanced in the fewest rounds, and in how many rounds?
7. Every row of `sv_survey.csv` carries the same date, taken in turn as each date from 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30. On which of these dates does the public segment report its smallest conveyance loss, and what is that loss in kilolitres?
8. In a copy of the extract, reservoirs RS-311, RS-333, RS-390, RS-624, RS-774 and RS-997 each lie in a catchment of their own, C10, C11, C12, C13, C15 and C16 in that order, each catchment in the basin of the reservoir's shipped catchment (table `station` and `bs_map.xml` changed to match), and `sv_survey.csv` keeps only its rows SR04, SR05, SR06, SR08, SR11, SR14, SR15, SR16, SR17, SR18, SR22 and SR23. In that copy the `total_ml` of SR04 is taken in turn as each multiple of 10 from 9110 to 9510. For which of these totals does the program complete, and at which of them does the South basin end with the exit `cycle`?
9. The East basin's `round_budget` is 8. How many megalitres does the East basin report as transferred?

In your final message, give the nine what-if answers. Then give these figures for the shipped extract: the number of reservoirs whose balanced storage is above their opening storage, the public segment's conveyance loss minus the commercial segment's in kilolitres, the total conveyance loss in kilolitres of the net gaugings between reservoirs of the North basin, the number of net gaugings in which both reservoirs end with a balanced storage of 1800 ML or more, and the shipped run's total of megalitres transferred minus the figure in the prior balancing summary. State the total conveyance loss in kilolitres of the net gaugings outside the North basin, with its part in each of the South, West and East basins, and the difference in megalitres between the largest and the smallest balanced storage of the West basin. Report only figures your own runs printed, and state the size of any check exactly as it printed. Claim only runs and checks you actually performed, and call a check or run passing only when its last run passed.

instruction:
The perception evaluation board needs the official Q3 2026 release review of the SKYE sidewalk-robot object detector: which frozen images are evaluated, what their ground truth is, what each candidate model detected on them, how each model scores, and whether a challenger replaces the incumbent. Everything the review uses was delivered to `/app/data`: one hundred files from the camera fleet, three labelling vendors, the inference cluster, the training team and the review board. The governing contract is `/app/data/eval_standard_v3.md` (PES-3). It defines every artifact and its exact layout, and it names the document that decides each question. The deliveries contradict each other in places, and some of them look more authoritative than they are; PES-3 and the documents it names say which source wins.

Build the review engine as one self-contained file at `/app/out/evalctl.py`. Running

```bash
python3 /app/out/evalctl.py ESTATE_DIR OUT_DIR
```

must read only `ESTATE_DIR`, which is laid out like `/app/data` (same file names, different contents), and write these eight files into `OUT_DIR`: `eval_images.csv`, `exclusions.csv`, `ground_truth.csv`, `detections.csv`, `class_metrics.csv`, `operating_points.csv`, `leaderboard.json` and `reconciliation.json`.

The engine must meet all of these:

- It uses only the Python 3.12 standard library and the packages already installed in the image (pyarrow, openpyxl, python-docx, pypdf, pdfplumber, lxml, PyYAML, icalendar, tomli), and it needs no network. Only these nine packages count; packages that are present only because one of them depends on them (such as pdfminer.six or python-dateutil) are not allowed.
- Two runs on the same estate produce byte-identical files, and the output does not depend on the names or locations of `ESTATE_DIR` and `OUT_DIR`.
- It finishes an estate as large as `/app/data` within 1800 seconds on 2 CPUs. A smaller estate gets the same time per record: 1800 seconds scaled by its share of the delivered records (as PES-3 section 15 counts them) in `/app/data`, plus a quarter for margin.
- It will be run on other estates of the same layout, so every value it writes has to be derived from the estate it is given.

Then run the engine on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as the output directory, so that the review artifacts of this cycle are in place at:

- `/app/out/eval_images.csv`
- `/app/out/exclusions.csv`
- `/app/out/ground_truth.csv`
- `/app/out/detections.csv`
- `/app/out/class_metrics.csv`
- `/app/out/operating_points.csv`
- `/app/out/leaderboard.json`
- `/app/out/reconciliation.json`

Every artifact is graded exactly as PES-3 specifies it: every row, key, value, type, ordering rule and rounding step. A value that is almost right is wrong, and a row that is right on all but one field is wrong.

Do not modify anything under `/app/data`.

When you finish, reply with a short summary that names the release candidate and the decision for each challenger run, lists the deliveries you treated as not authoritative with the rule that demoted each one, and says which checks you ran to confirm the artifacts.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

The bureau's billing cycle extract is in `/app/data`. Build the billing run for this cycle as one Python program, `/app/out/transform.py`, called as `python3 /app/out/transform.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`. The documents shipped with the data govern this work. Use only the Python standard library.

Run it once on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as OUT_DIR, so that `/app/out` holds these reports: `/app/out/normalized.jsonl`, `/app/out/summary.json`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/product_summary.json`, `/app/out/region_central.json`, `/app/out/region_east.json`, `/app/out/region_north.json`, `/app/out/region_south.json`, `/app/out/region_west.json`, `/app/out/segment_consumer.json`, `/app/out/segment_corporate.json`, `/app/out/segment_enterprise.json` and `/app/out/segment_smb.json`. Every report must match exactly, byte for byte. The program will also be run on other extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular cycle. Each call finishes within 60 seconds. The output must be byte-identical across runs, working directories, extract locations and output directories. The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR and its own directory, and write nothing outside OUT_DIR. The program must open no network connection and start no other process. Leave the shipped extract in `/app/data` unchanged.

Before you finish, answer the eight what-ifs below. Each what-if is worked out by rerunning the whole billing run with exactly the change named, on a copy of the extract. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its own right. A stamp moved by some minutes keeps its own file's written form, and the day named for a stamp is the date the stamp itself shows.

1. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-33 whose stamp shows 2026-03-12 or a later date gets a stamp 9 minutes later, and plan P-BASIC gets 0 included minutes. What is the net_micro of summary.json?
2. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-08 whose stamp shows 2026-03-12 or a later date gets a stamp 9 minutes later, and minimum_invoice_micro in cycle.json becomes 20000000000. What is the sum of net_micro over the segment reports that have in_scope true?
3. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-11 whose stamp shows 2026-03-16 or a later date gets a stamp 6 minutes earlier. Take the net_micro of region_north.json on that copy, then set minimum_invoice_micro in cycle.json of the same copy to that value. On the result, what is the sum of net_micro over the region reports that have in_scope true?
4. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-31 whose stamp shows 2026-03-16 or a later date gets a stamp 9 minutes earlier. Over included minutes of plan P-EXEC in 0, 120, 240 and so on up to 1200, what is the smallest value at which the net_micro of summary.json is at most 93360000000?
5. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-18 whose stamp shows 2026-03-09 or a later date gets a stamp 6 minutes later, and rate_card in cycle.json names rate_card.csv. What is the net_micro of region_north.json?
6. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-25 whose stamp shows 2026-03-09 or a later date gets a stamp 12 minutes earlier, and holidays.csv gains the row west,2026-03-11,Founders Day. What is the after_hours amount in by_tier of summary.json?
7. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-13 whose stamp shows 2026-03-16 or a later date gets a stamp 9 minutes later, and plan P-EXEC gets 0 included minutes. What is the credit_micro of summary.json?
8. In both closing exports, every closing of handset H-15 whose stamp shows 2026-03-16 or a later date gets a stamp 6 minutes earlier, and minimum_invoice_micro in cycle.json becomes 20000000000. What is the sum of net_micro over those of the nine region and segment reports that have in_scope true?

In your final message, give the eight what-if figures by number. State the net_micro of summary.json for the shipped cycle together with the net_micro of each of the five region reports. Say how many reports your program wrote on the shipped cycle. For every check you ran on your program, give its size as the number of extracts and the number of closings it covered.
