instruction:
A model serving fleet ran a small program called the inference gate. Every shift it read the run of metered inference probes, scored each probe into a verdict, and rolled the shift up per endpoint, per precision class and for the fleet as a whole. When the serving controller was replaced the gate went with it and nobody kept a copy. What survives is in `/app/data`: one recorded shift, one older shift the team had already worked through and published the verdicts for, and a short file of digests over the four reports the gate wrote for the recorded shift.

The notes in `/app/data/gate.md` and `/app/data/reports.md` describe the gate and its four reports: the input columns, the way the meter column has to be read back, the carried endpoint state, the ordered stages, the verdict ladder, the key set of every report, the byte form each is written in, what the gate writes for a shift holding no probe at all, and how each digest is taken. What they do not give is any of the numbers, and they do not list them. Every figure the stages apply, every mode the carry update names and every threshold the ladder and the rollups consult was a controller constant nobody wrote down, and working out what that list even holds is part of the job. Read both notes end to end before you write anything: they are the only description of the contract you have to meet.

The evidence comes in two parts. First the worked example: `/app/data/example_probes.jsonl` with the four `example_` lookup tables beside it is an older shift, and `/app/data/example_verdicts.jsonl` holds the verdicts the gate wrote for it. Nothing else was published for that shift and nothing says which parts of the gate it exercises, so what it settles and what it leaves open is yours to work out.

The second part is thinner. `/app/data/probes.jsonl` and the four lookup tables beside it are the recorded shift, and no report for it survives. `/app/data/digest.json` carries one sha256 over each of the four reports, and a digest goes green only when every probe of the shift resolves correctly. There is no partial signal underneath it and no score is confirmed until the whole shift is. Everything the worked example leaves open has to be reasoned out of the stage order and the carried state, then confirmed in one go.

Rebuild the gate as a single reusable program at this path:

```text
/app/out/gate.py
```

The program takes two command line arguments, the input directory first and the output directory second, and writes `verdicts.jsonl`, `endpoints.json`, `precision.csv` and `shift.json` into the output directory in the exact form `/app/data/reports.md` describes, down to the key order, the separators, the integer formatting and the trailing newline of every file. It has to work on any shift in this schema rather than the recorded one alone: it will be driven over shifts you have never seen, holding endpoints, runtimes, variants and callers that are not in this directory, and over a shift holding no endpoint and no probe at all. Use only the Python standard library. Work every figure out from the input files at run time and keep precomputed answers out of the program. Two runs over one input directory must write byte identical files. Treat everything in `/app/data` as read only and leave it unchanged, and keep any scratch work elsewhere.

Check your fit rather than settling on the first reading that matches part of what you have. Set a block of the recorded shift aside while you work the constants out, then replay that held back block and check it too. Where two readings both fit what you have looked at, build a small input of your own on which they disagree and run both over it. Work one figure out a second time through a calculation separate from the program you deliver. Before you finish, take the digest of each of your own four output files and check all four against the published ones.

Run your finished program over `/app/data` and give a closing report in your final message. State each of these ten figures, using these names, as plain whole numbers measured over the recorded shift, and keep every one of them out of the report files themselves:

```text
total_score          the sum of score over every probe in the recorded shift
total_backlog        the sum of backlog_before over every probe in the recorded shift
top_score_total      the sum of top_score over every endpoint
flagged_score        the sum of score over every probe that resolved to flagged
saturate_band_score  the sum of score over every probe carrying the saturate band
high_band_score      the sum of score over every probe carrying the high band
base_band_score      the sum of score over every probe carrying the base band
clear_score          the sum of score_total over every endpoint that ended on clear
throttle_endpoints   how many endpoints ended on the throttle disposition
budget_end_total     the sum of budget_end over every endpoint
```

A partial gate that is written down and reported on is worth far more than a perfect one that never gets written. Put a first working version of the program at the deliverable path early, while you are still unsure of most of the constants, and print the ten figures from it. Everything after that is improvement on something that already exists.

Watch the clock and stop yourself. Work on the constants for at most 1500 seconds of elapsed time. The moment those 1500 seconds are gone, or the moment your last few attempts have taught you nothing new, stop the recovery work whatever state it is in, rewrite the program from the best reading you have, run it over `/app/data`, state the ten figures and end your turn. Do not carry on until the limit below is reached: that limit is where the work is cut off, not where it is meant to finish, and reaching it is a failure even if the code was close. Ending your turn early with partial work written down is what finishing this job looks like.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
The Corvel Basin Hydrometric Service published the January to March 2026 streamflow record of its CBHS-N gauging network from the saved compute pack `/app/data/dv_compute_pack.md`, and the published daily values in `/app/data/dv_pub_26q2.csv` are wrong. The errors reach the stage record, the gage-height corrections, the rating shifts, the winter factors, the unit values, the daily means and every statistic built on them. Everything needed to recompute the record from the raw logger shards is under `/app/data`: the handbook `/app/data/hydrometry_handbook.md` holds the rules and the order of authority, `/app/data/feed_layouts.md` describes the shard layouts, and `/app/data/output_contract.md` fixes the columns, keys, vocabularies, decimals and order of every report. Working out which of the other files can be trusted, and for what, is part of the job.

The finished work is one program, `/app/out/run_flowrecord.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/run_flowrecord.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`. It reads a data directory laid out like `/app/data` from whatever path it is given, leaves that directory untouched, and writes into OUT_DIR the twenty-one reports named below plus `manifest.json` and nothing else. After your last edit you run it once with `/app/data` as input and `/app/out` as output, so the files left in `/app/out` are its own output. It is run again later on fresh networks placed elsewhere, with other seeds, clocks, periods, profiles, minutes tables, workbook date systems, journals and shard file names, so every figure has to come out of the input at run time and nothing may be carried over from the shipped files. Each run has to finish within ten minutes, and two runs on the same input must write the same bytes. Arithmetic and rounding follow the handbook exactly. A report is accepted only when it matches the contract exactly, and every other report rests on the eight core reports (unit values, gage-height corrections, measurement evaluations, shift curves, ice periods, daily values, monthly summary and period statistics), which have to be exact on the shipped network and on every fresh one.

The reports are every selected reading as a unit value in `/app/out/unit_values.csv`; the correction segments in `/app/out/gh_corrections.tsv` and every field visit with its error in `/app/out/visit_errors.psv`; the evaluation and decision of every measurement in `/app/out/measurement_eval.csv`; the shift curve of every rating version in force in `/app/out/shift_curves.json` and the rating points used, errata included, in `/app/out/rating_tables_used.json`; the ice periods with their winter factors in `/app/out/ice_periods.jsonl`; the daily means with coverage and codes in `/app/out/daily_values.csv`, the monthly figures in `/app/out/monthly_summary.xml` and the period statistics in `/app/out/period_statistics.json`; the resolved station tokens in `/app/out/alias_resolution.csv`, the ingest counters in `/app/out/dedup_report.json`, the per-file counts in `/app/out/source_lineage.json`, every reading removed after admission in `/app/out/reading_exclusions.jsonl` and every unit-value edit with its outcome in `/app/out/amendment_ledger.psv`; the governing settings applied in `/app/out/parameters_used.yaml`; the comparisons with the published daily values in `/app/out/variance_vs_published.csv`, with the published shift worksheet in `/app/out/shift_vs_published.csv`, with the dashboard export in `/app/out/dashboard_disagreements.tsv` and with the unit-value cache in `/app/out/cache_divergence.jsonl`; and the summary in `/app/out/reconciliation.md`. The manifest, `/app/out/manifest.json` for the run into `/app/out`, lists the other reports in contract order with their sizes and SHA-256 digests.

Use only the Python standard library. Do not modify, add or delete anything under `/app/data`. When you finish, `/app/out` holds only the program and the twenty-two files named above; keep scratch work elsewhere.

Your final message lists the defects of the published run, each with the handbook section or minutes table that overrides it, and names the tables, sheets and files you set aside.

instruction:
One shift of the Kestrel Point terminal has closed, its ledgers were published and the publication was withdrawn after the vessel agents disputed it. What survives is the working papers under `/app/data`, minted for this shift alone, so nothing outside them settles anything. Recompute the shift and hand back the published documents and the program that produces them.

Start at `/app/data/readme_first.txt`, then `/app/data/terminal_contract_overview.md`, which names the fourteen stages and their specifications. `/app/data/data_lineage.md` maps each paper to its stage and names the papers that govern nothing. File names describe a role, not a content, so open them.

Three papers are not plain text and carry values found nowhere else. `/app/data/quay_capacity_workbook.xlsx` holds the ration damping fraction, the mass register factors, the base move charge, the teu factors and the vessel slot ceilings across six sheets, one of them live. `/app/data/berth_operations_memo.pdf` holds the ration pass budget, the minimum step, the protection depth, the surcharge ladder and the gang roster. `/app/data/stowage_ordering_directive.docx` holds the stowage ordering keys and the class ranks. Read all three, and select the live sheet by matching its key cell against the shift reference, not by name and not by position.

Work the fourteen stages in order. Put every move order on the slot grid, set aside what the ordered ladder catches, and pick one canonical order per cluster. Normalise every mass into kilograms through the register its declaration names, settle the vessel obligations, and materialise the opening yard. Build the move dependency graph and break its cycles by the stated rule. Admit each move against the yard as it stood immediately before that move, settling reserved capacity before free capacity is counted. Carry the state forward, set the planned stream against the crane confirmations, derive the rehandles and equipment charges from that state rather than from any count the papers carry, publish the capacity of every block against every slot, join the cutoff notices to the yard state you derived, ration the quay and settle what each vessel loads.

Publish every whole quantity as a whole number, every ratio at exactly nine decimal places, every charge in whole cents and every crane figure in whole minutes, in exact rational arithmetic, rounding where the stage specification places it and nowhere else. Keep binary floating point out and publish no negative zero.

Deliver thirty nine documents. Write the fifteen of the stage spine: `/app/out/canonical_events.csv`, `/app/out/container_dimensions.csv`, `/app/out/vessel_obligation.csv`, `/app/out/initial_occupancy.psv`, `/app/out/event_order.csv`, `/app/out/cycle_break_report.json`, `/app/out/move_eligibility.csv`, `/app/out/yard_occupancy.psv`, `/app/out/movement_accounting.jsonl`, `/app/out/rehandle_ledger.jsonl`, `/app/out/yard_capacity.csv`, `/app/out/load_eligibility.csv`, `/app/out/ration_trace.jsonl`, `/app/out/terminal_reconciliation.csv` and `/app/out/publication_manifest.json`, which carries the core digest over the six core documents and the publication digest over the rest. Write `/app/out/rejected_moves.tsv`, `/app/out/rejection_reasons.csv`, `/app/out/accepted_moves.csv`, `/app/out/container_state_history.psv`, `/app/out/container_state_final.csv` and `/app/out/dependency_order.csv`. Write `/app/out/yard_reservations.psv`, `/app/out/block_utilization.csv`, `/app/out/equipment_usage.csv`, `/app/out/equipment_exceptions.tsv` and `/app/out/slot_accounting.csv`. Write `/app/out/vessel_cutoff_status.csv`, `/app/out/vessel_container_manifest.psv`, `/app/out/load_sequence_ledger.json`, `/app/out/deferred_containers.tsv`, `/app/out/departure_ledger.json`, `/app/out/vessel_reconciliation.xml`, `/app/out/exception_summary.tsv` and `/app/out/audit_trail.conf`. Write one report per berth, `/app/out/berth_report_bt_alder.json`, `/app/out/berth_report_bt_calder.json` and `/app/out/berth_report_bt_marlow.json`, and the summaries `/app/out/daily_operational_summary.md` and `/app/out/final_control_totals.json`.

Match every document to `/app/data/output_schema_reference.md` exactly, header, column order, row order, key names and JSON value types, and follow `/app/data/serialisation_and_digest_contract.md` for encoding, line endings, key order, indentation, empty shape and trailing line feeds. `/app/data/worked_examples.md` fixes the form of the free text documents on an invented shift, so take shape from it and no figure.

Write `/app/out/yardledger.py` to the contract in `/app/data/yardledger_program_contract.md`. It has to accept a data option and an out option in either order, create the output directory when absent, write the thirty nine documents there, exit zero, write nothing else and leave its input directory as it found it. Restrict it to the Python standard library and have it read all three office papers. Hold nothing about this shift inside it: every identifier, control value, threshold, boundary and rung code has to be read from the directory it is pointed at. Two runs over one input directory have to produce identical bytes, and so has the same shift under another directory name.

Read `/app/data/corpus_sentinel_note.txt` before deciding a branch is absent. This shift leaves some documented branches unreached; implement those from their specifications.

Report, in your final message, the canonical event count and the orders set aside under each rung, the live sheet key with the sheet you took it from, the components the cycle breaking touched with the edge removed from each, the moves the reserved rung bound, the boxes whose mass was never declared, the vessels with no applicable call, the ration outcome of every slot and berth pairing with its pass count, and the boxes the load deferred with the charge each was republished at.

instruction:
The 2027 executive operations calendar store sits in `/app/data` together with the documents that govern how it is reconciled. The replicas, journals, registers and schedules in that folder disagree with one another in ways those documents settle, and a retired scheduler left figures behind that the current rules no longer produce. Rebuild the reconciliation program and leave its output on disk.

The program is `/app/schedule_repair.py`, a Python 3 program that uses only the standard library and runs as `python3 /app/schedule_repair.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, taking both directories from those two arguments and never from a fixed path. It reads only the store under DATA_DIR, writes nothing outside OUT_DIR apart from temporary files in the system temporary directory (`TMPDIR`, or `/tmp` when it is unset), creates OUT_DIR when it is absent, and two runs over one store write byte-identical files. The same program is run again over other stores built under the same documented rules that you have not seen: their files carry other names, their replicas use other encodings, their policy settings, editions and offices differ and they hold different amounts of data, so nothing it does may rest on the name of a file or a directory, on the shipped figures or on the shipped encodings. After your last change to the program, run it once as `python3 /app/schedule_repair.py /app/data /app/out` and leave what it writes in place.

That run writes twenty-five reports: the merge decisions `/app/out/decisions.jsonl` and their summary `/app/out/reconciliation.json`, the outbox replay `/app/out/outbox_replay.jsonl`, the occurrence list `/app/out/occurrences.csv`, the attendee resolutions `/app/out/alias_resolutions.tsv`, the candidate resolutions `/app/out/resolutions.tsv`, the exclusion and override records `/app/out/exceptions.jsonl`, the zone transitions `/app/out/zone_transitions.tsv`, the conflicts before settling `/app/out/conflicts.jsonl`, the settling trace `/app/out/settle_moves.csv`, the settled schedule `/app/out/settled_schedule.csv` with its summary `/app/out/settle_summary.json`, the load fold `/app/out/load_steps.tsv` with `/app/out/load_summary.json`, the attendance violations `/app/out/attendance.psv`, the legs `/app/out/legs.json`, the travel blocks `/app/out/travel_blocks.csv`, the busy conflicts `/app/out/busy_conflicts.tsv`, the synchronisation state `/app/out/sync_entries.tsv` with `/app/out/sync_tokens.json`, the chargeback rollups `/app/out/chargeback_offices.json` and `/app/out/chargeback_collections.json`, the authority audit `/app/out/authority_audit.csv`, the drift report `/app/out/drift.csv` and the manifest `/app/out/manifest.json`. Nothing else is left in the output directory. Every column, key, list order and serialisation detail of these reports is fixed by the documents in `/app/data`, and every value is exact, with no tolerance anywhere.

The merge decisions, the occurrence list and the settled schedule are the core of the run, and every other report is derived from them, so a single wrong reading upstream shows up in many reports at once, and no other report of a store counts as correct unless those three are exact for the same store. Each figure has to come from the source the documents declare in force for the store being read; a figure that also appears in a lower-authority copy is still taken from its authority. A store whose conflicts cannot all be settled still produces every report.

Leave every file under `/app/data` exactly as delivered and install nothing. When you finish, state in a short paragraph the occurrence count, the number of settling rounds, the stop reason and the manifest chain head of your run, and make those figures agree with the files you wrote.

instruction:
The flat and office-format files in `/app/data` are a detector-array flux
reconciliation extract from a four-instrument imaging array observed over three
epochs. The extract ships a written reconciliation contract, a set of reference
tables spread across many files, and a pre-computed pipeline output that is
known to be faulty. Deciding which inputs feed which figure is part of the task.
Read the contract, diagnose why the pre-computed flux values are wrong, and
produce a corrected reconciliation report by recomputing every figure from the
data rather than trusting the shipped output.

`/app/data/reconciliation_contract.md` governs how every figure is computed, and
`/app/data/report_schema.md` governs what the output looks like: the keys of
every artifact, the fixed strings, the key formats and the order of every list.
Follow both exactly. Where a reference table appears in more than one file,
`/app/data/file_role_index.md` names the authoritative source for each role.

Deliver a single reusable program at `/app/out/derive_report.py`, runnable as
`python3 /app/out/derive_report.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, that reads an extract in
this schema from `DATA_DIR` and writes the full report set into `OUT_DIR`. Run
it on the shipped extract so the deliverables land at the exact paths named
here.

Write the whole-corpus report to `/app/out/summary.json`, the per-observation
reconciled flux to `/app/out/reconciled_flux.json`, the applied-calibration
audit to `/app/out/calibration_audit.json`, and the input-integrity report to
`/app/out/data_quality.json`. Write the four per-instrument rollups to
`/app/out/instrument_G1.json`, `/app/out/instrument_G2.json`,
`/app/out/instrument_G3.json` and `/app/out/instrument_G4.json`, the per-epoch
totals to `/app/out/epoch_totals.json`, and the dead-pixel redistribution
closure to `/app/out/deadpixel_closure.json`. Write the band rollup to
`/app/out/band_rollup.csv`, the epoch rollup to `/app/out/epoch_rollup.tsv`, and
the instrument rollup to `/app/out/instrument_rollup.psv`. Write the
flagged-observation list to `/app/out/flagged_observations.xml`, the objective
summary to `/app/out/objective_summary.yaml`, the human-readable report to
`/app/out/reconciliation_report.md`, and the run status to
`/app/out/run_status.txt`. Write the provenance manifest to
`/app/out/provenance_manifest.json`, the anomaly ledger to
`/app/out/anomaly_ledger.json`, the ordered flux index to
`/app/out/ordered_flux_index.json`, and the dropped-observation list to
`/app/out/dropped_observations.json`. Write the exposure attribution of the
reconciled total to `/app/out/flux_attribution.json` and the hop-by-hop
dead-pixel relay audit to `/app/out/relay_audit.json`.

The contract also carries a settlement layer that runs on top of the reconciled
flux, turning each reading into a rate over the integration time its frame
received, discarding the frames that measured nothing and the hits that are not
sky, and settling the result into a pool, an attribution and a digest. Write the
settlement account to `/app/out/settlement_summary.json`, the per-observation
settled rates to `/app/out/settled_rates.json`, the frames whose shutter aborted
to `/app/out/zero_exposure.json`, the rejected cosmic ray hits to
`/app/out/cosmic_ray_rejects.json`, the near-saturated observations to
`/app/out/near_saturation.json`, the settled attribution to
`/app/out/settled_attribution.json`, the per-band settlement rendering to
`/app/out/band_settlement.csv`, and the ranked order the digest is taken over to
`/app/out/settlement_order.json`.

The reconciled figures are also cut along three pairs of dimensions, as
sections D1, D2 and D3 of the report schema set out. Each family carries its
own serialisation and its own row order, and the schema states both for each
one. Every file named below is written even where the pair it names has no live
observation.

Write the twenty instrument-and-band cells to `/app/out/cell_G1_u.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G1_g.json`, `/app/out/cell_G1_r.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G1_i.json`, `/app/out/cell_G1_z.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G2_u.json`, `/app/out/cell_G2_g.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G2_r.json`, `/app/out/cell_G2_i.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G2_z.json`, `/app/out/cell_G3_u.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G3_g.json`, `/app/out/cell_G3_r.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G3_i.json`, `/app/out/cell_G3_z.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G4_u.json`, `/app/out/cell_G4_g.json`,
`/app/out/cell_G4_r.json`, `/app/out/cell_G4_i.json` and
`/app/out/cell_G4_z.json`.

Write the fifteen epoch-and-band grids to `/app/out/grid_E1_u.psv`,
`/app/out/grid_E1_g.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E1_r.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E1_i.psv`,
`/app/out/grid_E1_z.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E2_u.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E2_g.psv`,
`/app/out/grid_E2_r.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E2_i.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E2_z.psv`,
`/app/out/grid_E3_u.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E3_g.psv`, `/app/out/grid_E3_r.psv`,
`/app/out/grid_E3_i.psv` and `/app/out/grid_E3_z.psv`.

Write the twelve instrument-and-epoch spans to `/app/out/span_G1_E1.tsv`,
`/app/out/span_G1_E2.tsv`, `/app/out/span_G1_E3.tsv`,
`/app/out/span_G2_E1.tsv`, `/app/out/span_G2_E2.tsv`,
`/app/out/span_G2_E3.tsv`, `/app/out/span_G3_E1.tsv`,
`/app/out/span_G3_E2.tsv`, `/app/out/span_G3_E3.tsv`,
`/app/out/span_G4_E1.tsv`, `/app/out/span_G4_E2.tsv` and
`/app/out/span_G4_E3.tsv`.

The settlement layer does not reuse the conventions of the layer beneath it. Its
normalisation rounds one way and only one way, its rejection rule names the
estimator it uses and the two samples it never rejects from, its medians settle
an even sample differently from the band median above, and the order it puts
bands in is not alphabetical. The contract states each of those; take none of
them from the layer above.

Every calibrated flux is an integer in micro-jansky, and no flux figure is a
floating-point value. The contract fixes the application order of the correction
stages, the sign of each correction, where a reading meets the detector's full
well and what that does to it, how a gain label resolves to the channel that
applies, how an epoch follows from a date, how the dead-pixel redistribution
closes and how its hops are audited, which observations a band median is allowed
to be taken over, how the reconciled total is apportioned across the instruments
so the parts sum to it exactly, which source wins when two disagree, and the
rounding mode. Work each of those out from the contract and the reference tables
rather than from the order the files happen to appear in. Serialize all JSON
deterministically with sorted keys and a trailing newline, keep the output
byte-identical across reruns, and keep the output identical when the input
observation rows are reordered.

The reusable program is graded on extracts you have not seen, in this same
schema, including extracts whose reference tables hold different values from the
shipped ones. Implement the contract in general rather than memorizing the
shipped numbers. Only the artifact paths named above are collected. Use only the
Python standard library, make no network access of any kind, and read nothing
outside `DATA_DIR` and write nothing outside `OUT_DIR`.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online
solutions or hints specific to this task.

instruction:
A regional dispatch authority runs four industrial sites. Each site owns a small set of
lanes, and every accepted work order has to be placed on exactly one lane. The authority
has handed you its written rule set, its directories, and a stream of encoded work-order
packets, and it wants the season settled: which orders run, where they run, and what they
cost.

Everything you need is under `/app/data`. Survey all of it before you start. The rules
live across several policy documents, the directories and the packet stream live in
tabular and encoded form, and no single file carries the whole picture. The documents
state each rule precisely and state the invariants the finished settlement has to satisfy,
but they deliberately stop short of telling you the order in which the rules bind or the
values of the constants the packet stream was written with. Those you recover.

The packet stream travels in an encoded wire form. The encoding document names every
transform the stream may carry and names the constant each transform depends on, but the
value of each of those constants is withheld. A held-out calibration population ships
alongside the field population, together with a short list of published control figures
computed from it. Exactly one assignment of the withheld constants reproduces every
control figure at once. Recover that assignment; a wrong constant yields a stream that
still parses and still passes its checksums while carrying silently wrong values.

With the constants settled, decode the field population, resolve each order to its
governing client and its governing programme revision, decide which orders the sites can
admit, place every admitted order on a lane so that no lane rule is broken and the total
lane cost of each site is as low as any feasible placement allows, and settle the money.

Deliver a reusable program at `/app/out/derive_report.py`. It must take an input
directory as its first argument and an output directory as its second, and it must derive
everything it writes from the files in the directory it is given. Running it against a
different corpus laid out the same way must produce that corpus's settlement, so no figure
recovered from the supplied corpus may appear in it as a fixed literal. Allow it a few
minutes per corpus at most: a corpus roughly twice the size of the supplied one has to
settle well inside ten minutes on one core.

Write the season summary to `/app/out/summary.json`, the reconciliation report to
`/app/out/data_quality.json`, and one rollup per region to `/app/out/region_North.json`,
`/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json` and `/app/out/region_East.json`.
Write one rollup per service segment to `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and
`/app/out/segment_public.json`. Every placed order belongs to exactly one region rollup and
exactly one segment rollup, the two partitions cover the same orders, and the money in the
rollups has to add back to the money in the summary with nothing left over. The
reconciliation report carries the residuals of those conservation checks and the verdict
on each invariant the rule set names.

One fully-formed rollup for a small probe population ships with the corpus. Take the shape
of your region and segment rollups from it. A labelled decode of that same probe population
ships too; it is the untrapped tier and its constants are its own.

The field names and value types of the season summary, the reconciliation report and the
derivation record are fixed in `report_schema.md`, which ships with the corpus. It names the
fields and none of the values, so follow it exactly and work every value out yourself. The
probe rollup and the labelled probe decode are there for you to read, not for your program to
read; it has to run against a corpus that carries neither.

Write your derivation record to `/app/out/policy_audit.json`. It records the work rather
than the answer: the candidate space you enumerated for each withheld constant, the
verdict you reached on every candidate value, the control figure that eliminated each
rejected value, the comparison of your recovered assignment against every published
control, the number of passes your admission settlement took to reach a stable state with
the congestion figure it settled at for each site, and the shape of your placement search.

Work in this order and record it. Settle every withheld constant against the calibration
population before you derive any figure for the field population. Record a verdict for
every candidate value in a constant's domain before you select the value for that
constant. After you settle the final constant, re-run your complete derivation from
scratch so that every report you leave behind is written by that final run and no report
carries a figure from an earlier attempt. Carry every monetary figure as a whole number of
micro units from end to end. Resolve each order's client to its governing form before you
select any governing programme revision.

Do no editing of anything under `/app/data`; treat it as read-only. Do not embed values
recovered from the supplied corpus in your program as fixed literals. Your program must read
only the directory it is handed, never a path written into its own source. This container has
no network access, so work entirely from what is already on it: do not install third-party
packages and do not expect to fetch anything. The Python standard library is sufficient for
this work.

You have 21600 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
Release engineering rejected the stage-1 CI ledger of the Trainyard estate. The tool that builds it, the `trainyard` package shipped as `/app/data/project.zip`, no longer installs on the Python 3.12 runtime, and the ledgers it produced before it broke disagree with the feed's own control blocks and with the approved rules. Repair the package and rebuild the stage-1 ledger with it.

Everything you need is in `/app/data/`. The stage-1 feed is the directory itself, described by its feed index, and `/app/data/stage0_close.json` is the closing state of stage 0, which stage 1 opens from. The rules are those of the approved revision of the CI ledger specification, together with the approved errata and the governance precedence document it incorporates. Where the shipped code and the approved rules disagree, the rules win; where two feed files disagree, the governance document decides which one counts.

Deliver:

- `/app/out/package.zip`: the repaired project as an installable src-layout package (`pyproject.toml`, `src/trainyard`, and the project's own test suite, kept unchanged and passing). It must run as `python -m trainyard reconcile --feed DIR --resume STATE --out DIR` with `src` on the path, for any feed with the same structure: a later stage opens from the `summary.json` the previous stage wrote. It must find files through the feed index and their control blocks, never by file name, read only the feed and the resume state it is given, and produce identical bytes on every run. It is installed with pip and run on a plain Python 3.12 with setuptools, where the only third-party packages that exist are `PyYAML==6.0.2`, `pyarrow==18.1.0` and `pypdf==5.1.0`, and only those the repaired `pyproject.toml` declares are importable, so it cannot rely on anything else this machine happens to have.
- The stage-1 ledger your repaired package writes from `/app/data/` and `/app/data/stage0_close.json`: `/app/out/build_report.json`, `/app/out/module_core.json`, `/app/out/module_metrics.json`, `/app/out/dependency_resolution.json`, `/app/out/selftest.json` and `/app/out/summary.json`, in the formats of the specification's output section. These six files must be written by your repaired package itself, run with `--out /app/out`; do not write, copy or edit them with anything else.

Write the seven deliverables to the exact paths above; nothing else under `/app/out` is read. Each output is accepted only as an exact match of the specified content, every row and every field, including its run control stamp; a ledger that is right on most rows is still rejected. Your package is also run on a later stage feed with your `summary.json` as its resume state.

When you are done, reply with the repairs you made to the package, grouped into installation repairs and rule repairs, and with the control counts and invariants you checked, saying which of them, if any, still disagree with the ledger.

instruction:
The flat files in `/app/data` are one collection round of the Regional Household Activity Survey, exported as the collection system emitted them. A written standard and a field-level index ship with the data. The standard is the contract: it defines every rule, every record layout and the exact shape of every report, and it decides which files, and which rows inside them, are in scope.

Take the round through to a disclosure-controlled publication set, and deliver the derivation as a program somebody else can run on the next round. Build it at `/app/out/derive_survey.py`. It runs as `python3 /app/out/derive_survey.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, reads an extract in this layout from the first directory and writes the complete report set into the second in one run. Use only the Python standard library. The program takes its input directory from its first argument, never from a path written into its source, and one run may take at most 120 seconds. Run it on the shipped extract so the reports land in `/app/out`. The program itself will be run again on the shipped extract and on other extracts in the same layout, with different households, benchmarks, settings and sampling structure, and the reports it writes on each are checked against the standard.

The report set is twenty-two files: `/app/out/frame_audit.json`, `/app/out/control_totals.json`, `/app/out/control_margins.tsv`, `/app/out/response_status.json`, `/app/out/design_weights.csv`, `/app/out/adjustment_cells.json`, `/app/out/adjusted_weights.csv`, `/app/out/raking_trace.json`, `/app/out/final_weights.csv`, `/app/out/weight_diagnostics.json`, `/app/out/replicate_design.json`, `/app/out/replicate_summary.csv`, `/app/out/estimates_activity_by_region.csv`, `/app/out/estimates_tenure_by_wquintile.csv`, `/app/out/estimates_hours_by_sector.csv`, `/app/out/estimates_band_transition.csv`, `/app/out/variance_components.json`, `/app/out/cv_screening.json`, `/app/out/primary_suppression.json`, `/app/out/secondary_suppression.json`, `/app/out/disclosure_audit.tsv` and `/app/out/closure_report.json`.

Every report must match the standard exactly, with its field names, field order, row order and serialization, and every figure in it is a whole number. Running the program twice over one extract, or over a copy of it under another directory name, gives the same bytes, and the output does not depend on the order of rows inside an input file.

Two settings of the round, the order the raking margins are applied in and the point at which raking rounds, were never written into the rule files. The published pilot figures shipped with the data settle them, as the standard explains.

Leave the shipped extract under `/app/data` exactly as you found it. Nothing else belongs in `/app/out`: the twenty-two reports and the program are the whole delivery, and a scratch file, a backup copy or a working note left there counts against it. Do not look up solutions online; everything the work needs ships with the data.

When the work is done, finish with a short written summary that answers these questions about the shipped round. None of the answers is written into any report.

1. If the round's raking used the other rounding point, keeping its margin order and iteration limit, what deviation in micro-units would its last iteration leave?
2. Of the other eleven combinations of margin order and rounding point, the best one reproduces how many of the published pilot figures?
3. If the minimum publishable count were two higher, how many cells across the four tables would change between published and suppressed?
4. If the maximum publishable coefficient of variation were 500 basis points lower, how many cells would change between published and suppressed?
5. What would the finished weight total be, in micro-units, if the margins were applied in the order the rule file lists them, with the round's rounding point?
6. If the trim trigger were 100 basis points higher, to how many strata would trimming apply?
7. If the iteration limit were doubled, what is the largest number of iterations any replicate's raking would use?
8. If the secondary cascade were limited to a single pass, how many cells would be suppressed across the four tables?

instruction:
# Pulldown Cadence Conform

You are the conform engineer at a post house that assembles delivery timelines from vendor source clips. Every correction stream, reference table, configuration layer and observation log the house holds sits in `/app/data`. The document `/app/data/conform_contract.md` is the single source of truth for how a timeline resolves, and `/app/data/index.md` names every file with the tier of authority it carries. The documents beside them settle timecode counting, provenance, record layout and scenario membership. Nothing tells you which parts of the material are wrong; finding that out is the task.

The house runs five delivery scenarios named visible, peak, steady, burst and latency. Build a conform engine at `/app/out/optimize.py` that resolves one scenario against the contract. It must expose `run_scenario(data_dir, scenario)` returning the scenario record as a dictionary, and must also run as `python3 /app/out/optimize.py --data-dir D --scenario S --out F`, writing that record to the path given. Your engine will be run again on extracts nobody has seen, holding the same file names with different events, configuration values and reference windows, so every rule it applies has to come from what it reads at run time.

Write the resolved record of each scenario to `/app/out/scenario_visible.json`, `/app/out/scenario_peak.json`, `/app/out/scenario_steady.json`, `/app/out/scenario_burst.json` and `/app/out/scenario_latency.json`. Each carries `scenario`, `cutoff_utc` exactly as the configuration writes it, the resolved `delivery_family`, a `timelines` list ordered by rising timeline identifier, and a `totals` map. Each timeline carries `timeline_id`, `record_frames`, `exit_phase`, `applied_events`, `audited_events`, `rejected_events` and an `events` list in resolution order. Each event carries `event_uid`, `canonical_code`, `generation`, `outcome` drawn from applied, audited and rejected, `reason_code` from the closed set the house publishes, `source_frames`, `record_in_frames`, `record_out_frames`, `phase_in`, `phase_out`. The totals map carries `timelines`, `events`, `applied_events`, `audited_events`, `rejected_events`, `record_frames` and `exit_phase_sum`.

Write `/app/out/perf_report.json` with `module` set to the engine path, `method` set to `relative repeated median`, a `scenarios` map holding `input_events`, `admitted_events`, `applied_events`, `record_frames`, `median_ns`, `reference_median_ns` and `speedup` per scenario, a `totals` map summing the first four, and `ok` set to true. The speedup is the reference median over your own median rounded to three decimals, and your engine has to resolve a scenario faster than the legacy module.

Write `/app/out/bottleneck_analysis.json` with `reference_module` naming `/app/data/reference_conform.py`, a `stages` list taken from the stage list that module publishes, a `stage_visits` map per scenario holding the visit count the house signed off per stage, a `dominant_stage` map naming the stage with the most visits, a `hot_timelines` map holding the five timelines of each scenario with the most applied events by falling count then rising identifier, and a `phase_carry_timelines` map counting timelines whose exit phase is other than zero.

Write `/app/out/recommendations.json` with a `scenario_actions` map holding, per scenario, the three leading reason codes by falling count then rising code, each entry carrying `rank` from one, `reason_code`, `count` and the `remedy` the house publishes; a `global_top_reason`; and a `global_counts` map of each code that occurred to its count across the five. Write `/app/out/data_quality.json` with a `scenarios` map holding, per scenario, a `rejected` map of reject code to count, an `audited` map of audit code to count and a `withdrawn` count, with a `totals` map holding `rejected`, `audited` and `withdrawn` summed across the five.

Write every record with sorted keys, no spaces between tokens, and one trailing newline. Frames, phases and tallies are JSON numbers. A record counts only when every figure is exact; one frame out of place on one event fails the artifact holding it, and the same holds for every map and count above. Leave `/app/data` exactly as you found it, write nothing into `/app/out` beyond the ten paths named here, and write no partial record if resolution stops.

Close with a short message to the delivery supervisor. Give the number of applied events in the visible scenario whose record out frame would land elsewhere if the cadence phase restarted at zero for every event, carrying that restarted count forward through the timeline, and give the same figure summed across the five scenarios. Give how many events took their measurements from the tape index and how many of those came from the later of the two indexes, counting only events that reached the point of measuring the source. Give how many delete records a higher revision superseded and how many correction records changed nothing because an identical record already stood, counted over the records each scenario admitted by recorded time before the revision on the event row is brought to bear. Give how many revision contests settled on source standing and how many settled on recording time, counted over every contest the correction streams raised, including contests naming an event the scenario does not carry. Give how many events the ingest logs carried past the cutoff that the event row on its own would have admitted, and how many admitted events carry a resolved recorded time equal to the cutoff instant. Give how many timelines sit inside the longest closed nesting ring and the lowest identifier within it. Give how many overrides were turned away for want of approval scope and which approver accounted for the most, counted over the overrides that take part by recorded time, weighing approval scope on its own so that an override turned away on timing as well still counts here, together with how many of those arose in the visible scenario and how many the leading approver accounts for. Give how many events took their recorded time from an ingest log rather than their own row and which host contributed the most, counted over every event the shards of the scenario carry whether or not the cutoff admitted it. Give how many speed conversions landed exactly on a half frame among applied events and which scenario held the most. Give the ordering you settled revision contests under and how many recorded contests you fitted it against. Counts without a named scenario cover all five. Say plainly what you settled each withheld rule on and what in the material told you so. None of these figures belongs in any artifact.

Work offline from the shipped material, using the Python standard library. Do not search online for solutions, hints or reference implementations. You have 10800 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
You are the conform engineer for a regional playout channel that runs into four markets,
and one transmission day has to be recomputed from source. The previous automated conform
of that same day survives in the corpus and it is wrong, so derive the day again from the
records rather than repair the old answer. Everything you need sits under `/app/data`.

Read `/app/data/readme_first.txt`, then `/app/data/pipeline_contract_overview.md`, which
names the fourteen stages and points at the specification for each one. The file names are
deliberately non-obvious, so `/app/data/data_lineage.md` records which file feeds which
stage and which files are decoys. `/app/data/glossary_and_field_dictionary.md` defines the terms and the fields of the main
input registers. `/app/data/output_artifact_contract.md` and
`/app/data/output_schema_reference.md` fix what to write and with which columns in which
order, and `/app/data/serialisation_and_digest_contract.md` fixes the bytes down to the
line ending. Two load-bearing sources are not plain text: `/app/data/contract_terms_workbook.xlsx` is a
real workbook carrying three control sets of contract terms, and
`/app/data/regulatory_minutage_memo.pdf` is a real document that is the only publication
of three settlement constants. Both carry values the day cannot be derived without.

Derive the day and write every artifact into `/app/out`. Publish the canonical ingest
attempt of every asset with its resolved rate and source span in
`/app/out/asset_register.csv`, the per-part channel frame counts in
`/app/out/segment_conform.csv`, the conditioned position of every break in
`/app/out/break_positions.csv`, and the placed start, trim and transmitted duration of
every slot in `/app/out/slot_placement.csv`. Publish every correction in
`/app/out/conform_trace.json` and the filler for each gap in `/app/out/filler_plan.csv`.
Publish the admitted spots in `/app/out/avail_plan.tsv` and every deferral with the reason
that settled it in `/app/out/deferral_ledger.jsonl`. Publish the market substitutions in
`/app/out/market_overrides.csv`, the four per-market break sets in
`/app/out/market_avails_mk_coast.json`, `/app/out/market_avails_mk_metro.json`,
`/app/out/market_avails_mk_north.json` and `/app/out/market_avails_mk_valley.json`, and
their union in `/app/out/market_avail_stream.jsonl`. Publish the money of every admitted
spot in `/app/out/settlement_ledger.psv`, the capped obligations in
`/app/out/makegood_ledger.json`, the unpriced and empty deliveries in
`/app/out/exception_ledger.jsonl`, and the per-advertiser totals in
`/app/out/advertiser_summary.csv`. Publish the advertising frames of every market clock
hour against the regulatory cap in `/app/out/minutage_report.csv`, and the residual each
carry scope was left holding in `/app/out/carry_ledger.json`. Publish the recomputed day
against the previous computation in `/app/out/reconciliation.xml`, the transmitted day in
`/app/out/playout_schedule.ini`, the two summaries in `/app/out/day_report.md` and
`/app/out/compliance_summary.md`, and the digest and day-level figures in
`/app/out/manifest.json`.

Hand the derivation back as a reusable program at `/app/out/conform.py`. It has to take an
optional data directory after `--data` and an optional output directory after `--out`,
creating the output directory and any missing parent when they do not exist, fall back to `/app/data` and
`/app/out` when given neither, read only the directory it was given, write those
twenty-five artifacts and nothing else, and only into the directory it was told to write
to, and leave its input directory exactly as it found it. It will be run against
transmission days of this channel other than this one, so build no figure and no
identifier from this day into it, and make two runs over the same inputs produce the same
bytes. Leave `/app/out` holding those twenty-five artifacts and `conform.py` and nothing
else, and keep one run over one day inside ten minutes.

Every published quantity is exact. Every frame count is a whole number of channel frames,
every amount of money is a whole number of minor units in the advertiser settlement
currency except the `gross_major` columns, which carry the currency's own number of
decimal places, and every ratio carries exactly ten decimal places. Do the whole
derivation in exact rational or whole number arithmetic and round only when a value is
written, in the directions the stage specifications and `/app/data/rounding_policy.yaml`
set out. Take the channel rate, the timecode base and the drop frame behaviour from the
records rather than from any rounded label. Honour the broadcast day boundary the channel
configuration publishes rather than a calendar day boundary. Apply the carry rule at every
conversion into channel frames, inside the scope each stage names, and publish what each
scope was left holding. Order every artifact as `/app/data/output_schema_reference.md`
and the Published section of each stage specification require, use the delimiter each
format takes, write one header row on every delimited artifact, sort json keys at every
level, and end every file with exactly one line feed and no carriage returns.

Resolve every closed vocabulary against `/app/data/deferral_reason_reference.txt`,
`/app/data/correction_reason_reference.txt` and `/app/data/snap_side_reference.txt`, and
publish only members of those vocabularies. Treat
`/app/data/legacy_commission_table.csv`, `/app/data/blackout_overlay_drafts.xml` and
`/app/data/prior_conform_register.csv` as the rejected sources that
`/app/data/data_lineage.md` says they are, consuming the last of the three only where the
reconciliation stage reports against it.

Work inside `/app`, leave `/app/data` unmodified, and use the Python standard library
alone, since the system Python carries no third-party package and none is needed. Every
identifier and every value in the corpus is specific to this channel, so the day has to be
derived from the records under `/app/data`. You have 14400 seconds to complete this task.

failed_criteria.justification: The program is substantially decomposed into named functions and classes and contains no obvious debug code, but it does not satisfy the explicit exception-handling standard. It contains multiple broad `except Exception` handlers that silently return, continue, or pass, including parsing and prior/control-loading paths, which can conceal malformed input rather than handling parse errors explicitly.

fired_negatives.justification: The final response claims that the control harness showed every file with `bad=0`, but the actual harness run in step 114 reported `cdn_attestations.xlsx` with `bad=101`. The transform's separate control logic handled sheet reordering successfully, but the specifically claimed all-green harness result was never shown.

instruction:
Corvid Cloud Platform closes its monthly SLA service-credit cycle from the exports in `/app/data`: one hundred files of collector telemetry, synthetic probes, outage and incident registers, maintenance changes, subscriptions, contracts, SLA policy, quotas, claims, treasury rates, ledgers and audit controls, in many formats. Start with `/app/data/source_register.md` (catalog of every file, reading conventions, record and control definitions, close parameters) and `/app/data/governance_charter.docx` (which source wins when sources disagree). The policies those two documents point to define how uptime and credits are computed. Sources disagree, some documents are drafts, snapshots or mirrors, and only the sections the charter designates are authoritative.

Deliver `/app/out/transform.py`, a reusable program, and the outputs it writes for the period named in the source register:

```bash
python3 /app/out/transform.py <DATA_DIR> <OUT_DIR> [--prior <PRIOR_OUT_DIR>]
```

With no arguments it reads `/app/data` and writes `/app/out`. `--prior` points at the output directory of the previous month's close; quarter-to-date state carries forward from it. The transform must also produce exactly the right outputs when it is run unchanged on the next month's exports (same file names and formats, new period in the source register, different records) with `--prior` set to your `/app/out`. It must be deterministic, read only the directories it is given, not depend on their paths or names, use only the standard library plus the parsers installed in the image, and finish within 25 minutes. Do not modify `/app/data`. There is no network.

Outputs (UTF-8, JSON documents with sorted keys and 2-space indent; JSON Lines compact, one object per line):

- `/app/out/normalized.jsonl`: one record per subscription active on at least one day of the period and not excluded, sorted by `subscription_id`, with exactly these fields: `subscription_id`, `account_id` (canonical), `product`, `region`, `region_group`, `segment`, `plan`, `sla_class`, `sla_version` (`v2`..`v5` or `custom`), `target_pct` (string, 3 decimals), `currency`, `fee_minor` (integer minor units), `active_days`, `active_windows`, `suspended_windows`, `maintenance_windows`, `eligible_windows`, `telemetry_windows`, `outage_windows`, `bad_windows`, `attributed_windows` (integers; windows are the five-minute UTC slots of the period; `telemetry_windows` counts the eligible windows that have a used telemetry record and `outage_windows` the eligible windows in which the subscription's product and region are in outage), `bad_window_digest` (first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the ascending zero-based window indices of the bad windows joined by commas), `uptime_pct` (string, 3 decimals, half-even), `credit_pct`, `credit_minor`, `claim_id` (claim identifier, `AUTO`, or null), `claim_filed_utc` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` or null), `fx_rate` (string, 6 decimals, or null), `credit_usd_cents`, `qtd_before_usd_cents`, `cap_usd_cents` (integer or null), `status` (`MET`, `UNCLAIMED`, `CREDITED` or `CAP_EXHAUSTED`).
- `/app/out/summary.json`: `status` (`PUBLISHED`, or `HELD` when the inputs fail the documented controls), `period`, `records`, `excluded`, `status_counts`, `credited_usd_cents`, `credit_minor_by_currency`, `eligible_windows`, `bad_windows`, `attributed_windows`, and `reconciliation` (integer counts: `files` and `records` over all input files, `control_blocks` the blocks checked against controls over all files, `control_failures` the number of files whose controls fail). A held close writes only `status`, `period` and `held_reasons` (sorted list with one `CONTROL_MISMATCH:<file>`, `MISSING:<file>` or `UNREADABLE:<file>` entry per failing file).
- `/app/out/data_quality.json`: `sources` (one entry per input file sorted by `file`: `file`, `records`, `control_blocks` (blocks checked against controls), `control_ok`; the audit control register, which nothing controls, reports `control_blocks` 0 and `control_ok` true, and a missing or unreadable file reports `records` 0, `control_blocks` 0 and `control_ok` false) and `exclusions` (`subscription_id`, `reason` in `UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT`, `INTERNAL_ACCOUNT`, `BETA_PRODUCT_REGION`, `NO_SLA_ENROLLMENT`; sorted by `subscription_id`).
- `/app/out/product_summary.json`: `products` keyed by product with `records`, `eligible_windows`, `bad_windows`, `attributed_windows`, `credited_usd_cents`, `status_counts`.
- `/app/out/region_central.json`, `/app/out/region_east.json`, `/app/out/region_north.json`, `/app/out/region_south.json`, `/app/out/region_west.json`: `region_group`, `records`, `status_counts`, `credited_usd_cents`, and `regions` keyed by region code with `records`, `eligible_windows`, `bad_windows`, `credited_usd_cents`.
- `/app/out/segment_consumer.json`, `/app/out/segment_corporate.json`, `/app/out/segment_enterprise.json`, `/app/out/segment_smb.json`: `segment`, `records`, `status_counts`, `credited_usd_cents`, and `plans` keyed by plan code with `records`, `credited_usd_cents`.

`status_counts` always carries all four status keys. `credited_usd_cents` and `credit_minor_by_currency` total only `CREDITED` records. When held, every other JSON output is `{"status": "HELD"}`, `normalized.jsonl` is empty and `data_quality.json` still lists the sources with empty exclusions.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

failed_criteria.criterion: The agent recomputes the family, total node and memory sums of its cache_plan.csv against the limits of the sheet in force.
failed_criteria.justification: The trajectory checks feasibility using the in-memory assignment and checks family_rollup.json, but it does not explicitly recompute all family, total-node, and memory sums directly from cache_plan.csv against ruleset_used.json.

instruction:
The platform team published the result-cache node plan `/app/data/cache_plan_published.csv` from the saved advisor query pack `/app/data/advisor_query_pack.md`, and the plan is wrong in more places than anyone has listed. Everything needed to redo it is in `/app/data`. The rulebook `/app/data/cache_planning_rulebook.md`, the pricing bulletin and the capacity workbook are the authority over every query, draft, digest, announcement, calendar, cache, hint, dashboard export and the published plan itself; `/app/data/feed_layouts.md` describes the record shapes and `/app/data/output_contract.md` fixes the exact shape, order, number format and rounding of every report. Working out which rules the published run broke, and which shipped files can be trusted, is part of the job.

The finished work is one program, `/app/out/plan_cache.py`, that runs as `python3 /app/out/plan_cache.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, reads a corpus laid out like `/app/data` from whatever directory it is given and writes the reports below into `OUT_DIR` and nothing else; once its last edit is done you run it on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as the output directory, so the files left in `/app/out` are its own output. It will be run again on fresh copies of the corpus placed elsewhere, with other shards, journals, merges, registrations, reservations, adoptions, errata, commitments, windows and profile settings, so every figure has to come out of its input when it runs and nothing may be carried over from the shipped files. A report counts only when it matches the contract exactly, and the core reports (the plan, curves, hourly load, rates, ruleset, commitment rounds, chargeback and plan totals) count only when every one of them is exact on the shipped corpus and on every changed copy at once, so a near miss anywhere earns nothing for the reports built on it.

The plan in `/app/out/cache_plan.csv` gives every candidate pool the node count that reaches the largest total saving the rulebook allows under each family limit, the total node limit and the memory budget, and it must be the plan left after the cluster commitments of the bulletin have been settled. Alongside it go each candidate pool's saving at every allowed node count in `/app/out/pool_curves.psv`; each pool's hourly usage and planning load in `/app/out/pool_hourly.tsv`; the per-hour totals across candidate pools in `/app/out/hourly_rollup.tsv`; the rates in force and the constants applied to each pool in `/app/out/rates_used.csv`; the ruleset sheet in force with its adoption in `/app/out/ruleset_used.json`; the deduplication counters in `/app/out/dedup_report.json`; the per-shard row and kept counts in `/app/out/source_lineage.json`; every posted adjustment, in the order applied, with its outcome in `/app/out/applied_adjustments.jsonl`; the resolution of every merge ledger entry in `/app/out/project_resolution.csv`; the scope of every project of the plan's org in `/app/out/scope_projects.csv`; every excluded in-window query with its reason in `/app/out/excluded_queries.jsonl`; the disposition of every existing reservation in `/app/out/reservation_dispositions.csv`; every pool that is not a candidate, with its reason, in `/app/out/excluded_pools.jsonl`; every cluster closed for missing its commitment, round by round, in `/app/out/cluster_commitments.jsonl`; the family rollup in `/app/out/family_rollup.json`; the cluster rollup in `/app/out/cluster_rollup.xml`; the chargeback of each pool's saving to projects in `/app/out/chargeback.csv`; its team rollup in `/app/out/team_rollup.json`; the plan totals in `/app/out/plan_summary.json`; the per-pool comparison with the published plan in `/app/out/variance_vs_published.csv`; the family reconciliation table in `/app/out/reconciliation.md`; and `/app/out/manifest.json`, listing the other reports with their sizes and SHA-256 digests.

Use only the Python standard library and install nothing. Do not modify, add or delete anything under `/app/data`, and when you finish `/app/out` should hold only the program and the twenty-three files named above, with scratch work kept elsewhere.

Your final message should list each defect you found in the published run with the file, query or rulebook rule that shows it; report the corrected total saving in cents, the total nodes planned and the memory units used; name the ruleset sheet in force with its adoption id and effective date, and the node limit and memory budget it sets; name every cluster closed for its commitment, in order; and name each pricing bulletin erratum you applied and each you did not, with the reason.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

failed_criteria.criterion: The agent executes a canonical-equivalence check on at least two distinct raw forms that SPEC makes equivalent, such as composed versus decomposed Unicode or redundant path segments. Evidence identifies the distinct inputs, the independently justified common canonical expectation, the observed planner results and their comparison; normalising an already canonical value or comparing duplicate outputs alone is insufficient.
failed_criteria.justification: Although the planner implements canonicalization and the corpus contains NFC/NFD and redundant-segment paths, no executed check identifies two distinct equivalent raw inputs, independently derives their common canonical value, and compares both observed planner results to it.

failed_criteria.criterion: The agent executes a checkpoint check that distinguishes an absent committed size from an explicit zero for an extent with positive expected size. Evidence identifies the inputs, the SPEC-derived never_started versus zeroed expectations, and a comparison with observed planner results, rather than treating both inputs as false or merely quoting resume_state statuses.
failed_criteria.justification: The trajectory reports counts and examples of resume statuses, including `zeroed`, but does not execute a focused comparison of a NIL committed value versus numeric zero for positive expected sizes with independently derived `never_started` and `zeroed` expectations.

failed_criteria.criterion: The agent executes a symlink-resolution check on a chain that closes into a cycle, comparing the observed resolution and hop count with an independently traced chain or a separately derived SPEC expectation. Evidence shows the links in the cycle and the expected traversal; copying the planner's own resolution or hop count into the expectation is insufficient.
