# 92dd0b24-4f27-5ec2-9084-7bcc527d2e05

The circuit office needs the open slate adjudicated and recorded. The published corpus sits in `/app/data`, the arbiter service in `/app/service/arbiter.py` and its console in `/app/service/arbiterctl.py`. Start the arbiter against `/app/data/registry_seed.json` before recording anything.

`/app/data/slate_contract.md` is the single source of truth for admission, identity, timing, cards, restrictions, carry and verdicts. `/app/data/api_contract.md` is the single source of truth for the protocol. `/app/data/source_index.md` names every feed with its producer and field order. `/app/data/slate_window.ini` fixes the slate id, the legality cutoff and the precedence cutover, and `/app/data/scenario_brief.ini` fixes the three scenarios. `/app/data/legacy_floor_runbook.md` records older floor practice and `/app/data/rules_committee_notes.md` records later errata; where either disagrees with the two contracts, the contracts govern. Two rules in the slate contract are settled by the adjudication observations and by nothing else in the corpus. Nothing here tells you which feeds carry defects or how many; finding that out is the task.

Write seven files. `/app/out/report.json` holds `slate_id`, `cutoff`, `entry_count` and `entries`, ordered by effective instant, then recorded instant, then submission id, with every entry holding exactly these keys:

```
submission_id player_id format venue effective_at recorded_at verdict
reason_code points_total copy_breach_count carry_before carry_after tier
governing_source channel
```

Instants are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC, `points_total` and the carries are integers, `points_total` is in centipoints, and `reason_code` is JSON null when the verdict carries no reason.

`/app/out/summary.json` holds `slate_id`, `entry_count`, `verdict_counts`, `reason_counts`, `source_counts`, `tier_counts`, `points_total_sum`, `copy_breach_total`, `carry_cap_hits`, `redirected_entries`, `materialized_entry_count`, `distinct_canonical_cards` and `rejected_events`. The four count maps carry one key per value that occurs, and a null reason appears under the key `none`.

`/app/out/transcript_summary.json` holds `slate_id`, `pages_walked`, `empty_pages`, `preseeded_entries`, `deferred_operations`, `conflicts_met`, `conflict_entries`, `console_operations`, `api_operations`, `refusals`, `journal_seq` and `digest`, where `conflict_entries` is sorted, `refusals` maps each refusal code that occurred to its count, and `preseeded_entries` counts the listed entries the slate also names.

`/app/out/final_state.json` is the state snapshot read back from the arbiter once recording is complete, with its keys unchanged.

`/app/out/scenario_alpha.json`, `/app/out/scenario_beta.json` and `/app/out/scenario_mode.json` each hold `basis`, `entry_count`, `verdict_counts`, `tier_counts`, `points_total_sum`, `changed` and `changed_count`, where `basis` is the token from the brief and `changed` is the sorted list of submission ids whose verdict differs from the baseline report, counting a submission id that appears in only one of the two as a difference.

The verdicts are `seated`, `amended`, `flagged`, `barred` and `unresolved`. The reason codes are `charge_cycle`, `chain_cycle`, `unknown_printing`, `no_prior_list`, `tier_bar`, `card_barred`, `copy_breach`, `points_over` and null. The tiers are `clear`, `caution`, `probation` and `barred`. The governing sources are `rider`, `global`, `addendum` and `base`. The formats are `classic`, `singleton` and `relic`. The channels are `api` and `console`. Use no token outside these sets.

Every entry the slate names passes through the arbiter, and a pre-seeded entry the slate does not name stays in the state the seed gave it. Send every operation through the service, take the sequence numbers, the refusal totals and the digest from the service rather than from your own bookkeeping, and leave `/app/data` exactly as shipped. Write nothing at the seven output paths other than those files, and leave no partial file behind on an error path.

An artifact counts only when every value in it is exact, so a near miss earns nothing there.

Close with a message that states, each labelled and each absent from all seven files: how many submissions in the whole season carry no admitted intake receipt; how many submissions are held by an entrant other than the one the handle assignment alone would name; how many deck lines in the governing lists of the admitted submissions name a printing that no admitted registry row matches; how many canonical keys lose their identity to an admitted reprint link in the formats the slate uses, as at the published close of the open stage; how many reprint links the corpus withdraws with the token their recorded instant column carries in place of a date; how many restriction revisions are retracted among those otherwise admitted; how many rider rows that their own instants would otherwise admit are turned away because their authorising judge held too low a rank; how many submissions carry an adjudication observation that disagrees with another observation of the same submission; how many standing occurrences the open stage window admits and how many of those an exception suppresses; how many accepted amendments that the legality cutoff admits are outranked by a higher accepted version of the same submission; and how many submissions fall in no governing stage window. Where one of these counts is over submissions, it covers every submission the feeds name for the season, whether a later event withdrew or superseded it or not. Label each count with the feeds you read it from. State in the same message which two conventions you settled from the observations, which reading you chose for each, and what in the observations settled it.

This machine has no network. Work only from the shipped corpus and the Python standard library, and do no online search for a published solution. You have 12600 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
You are the policy convergence engineer for the offline deterministic policy compiler shipped as `sealb-ctl` inside `/app/data/tool.zip`. Everything you need is on disk under `/app/data/`. The derivation contract is `/app/data/config_contract.md` and it is the sole authority on how the spine, the four zone profiles, the fifty evidence corpora and the delivered byte-shape of every artifact are produced; the broken source archive for the tool itself is `/app/data/tool.zip`. Repair the tool so every subcommand runs, drive the pipeline through it, and deliver the end state below. Use only the Python standard library. You may not pip-install, fetch over the network, synthesise, or hand-write any value: every bit of every artifact must be derived from files already in `/app/data/`.

Deliver all of these artifacts, byte-identical across repeated runs, each at the exact absolute path given:

- `/app/out/config.json` - the finished scalar-flat spine, produced by driving the repaired CLI (not by writing JSON by hand).
- `/app/out/profile_core.json`, `/app/out/profile_edge.json`, `/app/out/profile_dmz.json`, `/app/out/profile_mgmt.json` - the four per-zone scalar-flat profiles.
- `/app/out/aggregates.json` - one derived integer per corpus, keyed by corpus name.
- `/app/out/aggregates.csv`, `/app/out/aggregates.tsv`, `/app/out/aggregates.xml`, `/app/out/aggregates.ini`, `/app/out/aggregates.env`, `/app/out/aggregates.md`, `/app/out/aggregates.txt` - the aggregate map mirrored into each of the seven ancillary formats, corpora in sorted name order; the `.env` keys are the corpus names upper-cased.
- `/app/out/zone_totals.json` - counted-row totals per active zone, aggregated across every corpus.
- `/app/out/corpus_index.json` - a top-level `count` and a `corpora` list, each entry carrying `name`, `format`, `op`, `lo`, `hi`, `eligible_rows` and `value`.
- `/app/out/posture.json` - `aggregate_total`, `corpus_count`, `max_corpus`, `max_value` (ties broken by the earlier corpus name) and `nonzero_corpora`.
- `/app/out/rejected_ops.json` - a `rejected` list of every invalid journal operation and a `count`.
- `/app/out/validation_report.json` - `ok` and `checks` covering `all_artifacts_present`, `config_matches_policy`, `config_scalar_flat`, `command_failures`, `rejected_ops`, per-zone `profiles` (each with `scalar_flat` and `trailer`), `corpus_count` and `aggregate_total`.
- `/app/out/summary.json` - `tool`, `profile_tag`, `trailer`, `profiles`, `artifacts`, `artifact_count`, `inputs` (sorted names of every file under `/app/data/`), `input_count`, `corpus_count` and `aggregate_total`.
- `/app/out/report.json` - emitted by the repaired tool's own CLI as its run record; it carries `ok`, `tool`, `config_path`, `config_sha256` (the sha256 hex of the delivered `/app/out/config.json` bytes), `trailer`, and `commands` (one object per CLI call, each with `argv`, `returncode` and `stdout`). No timestamps or run-dependent fields anywhere.
- `/app/out/tool.zip` - the repaired tool, rebuilt so its sha256 is reproducible across repeated runs on the same inputs.
- `/app/out/manifest.sha256` - one `<sha256>  <name>` line per delivered artifact except `tool.zip`, `report.json`, and `manifest.sha256` itself, names in sorted order.

Honour every rule in `/app/data/config_contract.md`: how the spine is produced from the defaults, schema, validation rules and the journal; how each zone profile folds in `env_overrides.json`; how a journal operation is classified as valid or rejected; which journal operations drive which zone; what makes an evidence row countable; how each corpus's effective upper bound is derived; how each wire format is parsed; how each aggregation operator behaves when no row is counted; and the exact serialisation parameters for every JSON byte, every ZIP byte and the manifest. The contract carries the numeric offsets, the canonical-integer rule, the active zone names, the per-corpus bounds and operators, and the determinism requirements of every output. Nothing in `config_contract.md` is restated here; nothing outside it may be assumed. A manifest produced by `json.dumps(obj)` with default parameters will not match the contract.

The configuration is flat scalars only: no nested dicts or lists in the spine or in any zone profile. The pipeline is offline and deterministic: no network access, no wall-clock timestamps, no random seeds, no reliance on dict insertion order. Running the pipeline twice on the same `/app/data/` must produce byte-identical `/app/out/` artifacts, and every artifact the manifest lists must match the sha256 recorded there.

instruction:
The files in `/app/data` are one monthly extract of the Harbourline PM2.5 monitoring network. The documents shipped with the data govern this work.

Write a program at `/app/out/derive_report.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/derive_report.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, that reads an extract from DATA_DIR and writes its nine reports into OUT_DIR. It will also be run on other extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular month. Each call finishes within 60 seconds. The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR and its own directory, and write nothing outside OUT_DIR. It is self-contained: only the program and its reports are collected from its folder. Use only the Python standard library, make no network connection, and do not replace or patch standard-library modules, `sys.modules` or builtins. Its output must be byte-identical across runs, working directories, extract locations and output directories, and every report must match exactly, byte for byte.

Run it on the shipped extract with OUT_DIR set to `/app/out`, so the reports land at `/app/out/summary.json`, `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json`, `/app/out/region_East.json`, `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and `/app/out/segment_public.json`. Leave the shipped extract in `/app/data` unchanged.

Each what-if below is worked out by rerunning the whole report with exactly the change named, on a copy of the extract; everything else stays as shipped. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its own right.

1. `zone_rules.json` gains a daylight-saving period that begins `2026-01-19T02:00` and ends `2026-01-26T02:00` with a 60-minute shift. Give the sum of the daily values of all sites on the days 2026-01-19 to 2026-01-25.
2. Every receipt journal row recording the packet sent for a card row of unit AQ896 stamped `2026-01-20T01:15` or later is moved 30 minutes later, keeping its channel and frame. Give the sum of the daily values of site S2.
3. Every receipt journal row recording the packet sent for a card row of unit AQ896 stamped from `2026-01-10T00:15` up to but not including `2026-01-13T01:00` is moved 12 minutes later, and likewise for unit AQ246 from `2026-01-07T00:00` up to but not including `2026-01-10T00:00` (12 minutes later), unit AQ785 from `2026-01-06T00:00` up to but not including `2026-01-09T00:00` (14 minutes earlier) and unit AQ363 from `2026-01-25T00:00` up to but not including `2026-01-28T00:30` (14 minutes earlier), each row keeping its channel and frame. Give the number of pairs of a site and a day that are an exceedance day in exactly one of the two runs, this one and the shipped one.
4. In `unit_deployments.csv`, unit AQ896 is removed from site S2 at `2026-01-20T12:00` and installed at site S6 at that instant, and unit AQ680 is removed from site S6 at that instant; also, every receipt journal row recording the packet sent for a card row of unit AQ896 stamped `2026-01-20T14:45` or later is moved 20 minutes later, keeping its channel and frame. Give the valid readings of the East district rollup.
5. Every set entry for unit AQ634 in `span_register.csv` is given one common span factor, written with three decimals as the register writes them. Give the largest such factor at which site S4 is still in attainment.
6. Every receipt journal row recording the packet sent for a card row of unit AQ363 stamped from `2026-01-24T00:00` up to but not including `2026-01-28T00:30` is moved 14 minutes earlier, keeping its channel and frame. Give the design value of site S5.
7. Every receipt journal row recording the packet sent for a card row of unit AQ680 stamped `2026-01-15T00:00` or later is moved 15 minutes later, keeping its channel and frame. Give the sum of the daily values of site S6.

instruction:
The storage team has to restore the projects share after the ransomware incident, and the tool that should tell them what to restore, from which backup sets and from which media, is broken. The tool is the `restorekit` project shipped as `/app/data/project.zip`. It no longer installs on Python 3.12, and the plan it produced before it broke was rejected because it did not follow the restore specification. Repair the project and plan the restore with it.

Everything the restore depends on is in `/app/data/`: the restore request, the backup catalog parts, job history, server logs, registers, notices and the documents that govern them. The rules are those of the restore specification revision in force together with the documents it incorporates. Where the shipped code, a file's name or a file's own description disagrees with those rules, the rules win. Leave `/app/data/` unchanged.

Deliver:

- `/app/out/package.zip`: the repaired project as an installable src-layout package with its `pyproject.toml`, `src/restorekit` and the project's own test suite, kept unchanged and passing. It must run as `python -m restorekit restore --feed DIR --out DIR` with `src` on the path, for any restore feed laid out like `/app/data`, and write the five files below into the `--out` directory. It must identify feed files by their content, never by file name, read nothing but the feed directory it is given and its own files, and produce identical bytes on every run. A normal restore run writes nothing to the console. It is installed and run on a plain Python 3.12 that has setuptools and only these distributions: openpyxl 3.1.5, pyarrow 18.1.0, pypdf 5.1.0, PyYAML 6.0.3 and tzdata 2025.2.
- The restore plan for `/app/data`: `/app/out/restore_manifest.csv`, `/app/out/exclusions.csv`, `/app/out/media_pull_list.csv`, `/app/out/restore_chain.json` and `/app/out/reconciliation.json`, in the formats of section 11 of the specification. These five files must be written by your repaired package itself, run with `--feed /app/data --out /app/out`; do not write, copy or edit them with anything else.

Each deliverable is accepted only as an exact match of the specified content: every row, every field, the order and the custody trailer. A plan that is right on most rows is still wrong. Your package is also run on another restore feed with the same structure, for a different share, and its output there must be exact as well.

When you finish, list in your final message the restore rule corrections you made to the shipped project.

instruction:
The cryostat qualification team published the KTC-26B heat-load budget `/app/data/heatload_budget_published.csv` and stage margins `/app/data/stage_margins_published.json`, both produced by the saved solve pack `/app/data/budget_solve_pack.md`, and the budget is wrong in ways that reach sensor temperatures, link heat flows, intercept temperatures, stage loads and verdicts. Everything needed to redo it from the raw DAQ readings is in `/app/data`. The governance memo, the cryogenic property workbook, the campaign profile and `/app/data/thermal_budget_handbook.md` govern over the solve pack, the published files, caches, dashboards, bulletins, drafts, quick references, legacy files and stale overlays; `/app/data/feed_layouts.md` describes the record shapes and `/app/data/output_contract.md` fixes the columns, keys, order, vocabularies and number formats of every report. Working out which rules the published run broke and which shipped files can be trusted is part of the job.

The finished work is one program, `/app/out/run_budget.py`, which runs as `python3 /app/out/run_budget.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, reads a corpus laid out like `/app/data` from whatever directory it is given and writes into `OUT_DIR` the reports named below and nothing else; after its last edit you run it once on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as the output directory, so the files left in `/app/out` are its own output. It is run again later on fresh copies of the corpus placed elsewhere, with other runs, sensors, registers, memo tables, workbook sheets, profile knobs, site calendars, amendment journals and rulings, so every figure must come out of the input at run time and nothing may be carried over from the shipped files. Each of those runs must finish within 600 seconds. A report counts only when it matches exactly, and the stage temperature, intercept, link heat flow, stage load, cooler margin and run verdict reports count only when all of them are exact on the shipped corpus and on every changed copy at once, so a near miss there earns nothing for the reports built on them, and a changed copy counts only when every report written for it is exact.

The reports are the per-run sensor means in `/app/out/sensor_means.tsv`; the stage temperatures in `/app/out/stage_temperatures.csv`; every floating intercept node's settled temperature and heat balance in `/app/out/intercept_solutions.json`; every installed link's heat flow in `/app/out/link_heat_flows.psv` with its element-by-element junction temperatures in `/app/out/junction_profiles.jsonl`; the resolved segment geometry in `/app/out/link_geometry.csv` and joint conductances in `/app/out/joint_conductances.tsv`; the stage loads in `/app/out/stage_loads.csv`; the cooler capacities, reserves, margins and stage verdicts in `/app/out/cooler_margins.xml`; the run verdicts in `/app/out/run_verdicts.json`; the material, node, link and sensor token resolutions in `/app/out/alias_resolution.csv`; every reading exclusion count in `/app/out/reading_exclusions.jsonl`; the revision and void counters in `/app/out/dedup_report.json` and per-shard counts in `/app/out/source_lineage.json`; every amendment with its settled state in `/app/out/amendment_ledger.csv`; the governing sheets, memo tables, constants and per-run settings applied in `/app/out/parameters_used.yaml`; the audit of every value quoted by a lower-authority source in `/app/out/authority_audit.csv`; the link-by-link comparison with the published budget in `/app/out/variance_vs_published.csv`, the verdict comparison with the published margins in `/app/out/reconciliation.md` and the campaign table in `/app/out/budget_summary.md`; and `/app/out/manifest.json`, listing the other reports in contract order with their sizes and SHA-256 digests.

Use only the Python standard library and install nothing. Do not modify, add or delete anything under `/app/data`, and when you finish `/app/out` should hold only the program and the twenty-one files named above, with scratch work kept elsewhere.

Your final message should list each defect you found in the published run with the solve-pack step or handbook rule that shows it.

instruction:
You are the policy convergence engineer for the offline security policy compiler installed as sealb-ctl. The source archive `/app/data/tool.zip` ships a broken stdlib-only CLI. The written derivation contract lives in `/app/data/config_contract.md`, and `/app/data/config_schema.json`, `/app/data/defaults.json`, `/app/data/env_overrides.json`, `/app/data/validation_rules.json`, and `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` complete the spine. The fifty evidence corpora `/app/data/c01_cve_severity.csv` through `/app/data/c50_oauth_scopes.bang` carry the rows. Every bit of every delivered artifact must be derived from these files; nothing may be invented, networked, or hand-written. Use only the Python standard library.

Satisfy every one of these requirements:

1. Extract `/app/data/tool.zip` safely to `/app/tool` and repair the broken CLI so every subcommand runs offline.
2. Replay `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` strictly in ascending `seq` order; the file is intentionally out of order.
3. Classify each journal operation against `/app/data/validation_rules.json`; a `set` on an integer spine key must carry a JSON integer value inside its `bounds`, not a JSON string of digits.
4. Treat a valid `unset` as a restore to the `defaults.json` value for that key; last-set-wins while ignoring `unset` is wrong.
5. Generate the base spine as `/app/out/config.json` by driving the repaired CLI (init / set / validate), not by hand-writing JSON.
6. Produce the four zone profiles at `/app/out/profile_core.json`, `/app/out/profile_edge.json`, `/app/out/profile_dmz.json`, `/app/out/profile_mgmt.json` by starting from the finished spine, applying `/app/data/env_overrides.json` deltas, and replaying only that zone's valid journal operations.
7. Reduce the fifty corpora into `/app/out/aggregates.json`; the effective upper bound of every corpus is `hi + (R mod 97) + (J mod 31)`, where R is the finished-spine `rekey_interval_s` and J is the rejected-ops count. The two shifts are co-prime (97, 31), so a misclassified journal op can shift the aggregate of any corpus whose eligible rows sit near the shifted bound.
8. Count a row only when its `zone` is byte-exactly one of `core`, `edge`, `dmz`, `mgmt`, its `flag` is byte-exactly `active`, and `str(int(value)) == value` on the raw field bytes. Reject `-0`, `-00`, `-000`, leading zeros, leading `+`, surrounding spaces, underscores, hex, floats, units, words, scientific notation, and every non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari U+0966..U+096F, Arabic-Indic U+0660..U+0669, Gujarati U+0AE6..U+0AEF, full-width U+FF10..U+FF19).
9. Mirror aggregates into `/app/out/aggregates.csv`, `/app/out/aggregates.tsv`, `/app/out/aggregates.xml`, `/app/out/aggregates.ini`, `/app/out/aggregates.env`, `/app/out/aggregates.md`, and `/app/out/aggregates.txt`, corpora in sorted name order; `.env` keys upper-cased.
10. Emit `/app/out/zone_totals.json` with the counted-row total per active zone across every corpus.
11. Emit `/app/out/corpus_index.json` with `count` and a `corpora` list carrying `name`, `format`, `op`, `lo`, `hi`, `eligible_rows`, and `value`.
12. Emit `/app/out/posture.json` with `aggregate_total`, `corpus_count`, `max_corpus`, `max_value` (ties broken by the earlier name), and `nonzero_corpora`.
13. Emit `/app/out/rejected_ops.json` with `rejected` (the ascending `seq` list of every invalid journal operation) and `count`.
14. Emit `/app/out/validation_report.json` with `ok` and `checks` covering `all_artifacts_present`, `config_matches_policy`, `config_scalar_flat`, `command_failures`, `rejected_ops`, per-zone `profiles` (`scalar_flat`, `trailer`), `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`.
15. Emit `/app/out/summary.json` with `tool`, `profile_tag`, `trailer`, `profiles`, `artifacts`, `artifact_count`, `inputs` (sorted names of every file under `/app/data`), `input_count`, `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`.
16. Emit `/app/out/report.json` through the repaired tool's `export-report` subcommand with `ok`, `tool`, `config_path`, `config_sha256` (sha256 hex of `/app/out/config.json` bytes), `trailer`, and `commands` (one object per CLI call, each with `argv`, `returncode`, `stdout`). No timestamps or run-dependent fields.
17. Rebuild the repaired tool deterministically as `/app/out/tool.zip` (ZIP_STORED, fixed epoch, fixed external_attr, sorted member order) so its sha256 is reproducible across runs.
18. Emit `/app/out/manifest.sha256`: one `<sha256>  <name>` line per delivered JSON artifact except `report.json`, names in sorted order, two spaces between.
19. Every JSON artifact is written with these exact parameters: UTF-8, `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, indent=2, separators=(",", ": "), ensure_ascii=False)`, plus a single trailing `\n`. Default `json.dumps(obj)` breaks the manifest.
20. The configuration must stay flat scalars only; no nested dicts or lists in `/app/out/config.json` or in any profile.
21. Keep the workflow deterministic and offline: no network, no wall-clock timestamps, no random seeds, no reliance on dict insertion order. Running the pipeline twice must produce byte-identical artifacts.

instruction:
Northbeam Payments' ML platform team needs training-set release TR-2026.09 of the Sentinel card-fraud model built from the exports under `/app/data`, together with a reusable builder that the platform will run again for the next release. Start with `/app/data/source_register.md`, which catalogs every delivered file and maps every column, and `/app/data/release_build_specification.docx`, which defines the build, the publication gate and the exact content of every output. The policies, standards, handbooks, registers and logs that the specification and the register point to are part of the same contract. Sources disagree in places; the governance charter and the topical policies decide which source governs, and some files that look authoritative are not.

Deliver the builder at `/app/out/transform.py`:

```bash
python3 /app/out/transform.py <DATA_DIR> <OUT_DIR> [--prior <PRIOR_OUT_DIR>]
```

Run it on `/app/data` to produce this release's outputs in `/app/out`:

- `/app/out/normalized.jsonl` - the released examples of every split
- `/app/out/product_summary.json` - the release state: fitted preprocessing, vocabularies, class weights, drift reference and account clusters
- `/app/out/summary.json` - split counts, baseline AUC, drift and imputation counts
- `/app/out/data_quality.json` - the release status, the per-file reconciliation and every excluded candidate record with its reason
- `/app/out/region_central.json`, `/app/out/region_east.json`, `/app/out/region_north.json`, `/app/out/region_south.json` and `/app/out/region_west.json` - evaluation slices by region group
- `/app/out/segment_consumer.json`, `/app/out/segment_corporate.json`, `/app/out/segment_enterprise.json` and `/app/out/segment_smb.json` - evaluation slices by segment group

Formats, key names, list order and rounding are defined by the specification and must be followed exactly; every value is compared exactly.

The platform will run your `/app/out/transform.py`, unchanged, on the next release's exports as a delta release, with `--prior` pointing at a copy of your `/app/out`, and compare its outputs with the expected ones. The builder must be deterministic, must read only the directories named on its command line, must not depend on where those directories are, and must finish one release within 25 minutes. It may use the Python standard library and the parsing libraries already installed in this environment.

Do not modify anything under `/app/data`. The environment has no network access; install nothing.

When you are done, tell us the release status and how many examples each split (train, val, test and oot) released.

instruction:
You are the policy convergence engineer for an offline security policy compiler shipped as `sealb-ctl`. The source archive `/app/data/tool.zip` carries the broken stdlib-only CLI you must repair and then drive. The written derivation contract is `/app/data/config_contract.md`, and `/app/data/config_schema.json`, `/app/data/defaults.json`, `/app/data/env_overrides.json`, `/app/data/validation_rules.json`, and `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` complete the spine. The fifty evidence corpora `/app/data/c01_cve_severity.csv` through `/app/data/c50_oauth_scopes.bang` carry the rows. Every bit of every delivered artifact must be derived from these files; nothing may be invented, networked, or hand-written. Use only the Python standard library and the repaired `sealb-ctl`. No network, no wall-clock timestamps, no random seeds, no reliance on dict insertion order; two identical runs must emit byte-identical artifacts.

The derivation rules -- how to interpret the journal, what makes a journal operation valid, what makes an evidence row eligible, how zone profiles are built, and how corpus aggregates are shaped -- live in `/app/data/config_contract.md` and `/app/data/validation_rules.json`. Treat those files as the ground truth. Do not add rules the data does not state and do not drop rules the data states, even when a rule looks like a formatting quirk; a single wrong classification is observable across many of the fifty aggregates, so there is no slack to absorb a near-miss.

Goal. Produce exactly these artifacts under `/app/out`, written through the repaired `sealb-ctl` (not by hand-writing JSON), with the content and shape stated below:

1. `/app/out/config.json` -- the finished flat spine configuration. Keys are the ten `required_keys` of `config_schema.json`; values are scalars only (no nested dicts or lists). The four integer spine keys and `mode` carry the state left behind by the journal; `profile`, `producer`, `container`, `trailer` and `checksum` carry the values the contract and schema prescribe.
2. `/app/out/profile_core.json`, `/app/out/profile_edge.json`, `/app/out/profile_dmz.json`, `/app/out/profile_mgmt.json` -- one flat-scalar profile per active zone, built as the contract prescribes from the finished spine, `env_overrides.json`, and that zone's journal operations.
3. `/app/out/aggregates.json` -- a JSON object mapping each corpus's base name (without extension) to its single derived integer. Corpora listed by sorted name order on serialization.
4. `/app/out/aggregates.csv`, `/app/out/aggregates.tsv`, `/app/out/aggregates.xml`, `/app/out/aggregates.ini`, `/app/out/aggregates.env`, `/app/out/aggregates.md`, `/app/out/aggregates.txt` -- the same corpus->value map re-expressed in each format, corpora in sorted name order. Field names for the two-column tabular formats (`.csv`, `.tsv`, `.md`, `.txt`) are the pair `name`, `value`. INI uses a single `[aggregates]` section with corpus names as keys. XML uses a `<rows>` root with one `<row name="..." value="..."/>` per corpus. `.env` keys are the corpus names upper-cased. Every integer value is written in canonical base-10 decimal (no leading `+`, no leading zeros except the single `0`).
5. `/app/out/zone_totals.json` -- an object keyed by active zone (`core`, `edge`, `dmz`, `mgmt`) whose values are the integer count of eligible rows for that zone summed across all fifty corpora.
6. `/app/out/corpus_index.json` -- `{"count": <int>, "corpora": [...]}` with one object per corpus in sorted name order, each carrying exactly these fields: `name`, `format`, `op`, `lo`, `hi`, `eligible_rows`, `value`. `lo` and `hi` are the published bounds from `validation_rules.json` (not the effective upper bound used during eligibility).
7. `/app/out/posture.json` -- `{"aggregate_total": <int>, "corpus_count": <int>, "max_corpus": <str>, "max_value": <int>, "nonzero_corpora": <int>}`. `aggregate_total` is the sum of every corpus's derived value; `max_corpus` / `max_value` are the corpus with the greatest derived value with ties broken by the earlier sorted name; `nonzero_corpora` counts corpora whose derived value is not `0`.
8. `/app/out/rejected_ops.json` -- `{"rejected": [<int>, ...], "count": <int>}`. `rejected` is the sorted ascending list of `seq` values of every invalid journal operation, with no duplicates and no gaps relative to the journal.
9. `/app/out/validation_report.json` -- `{"ok": <bool>, "checks": {...}}` whose `checks` object carries at minimum `all_artifacts_present`, `config_matches_policy`, `config_scalar_flat`, `command_failures`, `rejected_ops`, `profiles` (an object keyed by zone with `scalar_flat` and `trailer`), `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`. `ok` is `true` only when every nested check is `true` and every integer check matches the other artifacts byte-for-byte.
10. `/app/out/summary.json` -- carries at minimum `tool`, `profile_tag`, `trailer`, `profiles`, `artifacts` (the sorted name list of files under `/app/out`), `artifact_count`, `inputs` (the sorted name list of files under `/app/data`), `input_count`, `corpus_count`, `aggregate_total`.
11. `/app/out/report.json` -- emitted by the repaired tool's `export-report` subcommand. Carries `ok`, `tool`, `config_path`, `config_sha256` (sha256 hex of the delivered `/app/out/config.json` bytes), `trailer`, and `commands` (one object per `sealb-ctl` invocation you made, each with `argv`, `returncode`, `stdout`, in call order). No timestamps, no run-dependent fields, no fields beyond those listed here.
12. `/app/out/tool.zip` -- the repaired tool, rebuilt deterministically from `/app/tool` so that two runs produce byte-identical bytes (ZIP_STORED, fixed epoch, fixed external_attr, sorted member order).
13. `/app/out/manifest.sha256` -- one line per delivered JSON artifact **except** `/app/out/report.json`, each line is the 64-character lowercase sha256 hex of the artifact bytes, then exactly two ASCII space characters (0x20 0x20), then the artifact basename; names in sorted order, and a single trailing `\n`.

Every JSON artifact (every file in the list above whose extension is `.json`) must be serialized with these exact `json.dumps` parameters: `sort_keys=True, indent=2, separators=(",", ": "), ensure_ascii=False`, encoded UTF-8, with a single trailing `\n` newline. Any other serialization -- default separators, missing `sort_keys`, extra trailing whitespace, BOM, CRLF, non-UTF-8 -- breaks `/app/out/manifest.sha256` even when the parsed JSON looks right.

Final-state invariants that your `/app/out/validation_report.json` must declare and your artifacts must actually satisfy:

- Every artifact listed above is present under `/app/out`; no additional files are left behind under `/app/out` that are not listed above.
- `/app/out/config.json` is flat (no nested dicts or lists) and matches, key-for-key, the state the contract requires.
- Every profile is flat and carries the per-zone `trailer` the contract prescribes.
- `rejected_ops.json["count"]` equals the number of entries in `rejected_ops.json["rejected"]`, equals the number of journal entries the contract classifies invalid, and feeds into the aggregate computation per the contract.
- `aggregate_total` in `/app/out/posture.json`, `/app/out/summary.json` and `/app/out/validation_report.json` are the same integer and equal the sum of `/app/out/aggregates.json` values.
- `corpus_count` in `/app/out/corpus_index.json`, `/app/out/posture.json`, `/app/out/summary.json` and `/app/out/validation_report.json` are the same integer and equal 50.
- The `aggregates.*` mirror files encode the same corpus->value map as `/app/out/aggregates.json`, in the same sorted name order, with the field names and casing stated above.
- `/app/out/manifest.sha256` hashes the exact on-disk bytes of each listed JSON artifact after serialization.
- No `sealb-ctl` invocation exits non-zero; `command_failures` in `/app/out/validation_report.json` is `0`.

Do not assume any numeric constant, bound shift, offset, canonical-digit rule, byte-exactness rule, replay-order rule or restore-on-unset rule from this instruction alone -- they are stated in `/app/data/config_contract.md` and `/app/data/validation_rules.json`, and that is where to read them. A pipeline that keeps only the last `set` and ignores `unset`, or that uses the published `hi` instead of the effective upper bound, or that treats non-ASCII decimal digits as valid integers, will produce an answer that *looks* finished and still fails many of the fifty aggregates.

Reconcile the telemetry extract in `/app/data` under its Markdown contracts.
Deliver a reusable Python program at `/app/out/derive_report.py`, invoked as
`python3 /app/out/derive_report.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`. It must also work on other
extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular extract.
Each call finishes within 60 seconds, including on the ranges stated in schema.md.

Run the program on the supplied extract. Write the whole report to
`/app/out/summary.json`, the clock audit to `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, the
amendment history to `/app/out/data_quality.json`, the regional reports to
`/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`,
`/app/out/region_West.json`, `/app/out/region_East.json`, and the account and
eligibility views to `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and
`/app/out/segment_public.json`. Every report follows the documents' layout and
byte form exactly. The program and reports must be regular files rather than
symbolic links. Outputs must be byte-identical across repeated calls and
different working directories, input paths and output paths.

The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR, OUT_DIR
and its own directory except the Python interpreter and standard library, and write
nothing outside OUT_DIR. Use only the Python standard library, and open no
network connection. Do not attempt to open files outside the allowed read locations.
Do not attempt filesystem writes outside OUT_DIR. Do not import ctypes or
_ctypes, or use native foreign-function interfaces.
Do not call os._exit.
The program launches no child processes. Preserve inherited
audit descriptors and audit hooks, including allowing audit finalizers to run.
When the evidence in an extract fits no assignment, or fits
more than one, the program stops with an error before writing any report.
Leave the supplied /app/data unchanged.

Answer these eight questions in your final message. Each question is independent.
For every question, start with a fresh copy of the supplied extract and remove
every atom whose identifier starts `seal-` from the atoms cells of both
allocation_groups.csv and allocation_candidates.csv. Then apply only the
numbered edit below. The removal and numbered edit together are that question's
complete stated change. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its
own right. Each answer is worked out by rerunning the whole pipeline with exactly
the change named, on that copy.

1. Add 17 to stamp for events whose integer event identifier is even. What is
   policy_audit.json weighted_state?
2. For every clock_residues.csv row, add three times the coefficient of S00 in
   its equation, reducing the result modulo 41. Leave all other cells unchanged.
   What is region_North.json final_state?
3. Replace every cycles.csv rounds cell with 999999999999999963. What is
   segment_public.json settlement?
4. Negate the quantity for stream-00 in cycles.csv. What is region_South.json total?
5. Replace revision with -1 in fold_corrections.csv rows whose integer amendment
   identifier is divisible by seven. What is region_West.json weighted_states?
6. Remove fold_records.csv rows whose integer position is divisible by seven.
   What is region_West.json weighted_states?
7. Triple quantity in allocation_requests.csv rows whose integer request
   identifier is divisible by five. What is segment_commercial.json weighted_credit?
8. Add 30 to value in allocation_candidates.csv rows whose atoms set contains
   p00. What is region_East.json total?

State the eight answers by question number and the number of required JSON
reports in the supplied extract's output set. For each check or run you describe,
state its observed size, reporting
only checks and runs you actually performed. Read back each artifact before
describing its contents. Keep checks of the changed copies separate from the
supplied extract.

instruction:
# Hollowbrand relay cycle RC-2411

You are the release operator for the Hollowbrand package relay. A promotion cycle has to be closed
and nobody wrote down which source wins when two of them disagree.

Every piece of evidence sits in `/app/data`. It holds fifty three files: specification documents, a
configuration layer, and the record tables those documents name. Where a document leaves an instant
or a revision comparison open, `/app/data/boundary_semantics.json` settles it. Begin at
`/app/data/data_index_spec.md`, which names every other file and says what each one governs. The
relay itself sits in `/app/service`. Read those modules before you call them. They are the authority
on what the relay accepts and they stay exactly as shipped, as does everything in `/app/data`.

Settle the whole cycle first. Only then open the first call to the relay.

Each promotion request that governs inside the cycle horizon receives one decision and one reason
code drawn from `/app/data/reason_code_registry.json`. The decision words come from the governance
document. When more than one gate fires for a single request, the registry `order` field settles
which code is reported. A request whose identifier appears more than once contributes once.
Requests whose submission falls outside the horizon contribute nowhere.

Start the relay, apply the admitted promotions through it, and close every channel on the ladder in
ladder order inside one final call that carries nothing else. Fill each earlier call to the
operation limit the operations runbook defines before you open another, and let exactly one call
repeat an earlier identity key so the relay replays its stored answer. Reach the relay on the
loopback port the runbook names, under the actor name it gives. One refused operation costs the
whole call, so no call may be aborted and no operation may be refused.

Write these seven files and nothing else into `/app/out`, each a JSON object:

```
/app/out/report.json
/app/out/summary.json
/app/out/transcript_summary.json
/app/out/final_state.json
/app/out/scenario_alpha.json
/app/out/scenario_beta.json
/app/out/scenario_mode.json
```

`/app/data/artifact_contract_spec.md` fixes the key sets, the field names, the value forms, the row
ordering and the indent for all seven. `/app/data/metrics_definitions_spec.md` fixes the rounding,
the place counts, the share distribution and the digest width for every figure in the summary.
`/app/data/scenario_definitions_spec.md` fixes what the two scenario files and the two comparison
modes change and what they leave alone. Follow those three documents to the letter: an artifact
counts only when every value in it is exact, and a single wrong figure costs that artifact.

`final_state.json` carries the state the relay reports after the last call, not a state you compose
yourself. `report.json` carries the full decision roster and the order in which the admissions were
applied. `transcript_summary.json` carries the call accounting for the session. `summary.json`
carries the cycle totals and metrics, the cover held for rollback across the ladder among them,
together with the depth the revalidation reached. The three scenario files carry the comparison runs.

Beyond the single apply address the artifact contract asks for by name, no artifact may hold a clock
reading, a host name, a file path, a duration, or any other field that would differ on a second run
of the same work. Run the work twice and expect the same bytes.

Close with a message to the operator that reports ten counts the artifacts do not carry. The scope
of three of the counts below is fixed in `/app/data/boundary_semantics.json`.

First, for the edge channel, the seats drawn from the tier one reserve, the seats drawn from the tier
two reserve, the seats drawn from the general pool, and the total seats that channel offered before
revalidation. Second, the same four figures for the canary channel. Third, the seats drawn from each
of the three pools for the staging channel, and the seats offered anywhere on the stable channel.
Fourth, the bound pairs that drew rollback cover in each of the four channels. Fifth, the size of one
rollback hold in each of the four channels. Sixth, the tier two reserve each of the four channels
still held once the cycle settled. Seventh, the general pool each of the four channels still held
once the cycle settled. Eighth, the tier one reserve each of the four channels still held once the
cycle settled. Ninth, the requests refused for want of room to cover them both ways, the requests
refused because the pool they reached was empty, and how the first of those two figures splits
between the canary and the staging channels. Tenth, the holders taken out by the first revalidation
pass, by the second, by the third, and across the whole cycle.

In that same message, say where each figure came from, name any quantity you left unsettled, and
keep it apart from the figures you derived in full.

Work only from what sits under `/app`. Do not look up a solution online and do not consult any
source beyond the loopback relay and the files shipped with this task. Python 3.12 and its standard
library are installed; nothing else is available and nothing can be installed.

You have 10800 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
You hold the allocation desk of a foundry group with four fabrication sites named North, South, West and East. Twenty four allocation cycles, C01 through C24, span 2031. Demand for wafer starts runs ahead of what the sites can start, so each cycle has to be apportioned. Your evidence is the flat corpus in `/app/data`: order book extracts, a contract registry, a legacy intake stream, state events, amendment notices, approval logs, entitlement ceilings, commitment agreements, capacity declarations, substitution factors, clock marks, customer master records and two settlement observation logs. The documents ending in `.md` together with `derivation_policy.ini`, `unit_declarations.ini`, `source_declarations.properties` and `reason_codes.json` are the contract, and the contract is the single source of truth. Read `corpus_index.md` first, since it names every file. One document declares itself withdrawn: it records an older desk practice and it governs nothing you deliver.

Build `/app/out/derive_report.py`. It accepts `--data <dir>` and `--out <dir>`, reads only the corpus handed to it, and writes nine documents: `/app/out/summary.json`, `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/region_North.json`, `/app/out/region_South.json`, `/app/out/region_West.json`, `/app/out/region_East.json`, `/app/out/segment_commercial.json` and `/app/out/segment_public.json`. Run it over `/app/data` so those nine documents are in place when you stop. Your program will also be run against extracts of this corpus that nobody has seen, at other scales and with other declarations in force, so each rule has to be read from the corpus at run time rather than from a value you noticed once. The Python standard library is all you get and there is no network.

`output_contract.md` fixes every key, every ordering and every spelling, and `reason_codes.json` fixes the closed vocabularies; both bind to the letter. Each region document carries the twenty four cycles of its site and one ledger row for each request that reaches that site inside the horizon, ordered by cycle, then by canonical customer identity, then by reported reference. Every figure is a whole number of wafer equivalents and exact equality is the bar, so a figure that is merely close is wrong. Canonical identities read like `CUS-0412#2`. Each ledger row carries one outcome and exactly one reason, picked by the precedence that `reason_codes.json` declares. Requests outside the horizon and requests whose customer cannot be resolved belong in the out of scope list of their region document rather than in the ledger, while a request that is inside the horizon and cannot claim still keeps its ledger row. `policy_audit.json` records how often each rule fired across the horizon, `data_quality.json` records what each source declared, what parsed and what was admitted, `summary.json` ties the regions and the segments together, and the two segment documents roll the ledger up by segment. Nobody recorded how many records disagree with each other, so there is no count to check yourself against.

Work the evidence in the order the contract sets out, because each later question stands on the earlier answers: which records are admitted at all, then which customer and epoch each record belongs to, then which records describe one and the same request, then which source governs each field, then which notices and events take effect, then what each request may claim, then what each site can start, and only then the apportionment itself. Two rules are deliberately absent from the contract. The settlement logs settle them, and `policy_audit.json` is where you report the reading you settled on, spelled exactly as the rule documents require. A reading that fits only some of the observations is the wrong reading. Where two rules could both apply to one record the contract says which one wins, so follow it rather than your own habit, and apply each rule no more widely than it is written, since reaching too far costs as much as stopping too short. Treat the corpus as read only, add nothing to the output directory beyond the nine documents and the program, and make a second run over the same input produce the same bytes.

Close by telling me, in your final message, eight quantities that none of the nine documents contains, each of them two exact whole numbers. First, had carried shortfall been ignored entirely, the total granted wafer equivalents across the horizon and the number of ledger rows whose outcome would change. Second, under the rival reading of the withheld source rule that every settled observation contradicts, the number of requests whose governing quantity would differ and the resulting total granted wafer equivalents. Third, with the settled survival age extended by one cycle, the number of shortfall lots that would expire and the total running shortfall at the end of C24. Fourth, with the clearing rule never applied, the total running shortfall at the end of C24 and the number of ledger rows whose grant would differ. Fifth, the total wafer equivalents handed out by the indivisible remainder step and the number of site cycles where it handed out at least one. Sixth, if the admission instant were lifted for every file, how many of the requests whose every source row was recorded after it would then claim, and the total they would claim. Seventh, had the notices that lack endorsement been applied anyway, the number of requests whose governing quantity would differ and the number of site cycles whose fill level would differ. Eighth, under the withdrawn document's pro rata practice, the total granted wafer equivalents and the number of ledger rows whose grant would differ. State each as a plain integer, name the quantity it answers, and say which evidence settled each of the two absent rules.

instruction:
You are the policy convergence engineer for the offline security policy compiler installed as sealb-ctl. The source archive `/app/data/tool.zip` ships a broken stdlib-only CLI. The written derivation contract lives in `/app/data/config_contract.md`, and `/app/data/config_schema.json`, `/app/data/defaults.json`, `/app/data/env_overrides.json`, `/app/data/validation_rules.json`, and `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` complete the spine. The fifty evidence corpora `/app/data/c01_cve_severity.csv` through `/app/data/c50_oauth_scopes.bang` carry the rows. Every bit of every delivered artifact must be derived from these files; nothing may be invented, networked, or hand-written. Use only the Python standard library.

Satisfy every one of these requirements:

1. Extract `/app/data/tool.zip` safely to `/app/tool` and repair the broken CLI so every subcommand runs offline.
2. Replay `/app/data/change_journal.jsonl` strictly in ascending `seq` order; the file is intentionally out of order.
3. Classify each journal operation against `/app/data/validation_rules.json`; a `set` on an integer spine key must carry a JSON integer value inside its `bounds`, not a JSON string of digits.
4. Treat a valid `unset` as a restore to the `defaults.json` value for that key; last-set-wins while ignoring `unset` is wrong.
5. Generate the base spine as `/app/out/config.json` by driving the repaired CLI (init / set / validate), not by hand-writing JSON.
6. Produce the four zone profiles at `/app/out/profile_core.json`, `/app/out/profile_edge.json`, `/app/out/profile_dmz.json`, `/app/out/profile_mgmt.json` by starting from the finished spine, applying `/app/data/env_overrides.json` deltas, and replaying only that zone's valid journal operations.
7. Reduce the fifty corpora into `/app/out/aggregates.json`; the effective upper bound of every corpus is `hi + (R mod 97) + (J mod 31)`, where R is the finished-spine `rekey_interval_s` and J is the rejected-ops count. The two shifts are co-prime (97, 31), so R and J cannot cancel each other and a misclassified journal op moves the effective bound of every corpus.
8. Count a row only when its `zone` is byte-exactly one of `core`, `edge`, `dmz`, `mgmt`, its `flag` is byte-exactly `active`, and `str(int(value)) == value` on the raw field bytes. Reject `-0`, `-00`, `-000`, leading zeros, leading `+`, surrounding spaces, underscores, hex, floats, units, words, scientific notation, and every non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari U+0966..U+096F, Arabic-Indic U+0660..U+0669, Gujarati U+0AE6..U+0AEF, full-width U+FF10..U+FF19).
9. Mirror aggregates into `/app/out/aggregates.csv`, `/app/out/aggregates.tsv`, `/app/out/aggregates.xml`, `/app/out/aggregates.ini`, `/app/out/aggregates.env`, `/app/out/aggregates.md`, and `/app/out/aggregates.txt`, corpora in sorted name order; `.env` keys upper-cased.
10. Emit `/app/out/zone_totals.json` with the counted-row total per active zone across every corpus.
11. Emit `/app/out/corpus_index.json` with `count` and a `corpora` list carrying `name`, `format`, `op`, `lo`, `hi`, `eligible_rows`, and `value`.
12. Emit `/app/out/posture.json` with `aggregate_total`, `corpus_count`, `max_corpus`, `max_value` (ties broken by the earlier name), and `nonzero_corpora`.
13. Emit `/app/out/rejected_ops.json` with `rejected` (the ascending `seq` list of every invalid journal operation) and `count`.
14. Emit `/app/out/validation_report.json` with `ok` and `checks` covering `all_artifacts_present`, `config_matches_policy`, `config_scalar_flat`, `command_failures`, `rejected_ops`, per-zone `profiles` (`scalar_flat`, `trailer`), `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`.
15. Emit `/app/out/summary.json` with `tool`, `profile_tag`, `trailer`, `profiles`, `artifacts`, `artifact_count`, `inputs` (sorted names of every file under `/app/data`), `input_count`, `corpus_count`, and `aggregate_total`.
16. Emit `/app/out/report.json` through the repaired tool's `export-report` subcommand with `ok`, `tool`, `config_path`, `config_sha256` (sha256 hex of `/app/out/config.json` bytes), `trailer`, and `commands` (one object per CLI call, each with `argv`, `returncode`, `stdout`). No timestamps or run-dependent fields.
17. Rebuild the repaired tool deterministically as `/app/out/tool.zip` (ZIP_STORED, fixed epoch, fixed external_attr, sorted member order) so its sha256 is reproducible across runs.
18. Emit `/app/out/manifest.sha256`: one `<sha256>  <name>` line per delivered artifact except `tool.zip`, `report.json`, and `manifest.sha256` itself, names in sorted order, two spaces between. The seven non-JSON aggregates views (`.csv`, `.tsv`, `.xml`, `.ini`, `.env`, `.md`, `.txt`) are included.
19. Every JSON artifact is written with these exact parameters: UTF-8, `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, indent=2, separators=(",", ": "), ensure_ascii=False)`, plus a single trailing `\n`. Default `json.dumps(obj)` breaks the manifest.
20. The configuration must stay flat scalars only; no nested dicts or lists in `/app/out/config.json` or in any profile.
21. Keep the workflow deterministic and offline: no network, no wall-clock timestamps, no random seeds, no reliance on dict insertion order. Running the pipeline twice must produce byte-identical artifacts.

instruction:
A water and power retailer has dumped one fiscal year of its metering book into
`/app/data` and then lost the program that read it. What survives is the written
contract at `/app/data/schema.md`, the four event files, the reference tables,
and the policy file the desk settled against. Your job is to rebuild the
pipeline.

The contract is the authority on every rule: how an event reaches its region,
its currency, its rate and its billing period, which events are malformed, how
the per account deposit ladder decides whether an event is accepted at all, and
the exact shape of every figure you must emit. Read it together with the bytes.
Deciding which file feeds which figure is part of the work, so treat the
directory as something to explore rather than a list handed to you.

Deliver a reusable transform program at `/app/out/transform.py`. It takes an
input directory and an output directory and writes every artifact under the
output directory, so the same code settles a directory it has never seen:

```bash
python3 /app/out/transform.py <DATA_DIR> <OUT_DIR>
```

Use only the Python standard library; anything you pip install now will be
absent later. The program must not open network connections or start other
processes. Money is integer USD cents throughout, and every JSON artifact is
written with sorted keys.

Write the normalized event stream to `/app/out/normalized.jsonl`, the book wide
roll-up to `/app/out/summary.json`, the data health report to
`/app/out/data_quality.json`, and the per tariff roll-up to
`/app/out/product_summary.json`. Write one file per top level region at
`/app/out/region_central.json`, `/app/out/region_east.json`,
`/app/out/region_north.json`, `/app/out/region_south.json` and
`/app/out/region_west.json`, and one file per segment at
`/app/out/segment_consumer.json`, `/app/out/segment_corporate.json`,
`/app/out/segment_enterprise.json` and `/app/out/segment_smb.json`. The keys
inside each file are fixed by the contract. Every region file and every segment
file is written on every run, including a bucket that drew nothing.

Two warnings worth taking seriously. An artifact counts only when every single
value in it is exact, so one cent or one unit out of place costs the whole file.
And the figures interlock: an account's running deposit balance decides which of
its later events are accepted, so an event you settle wrongly moves the balance,
changes which neighbours survive, and shifts every roll-up that touches them.

Finish by posting a closing message that reports what you built, where each
artifact was written, and the thirteen closing report figures the contract
defines. Those thirteen appear in no artifact, so they have to come out of your
own run.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online
solutions or hints specific to this task.

Such malformed strings can therefore continue through processing as identifiers.

instruction:
Aurelis Labs is closing release R7 of its post-training preference corpus, the human preference data that trains the preference model and drives the alignment run for `aurelis-r7-chat`. Four annotation vendors ran for one quarter and their exports disagree. Everything you need is under `/app/data`. Start with `/app/data/corpus_policy.md`, which publishes the release parameters and the release rules in the order they apply, and `/app/data/source_conventions.md`, which says how each source writes identifiers, numbers and instants. `/app/data/field_precedence.html` names the source that governs each field, and the errata register, the review board minutes, the metric definitions and the methodology appendix are part of the same contract. Sources conflict in places.

Deliver the builder at `/app/out/build.py`. It must run as a script:

```bash
python3 /app/out/build.py <DATA_DIR> <OUT_DIR>
```

Run it on `/app/data` writing to `/app/out`. The platform reruns this builder on every release and on corpora it has not seen, so it must be fast as well as exact: on a given corpus its median runtime must stay within twice the median time that a plain read-and-decode pass over the same exports takes with the standard decoders in the image.

## Deliverables

1. `/app/out/build.py` - the reusable builder.
2. `/app/out/annotator_standing.json` - per annotator gold calibration and standing.
3. `/app/out/verdict_admissibility.jsonl` - per verdict admissibility and reason.
4. `/app/out/comparison_resolution.jsonl` - per comparison resolved verdict, route and margin.
5. `/app/out/agreement.json` - agreement statistics overall, per vendor and per domain.
6. `/app/out/prompt_eligibility.jsonl` - per prompt eligibility and exclusion reason.
7. `/app/out/dedup_clusters.json` - near duplicate clusters and their canonical member.
8. `/app/out/preference_pairs.jsonl` - the released chosen and rejected pairs.
9. `/app/out/split_assignment.json` - family to split assignment and counts.
10. `/app/out/mixture_plan.json` - per source allocation after the epoch cap.
11. `/app/out/packing_plan.json` - sequence packing totals.
12. `/app/out/training_schedule.json` - steps, warmup, shards and accumulation.
13. `/app/out/slice_coverage.json` - per slice pair and token counts.
14. `/app/out/source_audit.json` - per export record counts.
15. `/app/out/control_reconciliation.json` - corpus totals.
16. `/app/out/release_gates.json` - the release gate decisions.

## Contract

17. Every ratio is a JSON number quantised to six decimal places, half to even, at the reporting step and at no earlier step.
18. Counts are JSON integers, never strings and never floats.
19. Booleans are JSON booleans.
20. A value that does not exist, including a ratio whose denominator is zero, is JSON null, never zero and never an empty string.
21. Identifiers are written in their registered form, as `source_conventions.md` lists it.
22. `annotator_standing.json` is an object keyed by annotator id, each value carrying `vendor`, `gold_items`, `gold_hits`, `gold_agreement`, `balanced_verdicts`, `a_side_bias`, `biased` and `standing`. `standing` is the string `admitted` or `gated`.
23. `verdict_admissibility.jsonl` carries one object per registered verdict with `verdict_id`, `comparison`, `annotator`, `admissible` and `reason`. `reason` is null when the verdict is admissible, otherwise the first applicable code in this order: `annotator_gated`, `outside_window`, `freeze_window`, `stale_amendment`, `unbalanced_biased`, `voided`.
24. `comparison_resolution.jsonl` carries one object per registered comparison with `comparison_id`, `resolved`, `route`, `votes` and `margin`. `route` is `adjudicated`, `majority` or `insufficient`. `resolved` is `left`, `right`, `tie` or `both_bad`, and is null, like `margin`, when the comparison does not resolve.
25. `agreement.json` carries `overall`, `by_vendor` and `by_domain`, each value giving `observed_agreement`, `kappa`, `rated_units` and `rater_pairs`. `by_vendor` is keyed by vendor name and `by_domain` by domain name.
26. `prompt_eligibility.jsonl` carries one object per registered prompt with `prompt_id`, `eligible`, `reason`, `cluster`, `family` and `source`. `reason` is null when the prompt is eligible, otherwise the first applicable code in this order: `retired`, `opted_out`, `contaminated`, `duplicate`, `over_length`, `no_resolved_pair`. `cluster` is null for a prompt in no cluster.
27. `dedup_clusters.json` is keyed by cluster id, each value giving `canonical`, `members`, `dropped` and `canonical_effective_at`. `members` and `dropped` are sorted ascending, and `canonical_effective_at` is an ISO 8601 UTC instant such as `2025-07-04T16:22:03Z`.
28. `preference_pairs.jsonl` carries one object per released pair with `pair_id`, `comparison`, `prompt`, `family`, `source`, `chosen`, `rejected`, `margin`, `route` and `tokens`. `pair_id` is `PP-` followed by the digits of the comparison id, so `CMR-001234` yields `PP-001234`.
29. `split_assignment.json` carries `families` (family id to `train` or `validation`), `family_counts`, `pair_counts` and `validation_share`; both count objects are keyed by `train` and `validation`.
30. `mixture_plan.json` is keyed by source name with `available_pairs`, `target_weight`, `allocated_pairs`, `effective_weight`, `epochs` and `capped`, plus a `_total` entry carrying `budget_pairs` and `allocated_pairs`.
31. `packing_plan.json` carries `sequence_length`, `packed_pairs`, `dropped_pairs`, `sequences`, `token_capacity`, `tokens_used`, `padding_tokens` and `packing_efficiency`.
32. `training_schedule.json` carries `sequences`, `global_batch`, `micro_batch`, `gradient_accumulation`, `optimizer_steps`, `warmup_steps`, `shards`, `shard_sequences` and `dropped_tail_sequences`.
33. `slice_coverage.json` is keyed by slice with `pairs`, `train`, `validation` and `tokens`. Slice keys are written as `slice_definitions.yaml` writes them, `<dimension>-<value>` over the dimensions `domain`, `difficulty`, `risk`, `locale` and `source`, for example `domain-finance` and `locale-de_DE`; only slices holding at least one pair appear.
34. `source_audit.json` is keyed by file name, naming every file in the data directory exactly once, documents included, with `rows`: the number of records the file carries in the record layout `source_conventions.md` describes (columns `rid`, `par`, `val`, `at`, `fa`, `fb` or their renamed forms), header lines excluded. A file with no records has 0.
35. `control_reconciliation.json` carries `prompts`, `completions`, `comparisons`, `verdicts`, `admissible`, `resolved`, `eligible` and `pairs`, where `resolved` counts comparisons whose `resolved` is not null.
36. `release_gates.json` carries `gates`, `undersized_slices`, `train_contamination_rate` and `total_pairs`. `gates` holds the booleans `min_slice_pairs_met`, `no_family_straddles_split`, `train_contamination_within_limit`, `kappa_above_floor`, `packing_efficiency_reported` and `release_approved`, and `undersized_slices` is sorted ascending.
37. Every JSONL artifact is sorted ascending by its own identifier field, holds no duplicate identifier, and ends with a newline.
38. Every JSON artifact is written with sorted keys and ends with a newline.
39. All artifacts are UTF-8 with LF line endings.
40. The `prompts`, `completions`, `comparisons` and `verdicts` totals in `control_reconciliation.json` must agree with the figures published in `/app/data/control_totals.html`.
41. The pair count in `release_gates.json` must equal the number of rows in `preference_pairs.jsonl`.
42. Every family named in `split_assignment.json` must appear in exactly one split.

## Rules of engagement

43. Use only the Python standard library and the packages already installed in the image.
44. This machine has no internet access; do not attempt to reach it.
45. Read only `<DATA_DIR>`, and never modify anything inside it.
46. Write only inside `<OUT_DIR>`; create nothing anywhere else, temporary files included.
47. The builder must be deterministic: two runs on identical input produce byte identical artifacts.
48. The builder must take its input and output locations from its arguments, and must not depend on the name of the directory it is given.
49. Values are compared exactly, at the documented precision, keys, types and ordering.

instruction:
The daybreak household assistant closed routing cycle HB-2034-231 and the published plan was withdrawn. The plan is plausible everywhere, yet three symptoms show at once: a device overruns its energy ceiling inside a window, a one-shot override the cycle should have spent is still on the books, and an action that should have stood aside for its fallback still holds the slot. What survives is the working papers under `/app/data`: the programme contract, one specification per stage, the policy papers, the closed vocabularies, the registers with their revision histories, the prior state, and this cycle's directive, workbook and memo. Every identifier, revision and threshold was minted for this cycle alone, so no source outside `/app/data` settles any of it. Leave those papers as you find them.

Start at `/app/data/00_start_here.txt`, then `/app/data/assistant_program_contract.md`, which names the fourteen stages and their papers. `/app/data/data_lineage.md` states the ten recording rules and maps each paper to its stage. `/app/data/readings_not_in_force.md` and `/app/data/known_traps_and_footguns.md` are reading aids that govern nothing; where they and a stage specification seem to part, the specification rules, and neither is a list of what the package gets wrong. File names describe a role, not contents.

Three papers are not plain text and carry values found nowhere else. Read all three. `/app/data/capacity_and_intensity_workbook.xlsx` holds the per window per device energy ceilings on several grids of the same shape, only one of them live, plus the class surcharges and scales. `/app/data/household_operations_memo.pdf` holds the scalar controls and the per routine occurrence caps. `/app/data/precedence_directive.docx` holds the seven policy layers with their ranks, the settlement key order, the mandatory reserve and the number of reconciliation rounds, and it settles each of those figures wherever another source disagrees.

`/app/data/project.zip` holds the `daybreak` package as the household runs it. Extract it, work out where it departs from the papers, and repair it there. Its own suite passes exactly as it shipped, which tells you where the faults are absent rather than where they are.

Deliver the repaired package as `/app/out/package.zip`, laid out with `pyproject.toml` at the archive root, a `src/daybreak` source tree, and the shipped `tests` directory carried through unchanged, module for module and byte for byte. Keep every module and every stage function the package expectations name, with the arguments and record shapes they shipped with, and use the Python standard library on the 3.12 series alone. It has to run as `python3 -m daybreak --data <papers> --out <destination>` with the two options in either order, create the destination when it is absent, write the twenty-eight derived documents there and nothing else, and leave the paper directory byte for byte as it found it. Hold nothing about this cycle inside it: every identifier, count, control value and threshold has to be read from the directory it is pointed at. Two runs over one directory have to produce identical bytes, and the same cycle under another directory name has to produce them again.

Publish every whole quantity as a whole number in the base unit its stage names, and every ratio at twelve decimal places, in exact rational arithmetic, rounding where the stage specification places it and nowhere else. Keep binary floating point out of the derivation and publish no negative zero. Carry the prior state, the resolved policy, the settled graph and the pools from one stage into the next. Settle every dependency cycle. Reconcile the capacity binding after the fallbacks are proposed, not before.

Write the intake record: `/app/out/unit_normalization.json`, `/app/out/alias_resolution.jsonl`, `/app/out/expansion_ledger.csv`, `/app/out/config_resolution.json`, `/app/out/parameter_audit.csv` and `/app/out/trigger_eligibility_index.json`. Write the graph record: `/app/out/dependency_graph.json`, `/app/out/cycle_break_ledger.json` and `/app/out/canonical_action_order.json`. Write the binding record: `/app/out/resource_demand.csv`, `/app/out/window_capacity_report.csv`, `/app/out/initial_allocation.json` and `/app/out/displaced_action_queue.json`. Write the reconciliation record: `/app/out/fallback_expansion.json`, `/app/out/precedence_reconciliation.json` and `/app/out/final_action_order.json`. Write the state record: `/app/out/cooldown_state.csv`, `/app/out/derived_state.json`, `/app/out/suppression_ledger.csv` and `/app/out/next_state_snapshot.json`. Write the publication record: `/app/out/per_context_manifest.json`, `/app/out/per_device_manifest.csv`, `/app/out/daily_automation_manifest.json`, `/app/out/resource_utilization_report.csv`, `/app/out/terminal_action_report.md` and `/app/out/audit_ledger.jsonl`. Write `/app/out/run_manifest.txt` carrying the core digest and the publication digest, and `/app/out/summary.json` carrying the control totals. Write the repair record: `/app/out/build_report.json`, `/app/out/selftest.json`, `/app/out/defect_register.md` and `/app/out/verification_notes.md`. The register is a markdown table with one row per departure, not one per function: a function that departs from two rules takes two rows, and a fix that touches two functions takes a row for each. Every row names the function the departure sat in and one stage, the stage whose paper states the rule it breaks. Where that function is a helper several stages call, name the earliest stage in chain order whose result the departure changes; where it is a reader every paper passes through, name the first stage, by the paper to stage map in the lineage, that reads a paper carrying the trap it mishandles. The stage column is scored strictly against that rule, and the register is checked against the departures the shipped source really carries, so a row for code that was never wrong counts against it as surely as a missing row. The notes state the figures the output schema asks for, and each one is checked against the value this cycle actually yields.

Match every document to `/app/data/output_schema_reference.md` exactly, header line, column order, row order, key names and value types, and follow `/app/data/serialisation_and_digest_contract.md` for encoding, line endings, key ordering, indentation, empty file shape and the trailing newline. Take the two digests last, over bytes already written.

This cycle is one acquisition profile and does not reach every documented branch, so implement each quiet branch from its specification rather than from what this cycle exercises. Use only the reason codes the glossary admits.

Report, in your final message, the live workbook grid with the key cell you matched it on, the start of the last window in milliseconds, the count of instances set aside under each reason as your last run's `suppression_ledger.csv` records it, and every defect you repaired beside the stage your defect register names for it.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task.
