instruction:
Our monorepo's dependency resolver was lost along with its source, and the release pipeline is blocked until it is back. Everything left of it is in `/app/data`. `conventions.md` holds the rules the team wrote down, `reports.md` gives the exact shape of the three output files, and `handover.md` holds notes an engineer wrote from memory. The team does not trust `handover.md`; where it disagrees with `conventions.md` or the worked examples, it is wrong. Read all three notes before you start writing code.

Two worked examples ship with their answers. Their input files carry the prefix `example_a_` or `example_b_`, and the files they should produce carry `example_a_out_` or `example_b_out_`. The five input files with no prefix (`index.jsonl`, `workspace.json`, `pins.csv`, `lock.prev.json`, `manifest.json`) are the live intake, and nobody has its answers.

`conventions.md` says that six rules of the old resolver were never written down. Working out those six rules from the worked examples is part of the task. They cover which copy of a republished package version is kept, when a release candidate may be picked, when a yank applies, when the previous lock is honoured, the order in which one requester's requirements join the queue, and which row wins when `pins.csv` names a package twice.

Both worked examples use mode word zero. The live intake's `manifest.json` carries mode word 254, and the other intakes the program will later meet carry other mode words. `conventions.md` says which seven bit values are in use and that what each bit does was never written down; working out what each bit does is part of the task as well. The live intake has no answers, but its manifest carries a SHA-256 for each report and for each member's share of the lock.

Write the resolver as one Python program at `/app/out/lockres.py`, run as `python3 /app/out/lockres.py IN_DIR OUT_DIR`. It reads the five input files with no prefix from `IN_DIR`, takes the mode word from that folder's `manifest.json`, and writes `lock.json`, `issues.jsonl` and `summary.json` into `OUT_DIR`, byte for byte in the form `reports.md` gives and replacing any copies already there. It exits with status 0 when it has written them. `issues.jsonl` must exist even when it is empty, and the `lock_digest` in `summary.json` must agree with the `lock.json` written in the same run. A run over an intake of a thousand index lines should finish in well under a minute. Write it as named functions, and leave no bare `except` and no debug print in the file.

The same program will later be run on other folders with this layout, with different packages, versions, members and damaged lines, so nothing about the shipped folder may be written into the program, including content hashes or the lock digest in code or comments. The program must use only the Python 3.12 standard library, must work with no network access, must leave `IN_DIR` unchanged, and must produce identical output when run twice on the same input. Leave everything under `/app/data` as it is.

Run your finished program over `/app/data` into an output directory of your own outside `/app/data`, and then end with a closing report that gives, for the live intake: `picked`, `sticky`, `conflicts`, `unresolved`, `yanks_applied`, `yanks_ignored`, `republished`, `malformed`, `retransmitted`, `pins` and the full `lock_digest`, each as your program wrote it. For each of the six unwritten rules, state the reading you chose and name the worked example file and package that settled it, or say plainly that the examples did not settle it and you made a choice. For each of the seven mode bits, state what your program does when it is set, or say that the bit stays open. Also say whether your program reproduced both worked examples byte for byte, and whether its live reports and member shares agree with every digest in the live `manifest.json`.

A partial resolver that is written down and reported on is worth more than a perfect one that never gets finished. Put the program in place and give the closing report within your first hour, and stop any search over rules or bits well before the time limit; a session that is cut off by the limit leaves no answer at all.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

instruction:
A mixture of experts training job regressed after its expert layers were placed under a compiled backend. Device utilisation collapsed, the compilation log kept emitting recompilation lines long past the warmup window, graph capture began reporting that the operation is not permitted while a stream is capturing, and the host resident set climbed until the job was killed. The orchestrator that produced the run is `/app/data/deployed_trainer.py` and the figures it published are `/app/data/deployed_run_summary.json`. Everything you need to replay that run correctly, to say where its arithmetic departs from the written contracts, and to settle the configuration it should have used lives in `/app/data`. Nothing there tells you which of its decisions is wrong and no list of faults is provided. Start from `/app/data/glossary.md`.

Write your planner to `/app/out/moeplan.py`. It answers five verbs. `build DATA_DIR OUT_DIR` reads a corpus directory and writes every record named below into an output directory. `trace CONFIG_DOCUMENT`, `replay RUN_DOCUMENT`, `settle CANDIDATE_DOCUMENT` and `resolve SEALED_DOCUMENT` each read one self contained JSON document that carries its own configuration and its own copy of every table, print one JSON object on standard output, and consult no fixed location on disk. The shape of those documents and the keys each verb prints are set out in `/app/data/output_schema.md`. The same program is run against other corpora built to the same contract with different expert counts, mesh sizes, schedules, thresholds and gate values, so derive every number rather than writing it down. Every error the planner raises must name the input value or the input file it rejected.

The records are `/app/out/route_plan.json`, `/app/out/capacity_plan.json`, `/app/out/mesh_plan.json`, `/app/out/dispatch_ledger.json`, `/app/out/drop_ledger.json`, `/app/out/alltoall_ledger.json`, `/app/out/guard_key_index.json`, `/app/out/recompile_report.json`, `/app/out/graph_break_ledger.json`, `/app/out/cudagraph_report.json`, `/app/out/host_memory_report.json`, `/app/out/steptime_report.json`, `/app/out/warmup_profile.json`, `/app/out/sealed_policy_resolution.json`, `/app/out/aux_loss_trace.json`, `/app/out/loss_curve.json`, `/app/out/gradient_ledger.json`, `/app/out/optimizer_trace.json`, `/app/out/convergence_report.json`, `/app/out/baseline_parity.json`, `/app/out/settlement_report.json`, `/app/out/rejection_ledger.json`, `/app/out/sensitivity.json`, `/app/out/audit_statistics.json`, `/app/out/deployed_diagnosis.json`, `/app/out/validation_report.json`, `/app/out/stage_manifest.json`, `/app/out/replay_manifest.json` and `/app/out/final_state.json`. Each record carries exactly the top level keys named for it in the shipped schema, no more and no fewer.

The settled configuration must come out of the documented candidate sweep rather than out of judgement, and abandoning compilation is not a settlement. The diagnosis must name the settings under which the deployed run departs from the contracts the register puts in force, and it must show where the published figures disagree with a correct replay of that same configuration. Two decisions this pipeline makes are absent from the prose and are pinned down instead by sealed evidence shipped with the corpus; recovering them by enumeration is part of the work, and a pipeline that is wrong upstream will find that nothing matches. Before you rely on the planner, show by executing it rather than by description that `trace` and `replay` over a document assembled from `/app/data/sample_run_config.json` reproduce what `/app/data/worked_step.md` states for that configuration, and that `trace` over a document assembled from `/app/data/deployed_config.json` records recompilation events after the warmup bound.

Canonical byte shape, JSON value types, rounding cadence, storage width and accumulator width are fixed by the numeric contract and the shipped schema in the corpus, and an integer, a float and a boolean are never interchangeable. Follow them at every point they name.

Use the Python standard library only. Import no third party package, install nothing at run time, and shell out to nothing. Two runs over the same corpus must produce byte identical records. Behaviour must not depend on the name of any directory or file it is given. Leave `/app/data` byte for byte unchanged. Read no location other than the corpus directory handed to `build` or the single document handed to any other verb.

Close by stating in plain sentences what you found and what you settled on, with the step at which the deployed run first exceeds its recompilation budget, the count of recompilation events recorded after the warmup bound, the settings the settlement changed and the value it settled each one to, the measured throughput ratio and the host memory gate verdict of the settled configuration, the closing loss, the convergence verdict, and the count of admissible candidates that survived the sweep together with the count removed before any rejection cause was weighed. Those numbers must agree with the records you wrote.

Everything required is in the provided files. You have 28800 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
The release train planner that built release candidate `R-NEXT` has been retired
because the package it produced disagreed with itself, and the release has to be
planned again. Everything you need is in `/app/data`.

`/app/data/release_engineering_handbook.md` is the authority for this build. The
two addenda it names, `/app/data/rounding_precedence_addendum.pdf` and
`/app/data/compatibility_window_notes.docx`, are the authority for what they
cover, and `/app/data/artifact_register.md` fixes the records, keys, order and
serialization of every output. Where any other file in that directory disagrees
with those four, those four win. The retired planner, its helpers, its notes and
its last report are in the directory for comparison only, and none of their
figures can be trusted.

Write a corrected planner at `/app/out/relplan.py`. It runs as

```bash
python3 /app/out/relplan.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR
```

and rebuilds the whole package into `OUT_DIR` from whatever corpus `DATA_DIR`
holds, exiting with status 0. The requirements are these.

1. Do not tie the planner to `/app/data` or to this corpus's particular values.
   The same planner will be run, as an unprivileged user with no access to
   `/app`, against other corpora of the same shape: one carrying this exact
   release state with its rows delivered in a different order, and one carrying
   revised revisions, workbook figures, policy rows and compatibility records.
2. Derive every number from the corpus. No released figure may be fixed in the
   source.
3. Use integer arithmetic throughout. No output field carries a float.
4. Use only the Python standard library, and reach no network service.
5. Treat everything under `/app/data` as read only.
6. Give every release unit the canonical identity the handbook defines and use
   it in every output.
7. Resolve each unit's toolchain revision and contract revision against the
   previous release, and report both sides of each delta.
8. Record every distinct invalidation cause a unit has, deduplicated and sorted,
   and keep direct causes distinguishable from propagated ones.
9. Rebuild exactly what the handbook invalidates and reuse the rest, with the
   artifact digest that justifies each reuse.
10. Price every build unit in whole ticks under the scaling order and rounding
    the addendum sets out, and show each intermediate value.
11. Keep every pool inside its budget, with the budget, the reservation and the
    net figure reported per pool.
12. Admit prerequisite closures rather than units in isolation, and give every
    unit that is not built a traceable reason code.
13. Order the schedule so that every prerequisite, every migration constraint
    and every surviving ordering rule is satisfied, with one sequence number per
    scheduled unit.
14. Resolve dependency cycles under the declared policy, record what was removed
    and at what cost, and block what the policy blocks.
15. Select release consistent component versions and report every locally
    cheaper combination that compatibility rejects.
16. Keep deferred, blocked and excluded units out of the deployment manifest.
17. Make the generated client manifest agree with the contract revisions and the
    selected versions of the units that produce them.
18. Reconcile this release against the previous one and against the published
    artifact index.
19. Record every exception with the code the audit registry defines.
20. Emit the final release decision derived from the same state as every other
    output.
21. Make two runs over one corpus agree byte for byte.

When you are done, the package files in `/app/out` must be exactly what
`python3 /app/out/relplan.py /app/data /app/out` writes, byte for byte, with no
hand editing afterwards. The planner and the diagnosis note named below sit
beside them. The package is these files:

```
/app/out/normalized_inventory.jsonl
/app/out/revision_delta.jsonl
/app/out/toolchain_resolution.jsonl
/app/out/contract_delta.jsonl
/app/out/invalidation_reasons.jsonl
/app/out/invalidation_closure.jsonl
/app/out/generated_output_plan.jsonl
/app/out/build_unit_ledger.jsonl
/app/out/build_cost_breakdown.jsonl
/app/out/capacity_allocation.jsonl
/app/out/deferred_units.jsonl
/app/out/dependency_schedule.jsonl
/app/out/cycle_resolution.jsonl
/app/out/worker_pool_summary.json
/app/out/compatibility_matrix.jsonl
/app/out/rejected_combinations.jsonl
/app/out/version_selection.jsonl
/app/out/release_membership.jsonl
/app/out/deployment_manifest.json
/app/out/generated_sdk_manifest.jsonl
/app/out/migration_order.jsonl
/app/out/artifact_provenance.jsonl
/app/out/cache_reuse_manifest.jsonl
/app/out/release_delta.json
/app/out/audit_exceptions.jsonl
/app/out/release_decision.json
/app/out/conformance_summary.csv
/app/out/cost_amortization.jsonl
```

22. Share each generating unit's build cost across the components that
    require its interface, in whole ticks, so the shares add back to the
    cost they came from.
23. Leave the planner itself at `/app/out/relplan.py`.
24. Write `/app/out/diagnosis.md` with one numbered entry for each defect of the
    retired planner that your build corrects, naming the handbook or addendum
    rule each one broke.

instruction:
The extract mounted at `/app/data` is one settlement period of a model-serving platform: request logs of its traffic classes, the tenant register, correction layers, the rate card and the other material the settlement of reserved throughput needs. The documents shipped with the data govern this work.

Write a program at `/app/out/optimize.py` with three entry points. `python3 /app/out/optimize.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`, where DATA_DIR is an extract folder, settles the whole period and writes every report the documents define into OUT_DIR, creating OUT_DIR when it is absent, including the frozen reports `/app/out/scenario_visible.json`, `/app/out/scenario_peak.json`, `/app/out/scenario_steady.json`, `/app/out/scenario_burst.json`, `/app/out/scenario_latency.json`, `/app/out/perf_report.json`, `/app/out/bottleneck_analysis.json`, `/app/out/recommendations.json` and `/app/out/data_quality.json` when OUT_DIR is `/app/out`. `python3 /app/out/optimize.py EVENTS_LOG RULES_JSON`, where EVENTS_LOG is one request log and RULES_JSON is the control file of its extract, prints the result object of that class. The module function `aggregate(events_path, rules_path)` returns that same object. Run the directory form once on `/app/data` with `/app/out` as OUT_DIR, so the reports of the shipped extract sit in `/app/out` when you finish.

It will also be run on other extracts in the same layout, so nothing in it may depend on this particular period. Each changed extract is an extract in this layout in its own right. Each call finishes within 60 seconds. On a large workload, the `aggregate` call must also use at most 70 percent of the CPU time of a straightforward implementation that parses the whole request log again for every member of a pool in every settlement round.

Every report follows the layout and form the documents give, exactly: text reports byte for byte, database and workbook reports value for value. The text reports must be byte-identical, and the database and workbook reports value-identical, across runs, working directories, extract locations and output directories.

When an extract breaks one of the invariants that ct_svc.md lists, the program stops with an error and writes no report.

The program must leave DATA_DIR untouched, read nothing outside DATA_DIR, OUT_DIR and its own directory, and write nothing outside OUT_DIR. Use only the Python standard library, and open no network connection. The program runs as a single process and starts no other process. It reads no clock and uses no `random`, `uuid` or `secrets` module. Every except clause in the program names an exception class and never discards the error. Every function in the program is at most 50 lines long. The program is self-contained: it imports nothing from its own folder. Only `/app/out/optimize.py` and the nine frozen reports are collected from `/app/out`.

Compare the settled reservation of every tenant with the prior output of the extract and state the largest difference.

Each what-if is worked out by rerunning the whole settlement with exactly the change named, on a copy of the extract, with everything else as shipped; a what-if over a range of values reruns one copy per value. Work out each what-if answer with a run of your program on its edited copy.

1. For each starting step from 1 to 20 quarters given to pool pl-pe1, each on its own copy, which starting step gives the largest grand bill total of the period, and what is that total?
2. On copies of the extract whose meter sheet keeps only readings M11 to M25, for each whole number from 40 to 100 written as the RU of reading M25, each on its own copy, at how many of these values does the period settle, and which value gives the largest grand bill total among them, with that total?
3. For each cutoff_seq from 100 to 230 written in the control file, each on its own copy, which cutoff_seq values give the smallest grand bill total of the period, and what is that total?
4. If the meter sheet kept only readings M11 to M25, with reading M25 reading 70 RU instead of 69, what would the total overage units over all classes be?
5. If an amendment with seq 243 set the contracted_ru of tenant tn-7de in class steady to 31, what would the total settled reservation moved be?
6. If pool pl-bu1 started with a step of 14 quarters, what would the total settled reservation moved be?
7. If the amendment of what-if 5 were in place and pool pl-st1 also started with a step of 12 quarters, what would the grand bill total of the period be?
8. If the steady rate row effective from 2026-03-04 had an ru_rate_micro of 2300, what would the grand bill total of the period be?
9. If the burst rate row effective from 2026-03-13 had a round_fee_micro of 1170, what would the grand bill total of the period be?

In your final message, after the what-if answers, state four headline figures of the shipped extract: the total settled reservation moved (the sum over all members of the absolute difference between settled and contracted reservation), the total charged settlement rounds (the sum over all pools of the rounds the orchestration charge counts), the total demand in RU over all classes, and the total overage units over all classes. Also state the grand bill total of the period with its three parts (reservation, overage and orchestration charges), and the number of reports the directory form wrote. Report only figures your own runs printed. State the number of reports the directory form wrote as a listing of OUT_DIR printed it. Claim only runs and checks that your own commands performed. Report a check as passing only when its last run passed.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task. Do not use online solutions or hints specific to this task.

instruction:
A control plane operates an HTTP/3 reverse-proxy fleet that carries long-lived tenant streams across a sequence of scheduling epochs. Every epoch, every active stream must be assigned to exactly one node subject to node capacity, per-tenant fair-share, per-node token buckets, class-based preemption, migration penalties, and latency SLOs. Derive a discrete schedule that minimises the weighted sum of alpha times latency_cost, beta times migration_cost, and gamma times fairness_deviation under every hard constraint, then serialise a fixed set of report artifacts and chain them under an integrity manifest.

What you have. Under /app/data you will find the input corpus (fleet, streams, tenants, classes, latency, migration table, token buckets, epoch windows, constants, MTU matrix, rate profiles), a fully-traced 3-node 6-stream micro example in worked_micro_example.json, the complete written specification at /app/data/README-input-schema.md, and six sealed reference corpora (case-argosy.json through case-frigate.json) with companion seal files (seal-argosy.json through seal-frigate.json). Read the schema before writing any code.

Four rules that govern the algorithm's interior, one in the largest-remainder tie-break, one in the floor-versus-cap ordering, one in the SLO comparison, and one in the token-bucket refill rounding, were part of the original operational contract but their prose was lost from the shipped schema. Section 6 of /app/data/README-input-schema.md names the four missing rules and lists the candidate values for each. The sealed corpora were archived under the original settlements, so a scheduler that lands on the wrong reading for any of them will produce numbers that do not match at least one seal.

Your program will also be evaluated on freshly seeded corpora that are not in the archive. The settlements you land on must be the ones the archive was written under, not a combination that happens to fit only the six shipped seals.

What you must deliver. Produce exactly these eleven files in /app/out: /app/out/schedule_matrix.json, /app/out/fleet_utilization.json, /app/out/tenant_fairness_report.json, /app/out/migration_ledger.json, /app/out/preemption_events.json, /app/out/sla_violation_report.json (where total_breaches must be zero), /app/out/objective_breakdown.json, /app/out/fixed_point_trace.json, /app/out/integrity_manifest.json, /app/out/final_state.json, and /app/out/reusable_scheduler.py. Every JSON file must be canonically serialised as json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) followed by a single newline. integrity_manifest.json holds the SHA-256 of the on-disk canonical bytes of the eight preceding JSON artifacts; final_state.json folds those hashes into folded_digest_sha256. Exact shapes are documented in /app/data/README-input-schema.md section 4.

reusable_scheduler.py must accept a data directory and an output directory as two positional arguments and produce identical output when re-run against /app/data /app/out. Every scheduling input must come from its declared data directory; it may read its own program file solely to create the required reusable_scheduler.py copy, and it may use the Python standard library. It must read no environment variable for its scheduling inputs. Two consecutive runs of the same command on the same input must produce byte-identical output. The /app/out directory must contain exactly those eleven files when you finish, with no scratch files, no backups, no logs, and no intermediate artifacts.

What you must not do. Do not modify or delete anything under /app/data. Do not use environment variables to smuggle scheduling inputs into the scheduler. Do not search online for a ready-made implementation of this task. Do not report totals that disagree with the numbers inside your delivered artifacts.

Wrap-up message. When you finish, state the four integer totals your run produced: the number of streams considered, the number of migration events across all epochs, the number of SLA breaches, and the total_cost value. Each of the four numbers must agree with your delivered artifacts: the stream count and the total_cost in final_state.json, the migration event count in migration_ledger.json, and the SLA breach count in sla_violation_report.json.

You have 21600 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
The Halvard playout centre has to close five channel weeks of commercial airtime. The close extract is under `/app/data`. `/app/data/corpus_index.md` names every file and its layout and points at the rule and contract documents; those documents are the only authority for this close, and nothing in this prompt repeats or summarises a rule they carry. Read them and work out what this close requires from the data itself.

Write one program at `/app/out/optimize.py` that uses only the Python standard library, defines `reconcile(data_dir, workload)` and runs as

```
python3 /app/out/optimize.py DATA_DIR WORKLOAD
```

printing, as one JSON document on standard output and nothing else, the scenario object that `/app/data/output_contract.md` defines for that workload. Then use the program to write the five scenario artifacts `/app/out/scenario_visible.json`, `/app/out/scenario_peak.json`, `/app/out/scenario_steady.json`, `/app/out/scenario_burst.json` and `/app/out/scenario_latency.json`, and the four roll-ups `/app/out/perf_report.json`, `/app/out/bottleneck_analysis.json`, `/app/out/recommendations.json` and `/app/out/data_quality.json`, each holding exactly what the contract defines for `/app/data`.

The program will also be run on data directories you have not seen. They share this layout but may differ in workload names, channel, frame rate and timecode mode, zone and summer time change, broadcast day start, daypart set, sync tolerance, cutoff, number of broadcast days, prices and size, so every rule parameter must be read from the directory the program is given and none may be written into the source. One unseen workload has 28 broadcast days and about five times the spots of the largest workload here; on it `reconcile` must return within four times the time a straightforward single pass reference implementation takes on the same machine, plus two seconds. Two runs on the same input print byte identical output, the order of lines inside an input file never changes a result, the result never depends on where the directory sits, the program writes no file anywhere, and when an input file it needs is missing it exits with a non zero status and prints nothing.

Where a retired, historical or informal document in the extract disagrees with the current rule documents, the current rule documents govern. An artifact counts only when every entry and value in it is exact: a total that is right while a row behind it is wrong does not count, and neither does a correct object under another key, file name or path.

Leave every file under `/app/data` exactly as shipped. Do not install packages. Do not look up the solution or any part of the method online. You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.

Finish with a closing message that states the nine closing figures defined at the end of `/app/data/output_contract.md` for `/app/data`, each with its label and its three facts as exact whole numbers and a workload name, and says which run of which script produced them. None of these figures appears in any artifact.

instruction:
The flat files in `/app/data` are the October 2025 monthly retail
settlement extract of a mid-size electric utility operating across the
four regions of the Meridian Interstate Grid Compact (MIGC). The extract
ships alongside a written data contract at `/app/data/schema.md` that
defines every input file, every reference table, every rate class, every
time-of-use window, every rounding rule, every net-metering rule and every
output artifact shape. Read that contract in full and work out from it how
the customers, premises, tariff schedule, fuel adjustment index, holiday
and DST calendars, currency table, regulator orders, net-metering banks,
service tickets, meter reads and demand intervals fit together. Deciding
which inputs feed which figure is part of the task. Produce the exact
reconciled settlement report the contract describes, deriving every
figure from the data rather than handwriting sample answers.

Deliver a single reusable program at `/app/out/reconcile.py`. Its one-shot
mode is `python3 /app/out/reconcile.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`: it reads one
complete extract from `DATA_DIR` and writes the report set into `OUT_DIR`.
Run that mode on the shipped extract so that the whole-corpus
settlement report lands at `/app/out/summary.json`, the applied-rule
audit at `/app/out/policy_audit.json`, and the count and threshold checks
at `/app/out/data_quality.json`. Write the three rate-class rollups to
`/app/out/rate_class_residential.json`,
`/app/out/rate_class_commercial.json`, and
`/app/out/rate_class_industrial.json`. Write the three regional rollups
to `/app/out/region_meridian_north.json`,
`/app/out/region_meridian_south.json`, and
`/app/out/region_meridian_east.json`. Serialise every JSON deterministically
with sorted keys, two-space indentation and a trailing newline, and use
integer Meridian-credit-cents (mrcc) or integer Foreign-Trade-Unit-cents
(ftuc) throughout as the contract requires. No floating-point value
appears anywhere in the artifacts.

The same program must also support a long-lived mode invoked as
`python3 /app/out/reconcile.py --session OUT_DIR`. In this mode, read one
newline-delimited JSON command from standard input at a time. Every command
has exactly two string fields: `turn_id` and `data_dir`. The named directory
is a complete, independent twelve-file snapshot. Fully recompute and replace
all nine JSON reports in the shared `OUT_DIR`, then write exactly one JSON
acknowledgement line `{"status":"ok","turn_id":"<same turn_id>"}` to
standard output and flush it. Continue accepting commands until standard
input reaches EOF, then exit with status zero. Do not carry any derived value,
cache entry, open input, or prior report content from one turn into the next.
If the same snapshot returns later in a session, its artifacts must be
byte-identical to the earlier turn.

The reusable program is judged on multiple extracts you have not seen, both
as independent one-shot inputs and as consecutive turns of one session.
Every unseen snapshot follows the same schema, but any of the twelve data
files may differ: reference rows, effective windows, rates, signs, balances,
calendar treatments, currencies, regions, row order, and transaction rows
are all snapshot data rather than constants. File names, columns, JSON
shapes, allowed values, and the October 2025 period remain as specified by
the contract. Row order has no meaning unless the contract explicitly gives
an ordering rule. Each turn must acknowledge within five minutes. Only the
ten artifact paths named above are collected.

Your delivered script must use only the Python standard library and must
not initiate any network activity of its own. In one-shot mode it must not
read outside `DATA_DIR`; in session mode it may read only the `data_dir`
named by the current command. In both modes it must not write outside
`OUT_DIR`. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this
task.

You have 7200 seconds to complete this task.

instruction:
The files in `/app/data` are a revisioned spectrum-clearing extract. Read the complete contract in `/app/data/schema.md`. It defines the records, half-open time and frequency intervals, revision winners, quarantine rules, guard bands, geographic exclusions, primary activation preemption, exact revenue arithmetic, signed correction allocation, ordering, and every output schema.

Build a reusable Python standard-library program at `/app/out/clear_spectrum.py`, runnable as `python3 /app/out/clear_spectrum.py DATA_DIR OUT_DIR`. It must derive results from any extract following the contract, not from the shipped identifiers or answers. Run it on `/app/data` and write these deterministic reports: `/app/out/manifest.json`, `/app/out/data_quality.json`, `/app/out/grant_ledger.json`, `/app/out/spectrum_slice_ledger.json`, `/app/out/preemption_ledger.json`, `/app/out/party_settlements.json`, `/app/out/auction_adjustments.json`, `/app/out/exception_register.json`, and `/app/out/audit_trace.json`.

All JSON must use sorted keys, two-space indentation, and a trailing newline. Use integer seconds, integer kHz, integer cents, and `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP` exactly where the contract says. Input row order is irrelevant except where explicit stable keys break ties. Invalid rows are quarantined rather than silently repaired. The reusable program is also executed on fresh extracts that exercise documented interactions, so hardcoded visible answers will fail.

Only the ten declared artifact paths are collected. You have 7200 seconds. Do not use online lookup, network services, or non-standard packages.

instruction:
Hello, this is the archive desk at Konkan Coast Broadcast Archive. Our four tape vaults hold more copies of the digitised masters than the retention charter asks for, and the next tape order depends on a proper plan of which copies to keep and how the kept copies pack onto cartridges. We need that plan as a program the desk can run again every cycle, so please write the planner, run it once on this cycle's export and tell us what it found.

This cycle's estate export is in `/app/data`. Please start reading at `/app/data/archive_desk_brief.md`; it tells you which paper governs which question. The exact layout of every output file, with the status values and reason codes, is in `/app/data/plan_output_contract.md`.

Write the planner as `/app/out/optimize.py` in Python 3.12. The desk will call it like this:

```bash
python3 /app/out/optimize.py --data DATA_DIR --out OUT_DIR
python3 /app/out/optimize.py --data DATA_DIR --out OUT_DIR --prior EARLIER_OUT_DIR
```

What we need from the planner:

1. It works on any export laid out like this one. Later cycles come with other planning dates, other amendments, other cartridges and a different mix of objects, so nothing that belongs to this cycle can be fixed inside the program.
2. It reads only from the folder given with `--data` (and `--prior` when given) and writes only into the folder given with `--out`.
3. Given the same input it writes byte identical files every time, whatever the input folder is called and wherever it sits.
4. With `--prior` pointing at the output of an earlier run, each scenario carries forward the earlier tape volumes in the way the volume layout paper describes.
